We are seeking a motivated PhD student to use single-molecule techniques and computational tools to explore molecular interactions and apply them for therapeutic applications. 
 Job description 
We are looking for a PhD student passionate about understanding molecular mechanisms in biological systems. This position involves applying single-molecule techniques to study molecular interactions, including protein-ligand interactions and protein-peptide interactions. The candidate will work in an interdisciplinary environment, combining experimental approaches (single molecule fluorescence and biochemistry) with computational methods. The candidate will obtain single-molecule multiplexing data and validate machine learning predictions using the high-throughput data. The successful candidate will collaborate with international partners for therapeutic applications of this research. The project offers opportunities to make significant contributions to understanding molecular interactions and their implications for both fundamental and medical sciences.
 Job requirements 
 MSc degree (or nearing completion) in physics, biophysics, computational biology, or a related field.
 Strong programming skills (Python) and experience in data analysis and computational methods.
 Familiarity with molecular biology techniques.
 Excellent written and spoken English skills.
 Ability to work effectively in a collaborative, international, and interdisciplinary environment.
This position is part of a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network. Applicants must satisfy the MSCA mobility rule: at the time of recruitment, they must not have lived or carried out their main activity, such as work or study, in the Netherlands for more than 12 months during the previous 36 months. The rule applies regardless of nationality.
 TU Delft (Delft University of Technology) 
Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference.
For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow.
These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future.
At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional.
Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward.
 Faculty Applied Sciences 
With more than 1,100 employees, including 150 pioneering principal investigators, as well as a population of about 3,600 passionate students, the Faculty of Applied Sciences is an inspiring scientific ecosystem. Focusing on key enabling technologies, such as quantum- and nanotechnology, photonics, biotechnology, synthetic biology and materials for energy storage and conversion, our faculty aims to provide solutions to important problems of the 21st century. To that end, we educate innovative students in broad Bachelor's and specialist Master's programmes with a strong research component. Our scientists conduct ground-breaking fundamental and applied research in the fields of Life and Health Science & Technology, Nanoscience, Chemical Engineering, Radiation Science & Technology, and Engineering Physics. We are also training the next generation of high school teachers.
Click here to go to the website of the Faculty of Applied Sciences.
 Conditions of employment 
Doctoral candidates will be offered a 4-year period of employment in principle, but in the form of 2 employment contracts. An initial 1,5 year contract with an official go/no go progress assessment within 15 months. Followed by an additional contract for the remaining 2,5 years assuming everything goes well and performance requirements are met.
Salary and benefits are in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, increasing from €3059 - €3881 gross per month, from the first year to the fourth year based on a fulltime contract (38 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%.
As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills.
The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Fle

Join TU Delft to uncover the biology of cellular robustness in an industrial yeast process and translate your discoveries into innovative genome engineering strategies. 
 Job description 
You will join a vibrant and collaborative research environment within the Industrial Microbiology section of the Department of Biotechnology at TU Delft. The section brings together six principal investigators and a diverse international team of postdoctoral researchers, PhD candidates and technicians with complementary expertise in modelling, molecular biology, genomics, microbial physiology, synthetic biology and metabolic engineering. This multidisciplinary environment provides excellent opportunities for scientific exchange and collaboration.
This project, co-supervised by professors Jack Pronk and Jean-Marc Daran, is conducted in close collaboration with a leading biotechnology company. It focuses on understanding the molecular basis of a key robustness trait in a yeast-based production process that is already deployed at industrial scale. This unique setting offers an excellent opportunity to address fundamental questions in microbial physiology while working on a challenge of direct relevance to industrial biotechnology.
The successful candidate will investigate the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying robustness in industrial yeast strains and translate this knowledge into rational strategies for strain improvement. The project will combine cell biology, genome editing and quantitative physiological studies in laboratory bioreactors.
The position offers a unique opportunity to work at the interface of fundamental and applied research, to benefit from close interactions with experts across multiple disciplines, and to contribute to innovations that can have a tangible impact on sustainable biomanufacturing.

academictransfer:364014.description:
€3,204 - €4,051; Master's; 38 hours
About the position
 The Southern Ocean plays a disproportionately large role in the global ocean carbon cycle. Its carbon cycling is strongly influenced by zooplankton, especially Antarctic krill and salps, whose fecal pellets drive vertical carbon export. Krill depend closely on sea ice and under‑ice habitats, while salps thrive in warmer, often ice‑free waters. Warming and sea‑ice loss are already shifting their distributions and increasing spatial overlap, with implications for competition, food webs, and fisheries. Yet current ecosystem models represent these key grazers only crudely, leaving major uncertainties in future projections.
 This project asks how changing interactions between Antarctic krill and salps reshape Southern Ocean ecosystems and the global carbon cycle. It will explore how sea‑ice loss, warming, predation and fisheries affect krill and salp population dynamics, and how shifts in their relative dominance alter grazing, fecal pellet production and vertical carbon export. Ultimately, it aims to reduce uncertainty in projections of Southern Ocean functioning under future climate and fishing scenarios.
 What are you going to do?
 You will develop stage‑structured population models for both species, explicitly including life‑history processes, sea‑ice dependence, predation and fisheries. You will couple these models to an ocean-sea‑ice-biogeochemical framework for the Antarctic Peninsula to quantify impacts on vertical carbon export. Finally, you will explore future climate and fishing scenarios to assess how shifts in krill-salp dominance affect Southern Ocean functioning.
 Tasks and responsibilities: 
 Complete and defend a PhD thesis within the official appointment duration of four years
 Develop and analyze stage-structured population models for krill and salp
 Couple the stage-structured models to an ocean-sea ice-biogeochemical framework to quantify how zooplankton life-histories influences vertical carbon export and local carbon cycling
 Publish your results in international scientific journals
 Present your results at meetings and scientific conferences
 Discuss your work in our group meetings, incorporate feedback, and give input to others
 Assist in teaching activities and in supervising bachelor and master students
 Your profile
 Your experience and profile: 
 Completed, or soon-to-be completed MSc in the biological sciences or different fields in the natural sciences (e.g. computational, mathematical, earth or marine sciences) with a strong interest in ecology and modeling
 Demonstrated experience with mathematical modelling, and an ability to learn new concepts and (computational) methods as needed
 A demonstrated ability to work with programming languages such as R, Python, Matlab, or C++
 A keen interest in advancing our understanding of marine ecosystems, polar regions, and/or biogeochemistry
 Proficient communication skills in spoken and written English
 Experience in scientific writing, bifurcation analysis or numerical ocean modeling are considered a plus.
 Our offer
 A temporary contract for 38 hours per week for the duration of 4 years (the initial contract will be for a period of 18 months and after satisfactory evaluation it will be extended for a total duration of 4 years). This should lead to a dissertation (PhD thesis). We will draft an educational plan that includes attendance of courses and (international) meetings. We also expect you to assist in teaching undergraduates and master students. The preferred starting date is as soon as possible. For this position the University Job Classification profile “Promovendus” (PhD candidate) applies. Your salary will be € 3.204 gross per month in the first year and will increase to € 4.051 in the final year, based on full-time employment of 38 hours per week. In addition, you will receive a 8% holiday allowance and 8.3% year-end allowance.  
 A favourable tax agreement, the ‘30% ruling’, may apply to non-Dutch applicants.
 The  Collective Labour Agreement of Universities of the Netherlands  is applicable.
 Besides the salary and a vibrant and challenging environment at Science Park we offer you multiple fringe benefits:
 232 holiday hours per year (based on fulltime) and extra holidays between Christmas and 1 January;
 multiple courses to follow from our Teaching and Learning Centre;
 a complete educational program for PhD students;
 multiple courses on topics such as leadership for academic staff;
 multiple courses on topics such as time management, handling stress and an online learning platform with 100+ different courses;
 7 weeks birth leave (partner leave) with 100% salary;
 partly paid parental leave;
 the possibility to set up a workplace at home;
 a pension at ABP for which UvA pays two third part of the contribution;
 the possibility to follow courses to learn Dutch;
 help with registration at UvA- Housing for a studio or small apartment when you’re moving from abroad. 
 Are you curious to read more about our extensive package of secondary employment benefits, take a look  here .
 About us
 The  Institute for Biodiversity and Ecosystem Dynamics  (IBED) is one of eight research institutes of the  Faculty of Science  at the  University of Amsterdam . The research at IBED aims to unravel how ecosystems function in all their complexity, and how they change due to natural processes and human activities. At its core lies an integrated systems approach to study biodiversity, ecosystems and the environment. IBED adopts this systems approach to ecosystems, addressing abiotic (soil and water quality) and biotic factors (ecology and evolution of plants, animals, and microorganisms), and the interplay between those. The IBED vision includes research encompassing experimental and theoretical approaches at a wide variety of temporal and spatial scales, i.e. from molecules and microorganisms to patterns and processes occurring at the global scale. The University of Amsterdam has excellent  high performance computing  facilities. Furthermore, IBED has a dedicated  computational support team  with specialized knowledge of bioinformatics, (geo)database management and scientific programming. IBED also works with non-academic partners to deliver transdisciplinary science for society.
 The position will be based in the  Department of Freshwater and Marine Ecology . The department of Freshwater & Marine Ecology aims to increase our understanding of the biodiversity and dynamics of freshwater and marine ecosystems from the level of molecules and genes to entire ecosystems.
 Department of Theoretical and Computational Ecology . Research in the Department of Theoretical and Computational Ecology focuses on understanding the complexity of ecological systems by using theoretical and advanced computational approaches.
 Want to know more about our organisation? Read more about  working at the University of Amsterdam.
 Are you excited by ecosystem modeling, climate change and polar oceans? Do you enjoy quantitative work, coding, and turning ecology into equations? We are looking for a highly motivated PhD candidate who is eager to study Antarctic krill and salp population dynamics, and their impacts on Southern Ocean carbon export in a changing climate.
 About the position
 The Southern Ocean plays a disproportionately large role in the global ocean carbon cycle. Its carbon cycling is strongly influenced by zooplankton, especially Antarctic krill and salps, whose fecal pellets drive vertical carbon export. Welkom bij de Universiteit Maastricht! 
Universiteit Maastricht bouwt volop aan haar onderwijs en onderzoek in Parkstad. Juist daar liggen kansen om wetenschap en de samenleving nog sterker met elkaar te verbinden. Als kennismakelaar zorg jij ervoor dat vragen en behoeften uit de samenleving doorvertaald worden naar onderwijs en onderzoek binnen de Faculty of Science and Engineering (FSE).
 Kennismakelaar Faculty of Science of Engineering 
 Ons doel: vragen en behoeften uit de lokale samenleving in Heerlen doorvertalen naar passend onderwijs en onderzoek van FSE.
 Jouw collega’s : Docenten en onderzoekers van FSE en de wijkverbinder van Universiteit Maastricht in Heerlen.
Als kennismakelaar vorm je samen met de wijkverbinder de schakel tussen de regio en de Faculty of Science and Engineering. Samen zorgen jullie ervoor dat zowel de maatschappelijke als de academische kant van samenwerkingen goed op elkaar aansluiten en dat projecten inhoudelijk sterk en maatschappelijk relevant zijn.
De wijkverbinder haalt dagelijks vragen en behoeften op in de wijk in Heerlen en omgeving. Jij gebruikt jouw academische achtergrond om deze vervolgens door te vertalen naar onderzoek en onderwijs bij FSE. Denk aan studentenprojecten, tentamenvragen, of onderzoeksvoorstellen voor wetenschapsfinancierders. Daarvoor weet jij precies welke kennis, expertise en kansen in de faculteit aanwezig zijn. Andersom kunnen docenten en onderzoekers bij jou terecht met samenwerkingsbehoeften.
Bij al je werkzaamheden zoek je steeds naar de juiste balans tussen maatschappelijke relevantie en academische kwaliteit. Je begrijpt de maatstaven waaraan academisch onderzoek en onderwijs moet voldoen. We are seeking an enthusiastic and ambitious postdoctoral researcher to join the Kool group at the Princess Máxima Center for Pediatric Oncology. You will lead the molecular characterization of astroblastoma, a newly recognized pediatric brain tumor type, using state-of-the-art multi-omics and integrative bioinformatic approaches. Working in a highly collaborative environment together with the Artegiani-Hendriks group in the Máxima, you will uncover the developmental origins, molecular mechanisms and sex-specific biology of astroblastoma, providing a roadmap also for future therapeutic strategies.

Astroblastoma is a rare pediatric brain tumor for which no standard treatment currently exists. However, the mechanisms underlying tumor initiation, cellular origin and sex bias remain unknown.
As a postdoctoral researcher working on this collaborative project, you will perform comprehensive molecular characterization of astroblastoma tumors and developing human brain tissues. You will integrate bulk and single-cell -omics data to identify the molecular consequences of oncogenic fusion genes, define their developmental cell(s)-of-origin and uncover mechanisms underlying the striking sex differences observed in these tumors.
Your work will combine various -omic techniques, such as Hi-C, long-read whole-genome sequencing, (single-cell) RNA-seq, and (single-cell) ATAC-seq with publicly available developmental and tumor datasets to generate new biological insights. You will work closely with clinicians, computational biologists, molecular pathologists and organoid researchers at the Princess Máxima Center.
 Your profile

 Previous experience with pediatric (brain) tumors, developmental neuroscience, or cancer epigenomics is advantageous.

Your gross monthly salary will depend on your experience and background and is based on scale 60 of the Collective Labor Agreement “Algemene Ziekenhuizen”. You will also receive 8.33% holiday allowance and an 8.33% end-of-year bonus.

Our research integrates molecular biology, genomics, and advanced experimental models to accelerate the development of more effective and less toxic therapies. academictransfer:364071.description:
Thermoplastic composites are widely regarded as promising materials for the next generation of commercial aircraft, combining excellent mechanical performance with low weight. In addition, their melt-processable matrix enables automated, high-rate manufacturing of components that can subsequently be assembled into complex aerostructures using welding. This provides significant opportunities for more efficient and cost-effective aircraft manufacturing.
However, welded composite assemblies are challenging to inspect using conventional non-destructive inspection techniques. As a result, larger safety margins are often required in structural design, leading to heavier structures, while maintenance intervals may be more conservative than necessary. Developing reliable methods to continuously assess the structural condition therefore enable both lighter designs and more efficient maintenance strategies.
To address this challenge, the project aims to develop structural health monitoring technologies based on a digital twin . The digital twin will combine information from the physical structure with models and monitoring data to assess its current structural state and predict its remaining lifetime. This will enable the condition of welded structures to be monitored throughout their service life, allowing maintenance to be planned when it is actually needed rather than according to predetermined intervals. Ultimately, this approach aims to contribute to lighter, safer, and more sustainable aircraft structures .
 The PhD positions 
 Experimental characterization and digital twin development 
A key challenge in developing a reliable digital twin is accurately characterizing the static and fatigue behaviour of welded thermoplastic composite joints. Since there are currently no well-established standards for fatigue testing of these joints, the project will involve developing experimental methods to reliably characterize their mechanical performance and damage evolution.
The experimental results will be used to develop constitutive models for the welded interface. In particular, these models should describe progressive interfacial damage development as a function of fatigue loading. The models will be implemented and validated in commercial finite element (FE) software. The resulting FE model will define the digital twin of the welded structure and provide the basis for the second PhD project, which will use the digital twin together with monitoring data to develop prognostic structural health monitoring strategies.
In this project you will:
 Perform experimental characterization of the static and fatigue performance of welded thermoplastic composite structures.
 Develop constitutive models that accurately describe the performance of the welded interface.
 Implement the developed models in commercial FE simulation software for the development of a digital twin and validate their accuracy against experiments.
We are looking for a colleague who has experience in mechanical experimentation of the fatigue behavior of composite materials and/or polymers, and is able to develop and implement constitutive models in FE software.
 Development of a Structural Health Monitoring system 
The ability to estimate the current state of the welded thermoplastic composite joint and the development of this state over time, is of decisive importance for lifetime performance modelling. The key challenges are the robust integration of a sensor system in the structure and the analysis of measured signals, which are typically strongly affected by environmental and operational conditions. This project aims to tackle these challenges by using piezo-electric and/or optical fiber based sensor system, combined with physics informed data analysis method, exploiting the digital twin model developed by the first PhD project.
In this project you will:
 Implement an effective sensor integration method for welded thermoplastic composite structures, using piezo-electric sensors, fiber optical sensor, or a combination of both.
 Perform dynamic experiments of pristine and (gradually) damaged structures to collect data for the state estimation methods.
 Develop signal processing methods to estimate, enriched by physics-based information, the current state of the welded structure and its development under fatigue loading.
We are looking for a colleague who has experience in sensor integration and dynamic experimentation, knowledge of piezo-electric or optical fiber based measurements, and proficiency in signal processing methods enriched with physics-based information.

REQUIREMENTS:
You are a highly motivated researcher who is driven by curiosity and has:
 A Master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering or equivalent.
 Good team-working abilities and a positive can-do mentality.
 Strong reporting and communication skills
 Proficiency in English, both spoken and written (we require a TOEFL > 90 or IELTS > 6.5 score).
 Further, the position on fatigue characterization and mechanical modelling requires:
 Experimental skills in the mechanical characterization of fiber reinforced composites or polymers; experience with fatigue testing is desired.
 Theoretical knowledge and skills in the modelling of (failure) of fiber reinforced composites.
 Experience with the finite element method and programming experience in scripting languages like Python or Matlab.
The position on structural health monitoring requires:
 Experimental and theoretical skills in dynamics and experiences with piezo-electric and/or fiber optic sensors.
 Experience with signal processing methods of data, enriched with physics-based information.

Welcome to Maastricht University! 
The Brightlands Future Farming Institute (BFFI) invites applications for a Postdoctoral Researcher to contribute to the development of next-generation autonomous crop monitoring and decision-support systems for Controlled Environment Agriculture (CEA).
This project focuses on the development, validation, and integration of non-destructive plant sensing technologies, enabling data-driven—and ultimately autonomous—crop management in greenhouse and vertical farming systems.
 Postdoctoral Researcher in Autonomous Controlled Environmental Agriculture 
 Our goal: to develop next-generation autonomous crop monitoring and decision-support systems for Controlled Environment Agriculture. By integrating plant sensing, data and crop models, we aim to enable more precise and sustainable crop management.
 Your colleagues: You will be based at BFFI in Venlo, a collaboration between BASF and the Maastricht University Faculty of Science and Engineering. At BFFI, researchers and students work on plant genetics, growth strategies, and crop management with the aim of achieving optimal crop performance by integrating plant, environment, and management. The position offers close collaboration with the Department of Advanced Computer Science and the Sensor Engineering group, creating a highly interdisciplinary research environment at the intersection of plant science, engineering, and data science.
Controlled Environment Agriculture is rapidly expanding worldwide and includes high-tech greenhouse and vertical farm production of vegetables, fruits, herbs, and ornamentals. Dutch expertise plays a leading role in this global development. By controlling environmental factors such as temperature, light, and fertigation, growing conditions can be optimized for crop performance, allowing for local production, efficient resource use, and a high degree of mechanization.
At the same time, the sector faces significant challenges, including labor shortages and increasing complexity in crop management. CEA systems are particularly well suited to data-driven innovation, where continuous streams of sensor data inform decisions on climate, irrigation, lighting, and crop handling. The grower of the future will increasingly rely on integrated digital systems that combine practical expertise with real-time feedback and predictive insights.
At BFFI, we aim to improve CEA system design and crop management by developing technologies that serve plants, people, and planet. By integrating data from plant sensors, production systems, and environmental conditions into advanced models and dashboards, we seek to deepen our understanding of crop performance and enable more precise and sustainable cultivation strategies.
 What you do 
In this position, you will work within a European collaborative project focused on developing advanced sensing and modeling approaches for CEA systems. Your research will involve the deployment of:
 non-invasive sensors to monitor canopy light interception in greenhouse environments,
 spectral sensing in the visible and near-infrared (NIR) range to estimate sugar and starch content, chlorophyll levels, and plant water status,
 AI-based computer vision systems to monitor crop development,
 integrated sensing frameworks that combine multiple data streams into efficient decision-support tools for growers.
The data collected through these approaches will be integrated into crop growth and transpiration models and combined with other monitoring systems. Initial experiments will be conducted in university growth chambers and greenhouse facilities, followed by validation in commercial-scale greenhouse operations in both the Netherlands and Belgium, ensuring a strong link between fundamental research and practical application. Within this project, you will work in close collaboration with the Sensor Engineering department and the Department of Advanced Computer Science (DACS) at Maastricht University, providing a highly interdisciplinary research environment.
Beyond your core research activities, you will contribute to ongoing projects within the Brightlands Future Farming Institute (BFFI) and collaborate across disciplines in areas such as data acquisition and analysis. These projects span topics including the relationship between food production, environmental impact, and human health, as well as developments in agricultural robotics and automation. This environment offers broad opportunities to apply your expertise in different contexts and further develop your interdisciplinary profile.
In addition, you will have the opportunity to contribute to teaching within the newly established MSc programme in Crop Biotechnology and Engineering, allowing you to build valuable academic teaching experience.
 Are you ready to set the course for the years ahead? Then we'd love to meet you. 
 What you bring 
We’re not looking for checkboxes; we’re interested in who you are and what you bring. Do you recognize yours

academictransfer:364094.description:
Zorg jij graag dat de financiële administratie tot in de puntjes klopt? Binnen het team Finance & Control (F&C) van de Faculteit Sociale Wetenschappen (FSW) werkt het projectcontrolteam aan de financiële beheersing van onderzoeksprojecten die worden gefinancierd door diverse externe subsidieverstrekkers. Het team bestaat uit drie projectcontrollers en twee projectadministrateurs. Als projectadministrateur werk je nauw samen met de projectcontrollers en je collega-projectadministrateur in een omgeving waarin nauwkeurigheid, samenwerking en kwaliteit centraal staan.
 Wat ga je doen? 
Als projectadministrateur ben je verantwoordelijk voor de dagelijkse administratieve ondersteuning van onderzoeksprojecten. Je zorgt voor een correcte, tijdige en volledige verwerking van financiële en administratieve gegevens en ondersteunt daarmee de projectcontrollers in hun werkzaamheden. Je bent het eerste aanspreekpunt voor administratieve vragen binnen het projectcontrolproces.
Je werkt zelfstandig aan de administratie van verschillende onderzoeksprojecten en stemt hierover regelmatig af met projectcontrollers en andere betrokken collega's. Je signaleert wanneer informatie ontbreekt of niet klopt, onderneemt actie en zorgt ervoor dat zaken tijdig worden opgevolgd. Daarnaast draag je bij aan een eenduidige werkwijze en denk je actief mee over het verbeteren en efficiënter maken van administratieve processen.
Je werkzaamheden bestaan onder andere uit:
 Inrichten en bijhouden van project- en stamgegevens in het financiële systeem.
 Verwerken van budgetwijzigingen en administratieve mutaties.
 Aanmaken en verwerken van externe facturen.
 Beheren van projectdossiers en zorgen voor een complete en correcte digitale archivering.
 Controleren van urenregistraties, declaraties en facturen op juistheid en volledigheid.
 Bewaken van deadlines en opvolgen van ontbrekende informatie of afwijkingen.
 Ondersteunen bij diverse rapportages en projectverantwoordingen.
 Ondersteunen bij en, in overleg met de projectcontrollers, coördineren van audits.
 Bijdragen aan het verbeteren, uniformeren en borgen van administratieve processen en werkinstructies.
Je hebt daarbij veel contact met de projectcontrollers. Waar zij zich steeds meer richten op financiële analyse, sturing en advisering, zorg jij voor een solide administratieve basis. Zo vullen jullie elkaar aan en vormen jullie samen een belangrijke schakel in de financiële ondersteuning van het wetenschappelijk onderzoek binnen de faculteit.

REQUIREMENTS:
Je houdt ervan dat zaken kloppen. Je bent nauwkeurig, gestructureerd en zelfstandig en krijgt energie van het aanbrengen en bewaken van overzicht. Je voelt je prettig in een rol waarin kwaliteit, betrouwbaarheid en duidelijke afspraken centraal staan. Als iets niet klopt of informatie ontbreekt, signaleer je dat en durf je hierop door te vragen.
Tegelijkertijd kijk je graag naar het grotere geheel. Je denkt mee over hoe administratieve processen beter en efficiënter kunnen en vindt het leuk om samen met collega's tot een eenduidige werkwijze te komen.
Daarnaast beschik je over:
 Minimaal een afgeronde financiële of administratieve mbo-opleiding en mbo+/hbo-werk- en denkniveau.
 Ervaring met administratieve processen, bij voorkeur in een projectomgeving of binnen een financiële administratie.
 Affiniteit met financiële systemen (ERP), Microsoft Office en digitale dossiervorming.
 Een praktische en nuchtere werkhouding en plezier in zorgvuldig en gestructureerd administratief werk.
 Goede communicatieve vaardigheden en een collegiale, samenwerkingsgerichte houding.
 Het vermogen om overzicht te houden, prioriteiten te stellen en verschillende deadlines te bewaken.

academictransfer:364095.description:
Binnen de faculteit Geowetenschappen zijn we voor het departement Aardwetenschappen op zoek naar een senior coördinator bedrijfsvoering.
 Wat ga je doen? 
De senior coördinator is de beoogde rechterhand en eerste vervanger van de departementsmanager. Samen met de departementsvoorzitter en de onderwijs- en onderzoeksdirecteuren vormt de departementsmanager het bestuur van het departement. De departementsmanager heeft een centrale rol in de verbinding tussen faculteit en departement ten aanzien van de bedrijfsvoering. De senior coördinator bedrijfsvoering ondersteunt en vervangt de departementsmanager hierin wanneer nodig. We zijn op zoek naar een senior coördinator bedrijfsvoering die zich thuis voelt in de combinatie van een beleidsondersteunende en een uitvoerende functie in een academische setting.
Je bent een professional die verbindend optreedt en medewerkers in staat stelt om resultaten te boeken op het gebied van onderzoek en onderwijs. Je aandachtsveld is de bedrijfsvoering van het departement, waaronder financiën, personeel en facilitaire zaken. Inhoudelijke betrokkenheid bij onderwijs en onderzoek is beperkt en in de context van de bedrijfsvoering. Je bent voortdurend alert op de interne en externe ontwikkelingen en je bent in staat deze ontwikkelingen in een vroeg stadium te signaleren, te analyseren, alsmede (pro)actief te handelen.
De functie van senior coördinator bedrijfsvoering is nieuw in ons departement en de specifieke taakverdeling tussen manager en senior coördinator bedrijfsvoering wordt samen vorm gegeven. Daarin zal het zwaartepunt van de departementsmanager bij het lange-termijn beleid en de Planning & Control-cyclus liggen en zal het aandachtsveld van de senior coördinator bedrijfsvoering dichter op de dagelijkse bedrijfsvoering liggen en bij het (helpen) tot uitvoering brengen van het beleid. Het gezamenlijke takenpakket ziet er als volgt uit:
De departementsmanager en de senior coördinator bedrijfsvoering
 vertalen samen met het departementsbestuur de facultaire visie en strategie en matchen deze met de departementale kaders, prioriteiten en ambities, zodat daarmee een departementale visie en strategie ontstaat;.
 denken actief mee met de bestuurlijke en strategische discussies in het departement, met de wetenschappelijke staf, en maken een vertaalslag naar de bedrijfsvoering, waarbij rekening wordt gehouden met de facultaire en departementale kaders;
 geven sturing aan een managementteam dat verder bestaat uit drie bedrijfsvoerders/ beleidsmedewerkers met elk hun eigen aandachtsveld (HR/Finance, Onderzoek/Impact, Algemeen/Facilitair) en enkele management-/office assistenten.
 verzamelen en/of vertalen de benodigde managementinformatie, anticiperen daarmee op ontwikkelingen op de (middel)lange termijn en adviseren het departementsbestuur;
 hebben oog voor de optimalisering van (veranderende) bedrijfsprocessen en het creëren van een cultuur voor effectieve samenwerking, binnen het departement en breder in de faculteit.
Het financiële proces omvat de jaarlijkse departementale begrotingscyclus in afstemming met het departementsbestuur, en in samenwerking met afdelingen Finance & HR van het faculteitsbureau. Met betrekking tot de dagelijkse bedrijfsvoering gaat het om het mede bewaken van diverse budgetten, beheren van de projectportefeuille in samenwerking met de afdeling Research Support Office (RSO), het team project control van het faculteitsbureau, en de coördinator bedrijfsvoering HR/Finance in het departement, reageren op (financiële) vragen en verzoeken vanuit de wetenschappers, enz.
Het HR-proces omvat het opstellen en bijstellen van het strategische personeelsplan voor het departement en dit vertalen in de begrotingscyclus. Met betrekking tot de dagelijkse bedrijfsvoering betreft dit de in-, door- en uitstroom van medewerkers van AW met inachtneming van relevante beleids- en rechtspositionele kaders, in samenwerking met de afdeling HR van het faculteitsbureau en de coördinator bedrijfsvoering HR/Finance in het departement; incidenteel ook meedenken over re-integratiemogelijkheden bij ziekte, vervanging bij lang verlof, enz.
Diverse bijkomende processen spelen door het jaar heen een rol, zoals het mede bewaken/ monitoren van de voortgang van promovendi, verantwoordelijkheid voor de interne communicatie (ook nieuwsbrief), accuraatheid van mailinglijsten, verantwoordelijkheid voor het aandragen en doorzetten van vacatures, toetsen aan kennisveiligheid, organiseren van departementsbrede activiteiten, enz. De senior coördinator bedrijfsvoering vervangt – indien nodig – de departementsmanager in faculteitsbreed managementoverleg.

REQUIREMENTS:
Je hebt een academisch werk- en denkniveau en bent een betrouwbare, enthousiaste en sociale spil binnen de dynamiek van het departement, die geconcentreerd en nauwkeurig werkt, met oog voor detail. Je bent sterk analytisch en oplossingsgericht en hebt oog voor verbeterprocessen. Je weet goed om te gaan met vertrouwelijke informatie. Kennis van de bedrijfsprocessen en -systemen van de Universiteit Utrecht is geen nadrukkelijke vereiste, maar kan als een pré worden beschouwd. Datzelfde geldt voor ervaring met een universitaire financiële begrotings- en verantwoordingscyclus en met personeelsplanning.
Je hebt bewezen beleidsondersteunende en organisatorische capaciteiten in een complexe/matrix organisatie, met ervaring in het (mede-)aansturen van een team en zorgen voor effectieve samenwerking tussen teams. Je weet anderen te motiveren en op een positieve manier van feedback te voorzien, waarmee je bijdraagt aan de sociale cohesie binnen het departement. Je toont een flexibele en dienstverlenende instelling, met een drijfveer voor ontzorgen van de onderzoekers en docenten waar dat vanuit de bedrijfsvoering mogelijk is. Je hebt een goede sensitiviteit voor de nuchtere cultuur van bètawetenschappers, en beschikt over voldoende verbindend leiderschap en overtuigingskracht om bij hen het belang van zakelijke kaders goed over het voetlicht te brengen.
Je bent open en communicatief sterk en beschikt over uitstekende taalvaardigheden in het Nederlands en Engels, wat je o.a. ook tot uiting kunt laten komen in het schrijven van beleidsnotities/-adviezen.
academictransfer:364095.title: Senior Coördinator Bedrijfsvoering Aardwetenschappen

academictransfer:364099.description:
Ben jij een gepromoveerd onderzoeker met affiniteit voor en ervaring met het thema, een interdisciplinaire achtergrond en ervaring met evidence-based werken en samenwerken met de praktijk? Dan is deze baan is iets voor jou!
 Wat ga je doen? 
 De onderzoeker komt te werken in het project  De Wereld Werkt in Groningen  dat wordt gefinancierd door het Nationaal Programma Groningen. Dit project beoogt bij te dragen aan het behouden van international talent voor de regionale arbeidsmarkt (arbeidsmigranten, internationale studenten, kenniswerkers en hun partners, asielzoekers en statushouders). Doel is samenwerking en kennisdeling tussen bestuurders, beleidsmakers, professionals, werkgevers, ervaringsdeskundigen en onderzoekers te stimuleren. 
 De onderzoeker zal aan het project bijdragen in een werkpakket gericht op onderzoek, data & monitoring, geleid door Liesbet Heyse (Sociologie) en Nina Hansen (Sociale Psychologie). Dit werkpakket biedt de unieke kans om wetenschappelijk onderzoek met ervaringen in de praktijk te verbinden via een evidence-based aanpak. De onderzoeker zal onder andere kennisbehoeften rondom dit thema in de regio identificeren, initiatieven rondom de doelgroepen in de regio inventariseren en een literatuurverkenning doen naar good practices. We werken hierin nauw samen met onderzoekers van de Hanze Hogeschool en andere partijen in het project.

REQUIREMENTS:
We zoeken een gedreven onderzoeker, gepromoveerd in de sociologie, psychologie of aanverwante sociale wetenschappen met
 Ervaring met en achtergrond in wetenschappelijk onderzoek naar arbeid, integratie en/of migratie.
 Ervaring in systematisch literatuuronderzoek, het opzetten, uitvoeren en analyseren van interviews, focusgroepen en eenvoudige vragenlijsten.
 Affiniteit met en ervaring met tenminste één van de doelgroepen in dit project.
 Ervaring in transdisciplinaire of co-creatie samenwerkingen (i.e. het werken met praktijkpartners en/of maatschappelijke stakeholders en het werken met onderzoekers met verschillende disciplinaire achtergronden, met name in de sociologie en psychologie).
 Bij voorkeur ervaring met het evalueren van interventies.
 Goede verbale en schriftelijke vaardigheden in het Nederlands en Engels.
 Excellente communicatie, plannings- en organisatievaardigheden.
 Vermogen om zelfstandig te werken en goed te functioneren in een team.
 Aantoonbare capaciteiten op de volgende competenties: conceptueel vermogen, omgevingsgerichtheid, presenteren en resultaatgerichtheid.

CONTRACT: Een functie van 0,8 fte voor 1,5 jaar.
academictransfer:364099.title: Onderzoeker voor project ter verbetering van de arbeidsmarktpositie van internationaal talent in Groningen en Noord-Drenthe

academictransfer:364104.description:
The Institute for Environmental Studies (IVM) of Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam invites applications for a postdoctoral researcher within the Environmental Policy Analysis (EPA) department.
As the successful candidate you’ll work on two projects, funded by NWO Social Sciences and Humanities Open Competition XS. The EnerWar project (“The Energy Weapon in the Age of Global Energy System Transformation”) is led by Dr. Mathieu Blondeel. Together, you will develop a taxonomy of the energy weapon, exploring its use, impacts and effectiveness over time, as well as how the nature of the energy weapon will change as the global energy transition ramps up. The second project is led by Dr. Oscar Widerberg and investigates the future of corporate climate commitments after the election of US president Trump. In addition, you will also contribute to the department’s acquisition efforts, including applications for external research grants (Dutch & European).
 Your duties 
 you will develop a taxonomy of the ‘energy weapon’, identifying its use, impacts and effectiveness over time
 you will develop a publicly accessible and detailed database of the historical use of the energy weapon
 you will set-up and execute interview with corporate leader about net zero commitments
 you will support the planning and implementation of a workshop on net zero commitments
 you will publish research results in international peer-reviewed journals and impact-oriented journals
 you will contribute to the educational programmes at the IVM, such as the supervision of Bachelor and Master students
 you will contribute to the administrative responsibilities of the EPA department and to IVM-wide tasks, including the preparation and development of research proposals for funding through different national and European agencies

REQUIREMENTS:
you possess a PhD in Political Science, International Relations, or a related discipline, specialising in energy or climate politics (having obtained a PhD degree is required by the start of employment)
 keen interest in geopolitical and political economic dimensions of the global energy transition
 a proven track record of publications in international peer-reviewed journals
 strong qualitative research skills, such as interviews, document and content analysis
 knowledge of and experience in grant proposal writing
 excellent proficiency and communication skills in English
We realise that each individual brings a unique set of skills, expertise and mindset. Therefore we are happy to invite anyone who recognises themselves in the profile to apply, even if you do not meet all the requirements.

CONTRACT: 1 year
academictransfer:364104.title: Postdoc: Energy weapons and the future of net-zero in the energy transition

academictransfer:364126.description:
Je ontwikkelt en analyseert de online DNA-poli, een online poli voor families met erfelijke borstkanker. Dat doe je samen met onderzoekers, artsen, patiënten en patiëntvertegenwoordigers. De DNA-poli moet patiënten en familieleden laagdrempelige toegang geven tot informatie over erfelijke borstkanker in de familie en hen ondersteunen bij de keuze voor DNA-onderzoek. Met de online DNA-poli willen we de toegang tot genetische informatie en DNA-onderzoek voor patiënten en familieleden eenvoudiger maken. Een virtuele assistent is een belangrijk onderdeel van de DNA-poli.
Vervolgens ga je de online DNA-poli landelijk testen in een gerandomiseerde trial. Je onderzoekt hoe de DNA-poli wordt gebruikt, wat de ervaringen van patiënten, familieleden en zorgverleners zijn en of de DNA-poli bijdraagt aan passende toegang tot DNA-onderzoek.
De DNA-poli is onderdeel van een landelijk onderzoeksproject dat zich richt op het beter opsporen van mensen met een erfelijke aanleg voor borstkanker. Binnen dit project ontwikkelen we samen met collega’s en patiënten innovatieve strategieën om erfelijke borstkanker beter en eerder op te sporen. Dit doen we door knelpunten in het proces van genetisch onderzoek, counseling en familieonderzoek aan te pakken. Zo dragen we bij aan het voorkomen van ziekte en sterfte.
Het project wordt gefinancierd door KWF Kankerbestrijding.

REQUIREMENTS:
Je bent afgestudeerd, bij voorkeur in de geneeskunde.
 Ervaring als (basis)arts in de klinische genetica is een pre.
 Je hebt een goede methodologische basis.
 Je hebt ervaring met kwalitatieve en kwantitatieve onderzoeksmethoden.
 Je beschikt over uitstekende organisatorische vaardigheden en communiceert uitstekend in het Nederlands.
 Je werkt nauwgezet en zelfstandig en hebt een sterk analytisch vermogen.
 Je werkt graag samen in een multidisciplinaire setting.
Voor meer informatie kun je contact opnemen met prof. dr. Margreet Ausems, klinisch geneticus, via 0887553800.
Je voert het onderzoek uit in nauwe samenwerking met onderzoekers van het Antoni van Leeuwenhoek en de Universiteit Twente.
academictransfer:364126.title: Promovendus Ontwikkeling online DNA-poli voor families met erfelijke borstkanker

academictransfer:364129.description:
We are seeking a highly motivated and skilled research technician to join the Kops lab at the Hubrecht Institute. We study the molecular mechanisms that ensure accurate chromosome segregation during cell division, with a strong focus on genome stability and its relevance to human disease.
In this role, you will play a central part in the generation, maintenance, and experimental use of human cell lines, supporting ongoing projects that combine state-of-the-art cell biology, advanced fluorescence microscopy, and sequencing-based approaches. You will work closely with PhD students and postdoctoral researchers in a collaborative and international research environment, contributing directly to cutting-edge research in mitosis and chromosome biology.
The Hubrecht Institute is an international research institute of the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences (KNAW) and is embedded in a vibrant scientific ecosystem with strong links to Utrecht University and UMC Utrecht. The institute provides excellent infrastructure, core facilities, and a stimulating environment for scientific and technical development.
 Key Responsibilities 
 Maintain and culture mammalian cell lines under sterile conditions.
 Generate genetically modified cell lines using CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing.
 Produce lentiviral vectors and perform lentiviral transductions.
 Design and construct plasmids using standard molecular cloning techniques.
 Isolate DNA, RNA, and proteins from mammalian cell lines.
 Perform PCR, qPCR, and genotyping assays.
 Assist with fluorescence microscopy and NGS library preparation.
 Maintain accurate experimental records in an electronic laboratory notebook.
 Contribute to the organization and daily operation of the laboratory.

REQUIREMENTS:
Essential Qualifications 
 Completed HBO or Bachelor's degree in Molecular Biology, Cell Biology, Biomedical Sciences, Biotechnology, or a related field.
 Experience with mammalian cell culture and molecular biology techniques.
 Strong organizational skills, and the ability to work independently and collaboratively.
 Good communication skills and proficiency in spoken and written English.

CONTRACT: 1 year
academictransfer:364129.title: Research Technician - Molecular Cell Biology - Hubrecht Institute - Utrecht

academictransfer:364130.description:
We are looking for a doctoral researcher to study how generative AI is changing learning, expertise and relationships at work.
The PhD is a four year project that is part of EMANAIRE (Empowering Human Agency in AI-Augmented Futures of Work) , a Horizon Europe Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network. You will be based at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, while working as part of an international network of doctoral researchers and universities. The programme includes joint training, research seminars, methods workshops and opportunities to collaborate with partner institutions across Europe. A six-month secondment is planned as part of the project.
Because this position is part of an MSCA Doctoral Network, specific eligibility conditions apply : Candidates can be of any nationality but must not already hold a doctoral degree at the time of recruitment. Under the MSCA mobility rule , candidates must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the Netherlands for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately before their recruitment date.

REQUIREMENTS:
Your research will focus on what happens when generative AI becomes part of everyday organisational life. You will study how early-career employees learn their jobs, seek help, develop expertise and deal with responsibility when AI is increasingly involved in their work.
This is a qualitative research project , with substantial ethnographic fieldwork where you will be interviewing and observing people in organizations. Relevant masters degree backgrounds include organisation studies, sociology, anthropology, STS, information systems or related fields. We are looking for exceptional grades in a masters programme, particularly demonstrating strong writing, reading, critical thinking, and presentation skills. We are not looking for a primarily quantitative or experimental researcher. The project does not involve building AI systems.
This project requires someone who is curious about people and organisations. You need to be comfortable approaching and talking with a range of people, building relationships in the field, listening carefully and noticing what happens around you. Ethnographic research also requires persistence. You will be expected to problem solve on the go, keep detailed fieldnotes, conduct and analyse interviews, and share your findings with the team. KIN is a collaborative research group and we regularly share work-in-progress for feedback.

CONTRACT: 1 year
academictransfer:364130.title: PhD Vacancy: Knowledge Creation and Sharing in Augmented Organisations

academictransfer:364132.description:
Wil jij je ontwikkelen als onderzoeker en via onderzoek en innovatie bijdragen aan betere zorg voor mensen met een erfelijke ziekte? Dan is deze functie iets voor jou. De positie biedt jou de mogelijkheid om zinvol promotieonderzoek te verrichten en geeft je de kans om concreet bij te dragen aan vroege opsporing van erfelijke borstkanker. Je wordt begeleid door een breed team van experts, werkzaam in het UMCG, het RadboudUMC en het Amsterdam UMC en doet op landelijk niveau onderzoek. Interesse? Dan nodigen we je van harte uit te solliciteren.
 Wat ga je doen 
Als onderzoeker ben je betrokken bij het ontwikkelen en evalueren van methodes om familieleden te informeren bij erfelijke borstkanker. 
 Achtergrond van het onderzoek 
Erfelijke aanleg is een belangrijke oorzaak van borstkanker op jonge leeftijd en familiaire borstkanker. Patiënten met een verdenking op erfelijke borstkanker kunnen via de afdeling klinische genetica DNA-onderzoek krijgen. Als hierbij een erfelijke aanleg wordt vastgesteld, kunnen gezonde familieleden, die 50% kans hebben, zich laten testen op deze erfelijke aanleg. Bij familieleden met een erfelijke aanleg kan de kanker via regelmatige controles in een vroeg stadium worden opgespoord, of vrijwel worden voorkomen door preventieve operaties. Familieleden zonder erfelijke aanleg kunnen worden gerustgesteld. We zien dat slechts een deel van de familieleden naar een genetica afdeling komt voor meer informatie en indien gewenst DNA-onderzoek.
 Inhoud van het onderzoek 
In het onderzoek willen we beter begrijpen waarom een deel van de familieleden niet komt voor genetische zorg. Door middel van interviews onder patiënten, familieleden en zorgverleners willen we nagaan wat de behoeftes zijn en welke barrières worden ervaren. Ook willen we nagaan hoe de zorg in verschillende ziekenhuizen is ingericht en of dit gerelateerd is aan het percentage familieleden dat voor genetische zorg komt.
Op basis van de literatuur en de kennis die is vergaard via de interviews, zullen we via co-creatiesessies samen met patiënten, familieleden en zorgverleners strategieën ontwikkelen om het informeren en vroeg opsporen van familieleden te verbeteren. Deze strategieën zullen we via pilotstudies ook in de praktijk evalueren op effectiviteit en acceptatie. 
Het betreft een promotietraject in het UMCG van 1,0 fte gedurende vier jaar. Begeleiding gebeurt door een multidisciplinair team van begeleiders uit het UMCG (dr. Imke Christiaans en prof. dr. Adelita Ranchor), het RadboudUMC (dr. Maaike Haadsma) en het Amsterdam UMC (dr. Mirjam Fransen). Het onderwerp van dit promotietraject is onderdeel van een groter landelijk op te starten consortium op het gebied van erfelijke borstkanker ( Enorme impuls voor opsporing van erfelijke borstkanker ). academictransfer:364134.description:
The University of Twente, Faculty ITC, wishes to increase the number of women in the faculty to have a more balanced staff profile. During all phases of the selection process, we will therefore prioritize selecting women who fit the profile.
 Your challenge 
The Dutch government, through the Ministry of Education, Culture and Science, has responded to the current global environmental challenges by establishing sector plan positions in critical scientific domains. At the Department of Environmental Resources, one of our activities is to address these challenges by developing and applying Geostatistical models for bridging knowledge gaps, data scarcity and uncertainty gaps, and governance gaps related to monitoring the environment on which humans depend.
A part of this is **spatial statistics of sensor data integration for nature-inclusive solutions ** for monitoring stress and diseases of tree crops**.** Tree crops like cocoa, apart from their direct economic functions for smallholder farmers, sit at the intersection of many beneficial ecological functions (including carbon sequestration and cultural identity). However, these functions are threatened by environmental stressors and diseases such as Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus (CSSV) disease, which depend on the complex web of interactions between and within above-ground and below-ground biotic and abiotic factors. The prevailing data and methodological gaps that have perpetuated knowledge gaps in the spatial and spatiotemporal patterns of tree disease, and the widened governance gaps of farms, have motivated this topic.
You will develop spatial statistical methods to integrate ground-based IoT sensor data, remote sensing data, and in-situ data for mapping the spatial trends of cocoa diseases. You will be involved in setting up an IoT sensor network in cocoa farms in Ghana. You are expected to address data integration challenges, including (1) spatial misalignment of networks , (2) temporal misalignments of observations, (2) probabilistic or likelihood misalignments , and (3) data quality issues, such as uncertainties in measurements, sparsity of network coverage resulting in small N , _missing data _resulting from malfunction of sensors, and outliers . For the purposes of evaluating model transferability, you will make a comparison with other economically important tree crops in food forests in the Netherlands. You will design a measurement setup for cocoa trees and review the wide range of applications of IoT sensors, their uncertainties, and the observable variables above and below ground that are important for predicting tree crop diseases and stresses. You will also explore simulation scenarios to evaluate the impact of indigenous and formal farming management practices on plant diseases.

REQUIREMENTS:
An MSc related to geoinformation science and earth observation, spatial and spatiotemporal modelling, spatial statistics, and/or machine learning. You enjoy applying these modelling skills to analyse and explain interactions within environmental and ecological systems
 Able to handle and integrate multi-temporal and multi-spatial data from multiple sources, including earth observation data, IoT-based sensor data, and in situ data
 Comfortable with programming or scripting in Python or R for data analysis and for bringing your models to the data
 Good communication skills and an excellent command of the English language
 Enjoy engaging in team science with project and societal partners
 Willing to travel and to collect data in the field; familiarity with cocoa farming in Ghana is an advantage given the required interaction with local managers.
 Motivated to contribute to knowledge dissemination and uptake activities for societal partners while also embracing Open Science and FAIR data principles
 A passion for education in an international classroom.
 Interested in developing educational materials and teaching topics related to spatial modelling and understanding interactions in environmental systems.
 A dedicated and considerate advisor for MSc students.

academictransfer:364137.description:
What could reparations for colonialism look like? As a PhD candidate, you will explore this urgent question, using participatory and creative research methods to foreground the experiences and expectations of Indo and Indonesian communities affected by colonialism. 
Recent developments like the Rhodes Must Fall movement have highlighted the need to address historical injustices and global inequalities, but responses so far have often been superficial. Apologies, like the apologies the Dutch government offered to the Moluccan population in the Netherlands last summer, are often made, but more material forms of redress are slow to follow or remain absent altogether. Current scholarly debates in relation to historical injustices concern the potential and scope of reparations, which are often prioritised by survivors but politically sensitive. So far there is no consensus or empirical data on how reparations could address colonial legacies.
This important question will guide your PhD research in the NWO-funded project ‘Decolonising Reparations: Transforming the Legacies of Colonialism’, led by Dr Sanne Weber, Assistant Professor at the Department of Political Science. You will use participatory and creative research methods to investigate the impact of colonialism on affected communities within Indonesia and the Indonesian diaspora in the Netherlands, as well as what these communities expect from reparations for colonialism.
You will work together with participants on co-produced multimedia products about the potential role of reparations in addressing historical grievances. In addition, you will conduct interviews with a wider group of stakeholders and a vignette study with the broader population in Indonesia. You will receive training on participatory and creative approaches by the Principal Investigator. Strong knowledge of qualitative research methodologies and familiarity with participatory research approaches are an asset.
During your PhD, you will collaborate with the PI and a postdoctoral researcher who will focus on Belgium and the Great Lakes Region of Central Africa. By comparing these case studies and triangulating the diverse methods, the project will enable a better understanding of potential forms of reparations for colonialism. In this way, the project aims to contribute to the decolonisation of reparative justice theory to address the legacies of colonialism committed by Western Europe.
Your duties and responsibilities include:
 Developing a concrete and feasible research project fitting the overarching theme and resulting in the defence of an article-based PhD thesis at the end of the 4th year.
 Setting up and carrying out in-depth and independent participatory fieldwork.
 Authoring and co-authoring publications with other team members.
 Participating in conferences, workshops, seminars and other scholarly activities.
 Being part of the research team and contributing to the overall organisation and strategy of the team and the project.
 Being an active member of the Department of Political Science and the Centre for International Conflict Analysis and Management.
 As part of your PhD position, you will also contribute to teaching (max 5%) and will have the opportunity to work on components of your University Teaching Qualification (BKO) portfolio.
Your supervision team will consist of Dr Sanne Weber (main substantive PhD supervisor) and Dr. Haley Swedlund.
 Would you like to learn more about what it’s like to pursue a PhD at Radboud University? Visit the page about working as a PhD candidate .

REQUIREMENTS:
Required: 
 You hold a Master’s degree in political science or another relevant discipline, such as conflict studies, anthropology or development studies.
 You have a proven substantive research interest in issues of justice, including transitional, reparative and social justice, historical and ongoing injustice, reparations and redress, and theories of justice, decolonisation and intersectionality.
 You are trained in qualitative research and analysis methods. You have experience with conducting fieldwork, collecting and analysing qualitative data, ideally in relation to the theme of this project.
 You are familiar with Indonesia as you are from Indonesia or the Indo community, have worked or lived there, or have spent an extended period there.
 You are willing to conduct several months of in-depth fieldwork in Indonesia.
 You have a proven excellent command of written academic English.
 You have experience with planning, taking initiative, organising events and presenting your work to a wider audience.
 Desired: 
 You are trained in participatory and/or arts-based research methodologies.
 You have experience working with communities at a local level and have a good command of Bahasa or another relevant local language.
 You have proficiency in Dutch.
 You have experience with basic quantitative methods of research and analysis.

Have you completed your PhD? Are you eager to enrich your knowledge on biodiversity as a postdoc? Then Naturalis in Leiden is the place for you . Pursuing a postdoc at Naturalis means working on research with a truly global impact — contributing directly to biodiversity. With state-of-the-art museum collections and lab facilities, many inspiring colleagues, and access to our international network, Naturalis offers everything you need to strengthen your career as a scientist.
As a postdoctoral fellow...

 You build valuable professional connections by participating in both the academic and social activities of our PhD- and postdoc community. Furthermore, through our collaborations with diverse partners, you will strengthen your international profile.
 This is what you'll be doing 
As a postdoctoral fellow, you will work together with colleagues to meet the Integrative Taxonomy ambitions of Naturalis. Our goal is to have a more efficient and accurate source of species identification for difficult plant families. You will use cutting-edge genomic and Artificial Intelligence methods from several plant families to identify novel genomic regions and further develop and implement bioinformatic pipelines. For example, using AI we see opportunities to use the genomic data to train datasets for species identification and delimitation, such as image recognition, but we are also open to your innovative ideas. Your contribution will break new ground, moving beyond current plant DNA barcoding methods to explore these genome-wide and AI approaches in a high risk/high reward project.
Your work supports high-impact institutional programs such as ARISE, AcellARISE, and eDentity, which use AI and DNA samples to monitor biodiversity and identify Dutch biodiversity. Alongside shaping this research, you will actively share your discoveries through high-profile scientific publications and international presentations. Furthermore, you will have the opportunity to mentor students and contribute to teaching, fostering the next generation of biodiversity scientists.

academictransfer:364147.description:
Small particles such as pollen and microplastics in the environment are involved in triggering inflammatory diseases, but current methods for monitoring these particles rely largely on labor-intensive identification approaches and provide limited information on the diversity of particles present. We aim to develop a novel portable system for rapid and multidimensional characterization of inhaled particles using portable flow cytometry. The candidate will develop the analytical and experimental approaches required to distinguish particles based on their multidimensional characteristics. As a first step, these approaches will be developed and validated using well-characterized blood cells, building on the group's expertise in flow cytometry and cellular heterogeneity. Subsequently, the technology will be adapted and translated to the characterization of particles in environmental samples. The project combines flow cytometry, multidimensional data analysis, cell and particle characterization, and technology development, ultimately aiming to bring laboratory-based measurements towards a portable system for real-world environmental monitoring.

REQUIREMENTS:
You (nearly) completed a MSc degree in a relevant area of research such as immunology, cellular biology, biophysics, analytical sciences, or a related discipline and have experience with laboratory research.
 Experience with flow cytometry, cell culture, microscopy, molecular biology or quantitative data analysis is a plus.
 You are interested in developing and applying novel technologies and are willing to learn and work across disciplinary boundaries.
 You collaborate with colleagues, share knowledge and skills, and contribute to a positive team environment.
 You plan and organize your work effectively and take responsibility for your own research.
 When experiments do not work as expected, you critically evaluate the results and explore alternative approaches.
 You communicate your findings clearly, both in writing and when presenting scientific data.
 You approach scientific questions with curiosity, take initiative and actively seek to understand and solve new problems.
There is no fixed closing date for this vacancy. We will close the vacancy once we have found a suitable candidate.

Challenge: Master electrically-induced pH gradients; Change: Investigate electrochemical interfaces to optimize separation performance; Impact: A chemical-free and circular Dutch process industry 
 Job description 
Industrial processes and wastewater treatment currently depend heavily on chemical processing aids, increasing energy consumption and adding complexity to process operations and logistics. In this project, a collaborative initiative involving both academic and industrial partners, coordinated by the Institute for Sustainable Process Technology (ISPT), we aim to develop a fundamentally different approach. By harnessing electric fields to create local pH gradients and electrostatic molecular interactions, we seek to replace conventional chemical processing aids.
As a PhD candidate at TU Delft, you will investigate the fundamental behavior of electrically induced pH gradients at critical interfaces, including electrodes and membranes used in electrochemical separation processes. You will work towards specific user-cases / user-applications and demonstrate the membrane processes in close collaboration with the partners and other collaborators in the consortium, which are not yet known and will be defined throughout the project. Your main research will focus on:
 visualizing and quantifying local pH gradients using Fluorescence Lifetime Imaging Microscopy (FLIM) to understand their influence on separation performance and membrane durability;
 elucidating transport phenomena in membranes by integrating your experimental observations with advanced electrode characterization data generated within the consortium; and
 developing membrane modification strategies to enhance performance, durability, and antifouling properties, thereby reducing energy demand as well as capital and operational costs for specific user-cases.
In close collaboration with project partners and other research groups at the TU Delft, you will also contribute to the development of physics-informed models by performing two-dimensional simulations of local pH gradients. These models will link interfacial mass transport limitations near membranes and electrodes with system-level performance, enabling the design of more efficient and sustainable electrochemical separation technologies.
You will join the interdisciplinary research team of the Bazyar Lab within the Department of Chemical Engineering, section of Catalysis, Separation, and Electrochemical engineering (CaSE), working under the supervision of Dr. Hanieh Bazyar . As part of this project, you will collaborate closely with Dr. Jouke Dykstra at Wageningen University and with industrial partners from the Dutch food, paper, and chemical sectors.
At the Bazyar Lab, we are driven by the ambition to advance sustainable process engineering through the development of innovative separation materials and technologies. We foster an open, collaborative, and supportive research environment where team members share knowledge, help one another, and receive the guidance and training needed to grow into independent researchers.
In addition to conducting research, you will contribute to education by serving as a teaching assistant in various courses, supervising bachelor thesis projects, and mentoring master's students during their graduation research. Through these activities, you will further develop your leadership, communication, and supervisory skills.
 Job requirements 
You are motivated to conduct innovative research that supports the transition toward sustainable process engineering. Working at the intersection of electrochemistry and separation technology, you apply strong analytical skills to address complex challenges. You thrive in interdisciplinary and international collaborations, communicating effectively with a wide range of stakeholders, while also being confident in working independently. Beyond research, you are keen to supervise master's and bachelor's students and continuously broaden your expertise and professional capabilities.
To be considered for this position, you should possess:
 An MSc degree in Chemical Engineering, Process Engineering, Applied Physics, Physical Chemistry or a closely related discipline.
 Hands-on experience with electrochemical systems and/or electrically driven separation technologies.
 Knowledge of membrane processes, transport phenomena, advanced characterization techniques, such as fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM), and/or experience with 2D computational modeling.
 Experience with designing custom-built experimental set-ups
 Strong written and verbal communication skills in English, enabling you to thrive in an international and multidisciplinary research environment.

academictransfer:364160.description:
Within the NWA research programme BIO COMPaSS (BIOlogical age-driven, COMmunal, Personalised System for Sustainable health promotion), universities, university medical centers, companies and citizens work together to motivate people towards a healthier lifestyle by providing insight into their biological age – a metric that often says more about health than chronological age. The project aims to develop an evidence-based set of biomarkers of ageing and to test how these can be used for sustainable health promotion.
As a PhD candidate in Work Package 3 (WP3), within the Department of Rehabilitation Medicine at Amsterdam UMC, you will focus on the characterization of biological-age-related phenotypes. You will investigate which combinations of biomarkers (epigenetic, metabolic, organ-specific, functional and lifestyle-related) form patterns that provide information about someone’s current and future health and functioning.
You will use rich existing datasets (for example large cohorts and registries) and work closely with other BIO COMPaSS PhD candidates who focus on causality, interventions and implementation. The insights you generate on phenotypes and biomarker profiles will be an important building block for personalized lifestyle interventions within BIO COMPaSS.
 Would you like to know more about the different phases within the PhD trajectory? You can read more about this on this page . 
As a PhD candidate, you coordinate and conduct the research within WP3 in close collaboration with clinical and methodological experts. Your work will be largely data-driven, always with a clear eye on application in rehabilitation practice.
Your tasks include:
 Designing and conducting a systematic review of biomarkers of biological age (epigenetic, metabolic, organ-specific, functional), including assessment of clinimetric properties.
 Selecting, linking, cleaning and harmonizing existing datasets, including population studies and clinical databases, in collaboration with partners within BIO COMPaSS.
 Applying advanced statistical and data-science methods (e.g. clustering, latent class/latent profile analyses, dimension reduction, multimodal integration, prediction models) to identify biological-age phenotypes.
 Characterizing the identified phenotypes in relation to health and functioning.
 Contributing to the translation of phenotypes into practical biomarker sets that can be used in clinical follow-up and lifestyle interventions.
 Publishing results in international peer-reviewed journals and presenting at (inter)national conferences.
 Working closely with PhD candidates, postdocs, clinicians, epidemiologists, data scientists and other researchers in the BIO COMPaSS consortium.
From year 4 onwards, specific tasks will gradually be transferred to a second PhD candidate within WP3, with whom you will already collaborate closely from the start. You will complete your project with a PhD thesis.

REQUIREMENTS:
You have a strong analytical interest in ageing, lifestyle interventions, biomarkers and data analysis, and you are keen to conduct research with direct relevance for the health of people with (or at risk of) lifestyle-related conditions.
In addition, you have:
 A completed Master’s degree in a relevant field, for example Human Movement Sciences, Epidemiology, Biostatistics, Bioinformatics, Health Sciences, Biomedical Sciences, Data Science or a related discipline.
 Affinity with ageing and biomarker research, preferably including epigenetic or metabolic biomarkers.
 Good programming skills in statistical software (e.g. R, Python or similar), or strong motivation and demonstrable basic skills to learn this quickly.
 Preferably experience with analyzing large and/or high-dimensional data (e.g. omics, extensive clinical datasets, registries).
 Interest in or experience with advanced statistical methods (e.g. multivariate models, causal inference, machine learning) is an asset.
 Good oral and written communication skills in English.
 Preferably good command of Dutch, in view of coordination with clinical partners and, where needed, contact with patients.
 A proactive attitude, strong organizational skills and the ability to work both independently and in a multidisciplinary team.
We greatly value an inclusive work environment and explicitly invite candidates with diverse backgrounds and experiences to apply.
