academictransfer:364214.description:
Microscopic calcite (CaCO3) shells of plankton sink through ocean waters to the seafloor by the trillions each year, taking along essential nutrients such as phosphorus (P). Ocean acidification is likely to alter global CaCO3 fluxes, with so far unknown consequences for P cycling, ocean fertility and CO2 uptake. Our lack of knowledge regarding these feedbacks limits our insight in ocean functioning under environmental change, both in the (ancient) past and the human-impacted future.
 Your job 
The NWO-funded PHOSFLUX project aims to shed light on these unknowns, by quantifying the role of CaCO3 fluxes and acidification in global marine P cycling through a combination of field work in the North Atlantic Ocean, laboratory experiments and numerical modelling. A scientific cruise with our research vessel Pelagia will allow us to investigate CaCO3 – P interactions in the field. Through controlled lab experiments, we will dive deeper into the underlying chemical and mineralogical processes, to eventually capture them in physical-chemical models that predict the impact of acidification on marine P cycling.
The PHOSFLUX project is a collaboration between the NIOZ (dr. Peter Kraal) and Utrecht University (UU; prof. dr. Mariëtte Wolthers), combining unique sea-going and on-shore experimentation with advanced analytical tools to understand mineral-water interactions from microscopic to ocean-basin scale. Besides PI’s Kraal and Wolthers, the PHOSFLUX team consists of a NIOZ-based PhD student performing experiments and analyses, and a UU-based postdoctoral researcher who focuses on modelling the CaCO3 – P interactions.
As postdoctoral researcher within PHOSFLUX, your role is to model P dynamics in sinking and deposited marine snow in relation to changing environmental conditions in the water column. To achieve this, you will create a reactive-transport model for P dynamics that will include processes such as CaCO3 dissolution, organic matter decomposition and adsorption/incorporation of PO4 into solid phases of marine snow. You will test the performance of your model by simulating experimental and field data in collaboration with the PHOSFLUX PhD student.

REQUIREMENTS:
We are looking for a highly motivated postdoctoral candidate with a background in biogeochemical modelling.
You must have successfully completed a PhD programme in Earth Sciences, Environmental Sciences, Biology or a related discipline by the time the position starts. Preferably, you also have:
 Experience and affinity with biogeochemistry and marine research;
 Experience in numerical modelling of mineral-water interactions and/or organic matter degradation processes;
 Experience or strong interest in synchrotron-based analysis techniques
You approach scientific problems with determination and are eager to develop multidisciplinary skills. You must be willing to travel abroad to join the PHOSFLUX team during synchrotron beamtimes and to present your research to an international research community. As this project requires close collaboration within the research team, candidates are expected to be excellent team players. You also have excellent written and spoken English skills and good general communicational skills. We highly encourage applicants from diverse backgrounds to join us.

Computational design of mechanical metamaterials for 3d printed footwear 
 Job description 
The Faculty of Industrial Design Engineering at TU Delft is seeking three highly motivated researchers to join an exciting collaborative research project on 3D-printed footwear innovation, carried out in close collaboration with industrial partners.
The project aims to develop an integrated computational design and digital fabrication workflow for next-generation footwear. The research combines biomechanics, computational design, mechanical metamaterials, additive manufacturing, and digital workflows to create novel footwear concepts with improved performance and manufacturability.
One of the three positions will focus on mechanical metamaterials design.
This researcher will develop computational methods and experimentally evaluate mechanical metamaterials for footwear applications.
Responsibilities:
 Design mechanical metamaterials for functional performance
 Perform computational modelling and simulation
 Prototype and experimentally characterise designs
 Optimise structures for manufacturability and performance
 Collaborate closely with the computational design and biomechanics researchers
 Job requirements 
 MSc (or equivalent) in Mechanical Engineering, Computational Science and Engineering, or a closely related discipline
 Strong background in mechanics and finite element analysis
 Experience with topology optimisation and/or inverse design
 Experience with additive manufacturing or mechanical testing is an advantage
 Programming experience in Python, MATLAB, or C++ is desirable.
 TU Delft (Delft University of Technology) 
Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference.
For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future.
At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward.
 Faculty Industrial Design Engineering 
Matching the evolution of people with the speed of the revolution of technology. This is the focus of the Faculty of Industrial Design Engineering (IDE). Delft designers act as a bridge between advances in technology and the needs of people, organisations and society to create products, services and systems with purpose.
IDE is a leader in design research across the application areas of mobility, sustainability and health, as well as its development of design tools and methods. A 350-strong research team and over 2,000 students work together in our inspiring hall, labs and studios.
In close cooperation with industry, the public sector and NGOs we rehearse possible futures in research and education to design for a complex future.
Click here to go to the website of the Faculty of Industrial Design Engineering.
 Conditions of employment 
 Duration of contract is 12 months. Temporary.
 A job of 32-36 hours per week.
 A salary based on scale 8 or 10 will be applicable and is depending on graduation date and years of relevant work experience after graduation. With a salary between €3537 - €5760 gross per month based on a fulltime contract (38 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%.
 An excellent pension scheme via the ABP.
 The possibility to compile an individual employment package every year.
 Discount with health insurers on supplemental packages.
 Flexible working week.
 Every year, 232 leave hours (at 38 hours). You can also sell or buy additional leave hours via the individual choice budget.
 Plenty of opportunities for education, training and courses.
 Partially paid parental leave

Wil jij als HR-professional bijdragen aan de verdere strategische positionering van HR en écht impact maken op mens en organisatie?
 Wat ga je doen? 
Het HR team van de faculteit Geowetenschappen is een vakkundig team met brede kennis en een grote betrokkenheid bij goede dienstverlening. De afgelopen jaren is de HR-adviesfunctie verschoven van een operationeel-tactische naar een tactisch-strategische partnerrol. Een ontwikkeling die nog volop in gang is. Jouw expertise en actieve bijdrage zijn dan ook van cruciaal belang om deze verschuiving succesvol te realiseren en HR daadwerkelijk als strategische partner binnen de faculteit en de universiteit te positioneren. Dat vraagt ontwikkeling in ons eigen team – denk aan beter benutten van onze eigen expertise, delen van vakkennis, een duidelijker gezicht naar buiten – en het bestendigen van goede samenwerkingsrelaties buiten het team. Daarnaast brengt de komst van een nieuwe SAP applicatie (in 2028) veranderingen in onze processen, wat vraagt om eenduidige werkwijzen van het merendeel van onze werkprocessen.
Als HR adviseur van alle ondersteunende diensten in de faculteit adviseer je gevraagd en ongevraagd leidinggevenden op het gebied van personeels- en organisatievraagstukken. Je begeleidt leidinggevenden en teams bij de implementatie en ontwikkeling van strategische personeelsplanning. Je geeft strategisch-tactisch advies waarbij je draagvlak creëert, en oog hebt voor de bredere organisatiedoelen en de lange termijn. Dit betekent dat je actief bijdraagt in veranderingen van positionering HR. Hierbij werk je nauw samen met alle collega’s binnen het team. Je adviseert en ondersteunt bij complexe HR casuïstiek.
Samen met het Hoofd HR zet jij je in voor de coördinatie en communicatie van ons HR meerjarenplan. M.b.t. de uitvoering enthousiasmeer, motiveer je anderen, bewaak je de voortgang en communiceer je over de status met verschillende stakeholders. Daarnaast draag je bij aan faculteitsbrede zaken zoals het coördineren van het medewerkerstevredenheidsonderzoek en de ingezette cultuurverandering van Erkennen en Waarderen waarbij het er om gaat dat elke bijdrage aan het geheel telt en samenwerking over grenzen heen gestimuleerd wordt. Binnen ons team ben je sparringpartner en expert m.b.t. ons functiehuis, vanuit dat kader neem je ook deel aan de kenniskring op dat gebied. Wij zoeken een door de wol geverfde HR adviseur met veel ervaring in het begeleiden van SPP en die enthousiast bijdraagt aan de verdere ontwikkeling van onze afdeling, het faculteitsbureau en de organisatie als geheel. How can we accelerate the discovery of next-generation materials — from porous architectures for CO₂ capture to photoactive systems for sustainable solar-energy conversion and unprecedented photomedicines? In this PhD project, you will build a self-driving laboratory platform that will help solving outstanding questions at the forefront of (photo)chemistry by implementing automated spectroscopy workflows for molecular systems and thin films in combination with AI-driven process optimization. Help us shape the future of chemical research!
 Self-driving lab platform for photochemical and porosity research 
Join a highly interdisciplinary project with the spectroscopy at its core at the University of Amsterdam that brings together photophysics, spectroscopy, automation, flow technology and functional materials supervised by a team of passionate experts: Dr Tomáš Šolomek, Dr Bettina Baumgartner, and Prof Tim Noël.
The project aims at establishing a self-driving platform based on RoboChem, extending its capabilities to research in porous and photoactive materials. You will first implement new reliable and quantitative diffusion-ordered optical spectroscopy that will permit rapid and automated determination of fundamental photochemical parameters, such as optical spectra, quenching, or quantum yields. This will aid and abet discovery of new systems for photoactivated chemotherapy. Second, you will develop a flow-based ATR-UV–Vis spectroscopy platform that follows the formation of porous or photoactive thin films in real time. By measuring both polarization directions, you will determine how molecular building blocks become oriented during film growth, and how the films respond to external perturbations, such as molecular guests, light or charge. The focus will be on organic cages and metal–organic framework (MOF) thin films as key material classes.
The broader goal is to create robust, automated set of spectroscopic tools that connect molecular structure and organization, their properties and function.
 This is what you are going to do 
 Design and build flow setups using 3D printer, pumps, valves operated by a computer and the corresponding software. 
 Develop flow cells to connect various spectroscopic tools to the setup. 
 Create and validate reproducible automated workflows for quantitative photophysical measurements to obtain optical spectra and quantum-yields. 
 Implement AI methods to search in the parameter space that affects the measured data and translate the observations into mechanistic insight. 
 Develop a controlled flow system for in situ ATR-UV–Vis spectroscopy including polarization and use it to monitor the formation, orientation, and evolution of porous or photoactive thin films. 
 Turn the developed methods into robust, documented and transferable experimental workflows, analyse the resulting multidimensional datasets, publish the results and collaborate closely with the supervisory team and colleagues.

 You enjoy experimental research and want to work at the interface of physical chemistry, spectroscopy, photochemistry and instrumentation.  You are interested in instrument automation and quantitative data analysis. Experience with Python, LabVIEW, or Matlab for instrument control/data processing is required, but you do not need to be an expert at the start. 
 You can document experiments carefully, work safely with chemical samples and solvents, and communicate results clearly with collaborators from different scientific backgrounds. 
 Strong initiative and passion for science.

You will have room to develop expertise in quantitative photophysics, optical spectroscopy, laboratory automation, flow systems and functional thin-film materials, while working with supervisors who bring complementary expertise.

Do you want to help combat animal disease outbreaks such as foot-and-mouth disease and bluetongue? Do you have experience with virological, immunological, and molecular techniques, and do you want to participate in research into viral diseases and thereby contribute to the health of animals and humans? Then read on and apply quickly!
An important task of WBVR as a national reference laboratory is to develop and validate diagnostic tests to detect notifiable viral diseases as effectively as possible at an early stage. In addition, research is conducted into these viral diseases to develop expertise to advise the government on the prevention and control of animal disease outbreaks.WBVR also collaborates with various clients to develop new vaccines and study their efficacy. Within the One Health Virology team, we are looking for a flexible researcher with a Bachelor's degree to work on this.
An important part of the work involves setting up, adapting, validating, and accrediting diagnostic tests (particularly PCR, sequencing, ELISA, and VNT). In addition, you are involved - especially during the critical period of an outbreak - in the further characterization of detected viruses (PCRs, whole-genome sequencing) and database management. If the situation requires it, you also contribute to the rapid development of new diagnostic tests. Furthermore, you work on (molecular) virological research projects aimed at developing and testing new vaccines and combating various viral diseases. For these tasks, experience with virological, immunological, and molecular techniques is important, alongside quality awareness and communication skills.
 Your duties and responsibilities include: 
 performing, setting up, validating, and accrediting diagnostic tests for notifiable animal diseases such as foot-and-mouth disease and bluetongue;
 contributing ideas for improving diagnostics and setting up new techniques;
 conducting research projects. These may include molecular virological studies into new vaccines, as well as studies to test the efficacy of new vaccines.
 Your team 
You will be working alongside your colleagues in the One Health Virology department at Wageningen Bioveterinary Research (WBVR) in Lelystad.
 You will work here 
 Wageningen Bioveterinary Research (WBVR) is a leading research institute in the field of animal health, and public health. Its unique selling point lies in its interdisciplinary approach to research and its focus on innovative solutions for complex problems in these fields.
WBVR has a unique position in the Netherlands, as it is the only research institute that is allowed to work with the most animal viruses and bacteria up to level vBSL4 (vDM4), such as foot-and-mouth disease and African swine fever in laboratories and animal facilities, were large livestock animals (o.a. cattle) and smaller rodents can be housed. Also, facilities are in place to do research and animal experiments for BLS3 pathogens such as avian influenza and Coxiella. Different experts on specific pathogens, host responses, bioinformatics, pathology, epidemiology and diagnostics allows WBVR to work on the mission and vision of WBVR.
WBVR contributes to a society where animals and humans live a healthy life by scientific research to prevent the spread of animal diseases and promote health.
WBVR adds value to the agricultural and life sciences value chains by conducting contract research, R&D, and statutory research tasks. We serve the interests of the Dutch agro-food sector, (veterinary) public health, and the life sciences & health sectors. As contract-research organization we focus on market needs in the animal and human life sciences sectors.
WBVR has 3 focus points, healthy livestock, one health and high tech animal models (including the 3R’s).

REQUIREMENTS:
You possess: 
 a Bachelor's degree in Life Sciences, such as Biology and Medical Laboratory Research (HLO program);
 knowledge of and experience with performing (molecular) virological and immunological techniques and ensuring the quality of tests;
 affinity with laboratory diagnostics and quality matters (ISO 17025);
 you are proactive, work accurately, think analytically, and can organize your work well;
 you value good teamwork;
 you have a good command of the Dutch language, both spoken and written The work will largely take place in buildings subject to quarantine restrictions based on EU regulations upon departure.

academictransfer:364257.description:
The immune system plays a central role in protecting the body against pathogens and detecting and eliminating abnormal cells, including cancer cells. Dysregulation of the immune system can lead to a wide range of autoimmune, inflammatory and immunodeficiency disorders.
Lymph nodes are key organs of the immune system. They play a crucial role in immune cell activation and the initiation of adaptive immune responses. Despite their importance, many of the cellular and molecular processes that govern lymph node function remain poorly understood.
As a postdoc in computational immunology, you will develop a mechanistic, spatio-temporal multiscale computational model of the lymph node. You will integrate agent-based modelling with differential equation-based approaches to better understand immune responses.
This is a two-year postdoctoral position. You will have the opportunity to contribute to the development of this research line and use computational modelling to address fundamental questions in immunology.
You will develop a mechanistic multiscale model of the lymph node, with a focus on understanding adaptive immune responses. You will work closely with principal investigators and fellow researchers at Amsterdam UMC and other institutes. You will also present and discuss your results in team meetings.
Your tasks include:
 Developing an initial model in the Julia programming language, focusing on T-cell activation at the cellular and molecular level, including cell motility and cell-cell interactions, gene regulatory and signalling networks, and chemokine gradients.
 Extending the model to include additional lymph node compartments or processes, such as the B-cell region and germinal centre dynamics, or stromal and fibroblast populations.
 Using single-cell omics and other datasets from public repositories and collaborators to define and parameterize the model.
 Ensuring that the model is well documented and accessible to other researchers by using our ENCORE framework .
 Contributing to teaching at Amsterdam UMC or the University of Amsterdam and writing a grant proposal to attract research funding and establish your own research line.

REQUIREMENTS:
You are a computational scientist with a strong interest in biology, immunology and single-cell omics. You combine technical expertise with analytical thinking and clear communication. You are an ambitious researcher who enjoys working in an interdisciplinary environment and taking the lead in developing a research project.
You bring:
 A PhD in computational science or a related field and experience in a previous postdoctoral research position.
 Experience with agent-based modelling and differential equations.
 Strong programming skills in Julia or Python and experience with tools such as Git, Visual Studio Code and CoPilot or Claude Code.
 Strong communication, presentation and scientific writing skills, with the ability to work independently and collaboratively.
 A good command of English, both spoken and written.
Knowledge or experience with R, immunology and single-cell omics is an advantage.

What if a simulation did not just approximate physical laws, but obeyed them exactly? Join us to design structure-preserving fast FEM solvers for time-dependent PDEs, from fluids to electromagnetics. 
 Job description 
The Numerical Analysis group within the Delft Institute of Applied Mathematics at TU Delft (see link) is offering a full-time PhD position in the area of efficient structure preserving finite element methods for time-dependent PDEs.
Time-dependent PDEs are ubiquitous in science and engineering, governing the behaviour of fluids, electromagnetics, and many other physical systems. Numerical discretization techniques are fundamental to obtaining (approximate) solutions of these PDEs. Better approximations are typically achieved by refining the mesh and time steps, and/or increasing the order of the methods (e.g. increasing the degree of basis functions in finite elements), leading to larger systems that are computationally more expensive to solve. For this reason, numerical methods that can produce a more accurate solution with the same mesh, time step, and order are advantageous. One approach to constructing more accurate numerical methods is to design them such that key properties of the PDEs are exactly preserved, instead of only approximated: for example, conservation of energy, mass, and momentum; symplecticity; or preservation of the underlying de Rham complex structure. This class of numerical methods is called structure-preserving discretization, and is the main topic of this project. Specifically, this project will focus on both the construction of structure-preserving discretizations for time-dependent PDEs and the efficient solution of the resulting systems with iterative solvers for large-scale systems and HPC. The ultimate aim is to develop solvers that have strong theoretical foundations and are practically viable for real-world applications.
The PhD will be supervised by Artur Palha in the Numerical Analysis group at TU Delft. The group is internationally recognized for its contributions to structure-preserving finite element methods, iterative methods, and parallel computing.
Besides carrying out mathematical research and preparing scientific publications, you will be expected to actively participate in seminars and discussions within the department, as well as present your work at (inter)national conferences and workshops. You will also carry out minor teaching tasks (at most 15% of your time). Teaching and communication will be in English. If desired, you can take Dutch language courses offered by the TU Delft Language Center.
 Job Requirements 
 Strong Background: You hold a Master’s degree (MSc) in Applied Mathematics, Computational Science, Physics, Aerospace Engineering, or a closely related field. You have a solid foundation in numerical analysis, partial differential equations, and numerical linear algebra.
 Theoretical and Practical Balance: You enjoy developing and analyzing mathematical theory, but also have the skills and motivation to implement algorithms and test them in practice.
 Programming Skills: You are proficient in at least one scientific programming language (such as Python, Julia, C++, or MATLAB) and are motivated to work with parallel computing environments.
 Collaborative Communicator: You are able to communicate your ideas clearly and work effectively with a diverse set of researchers and stakeholders, both within mathematics and in application domains.
 Curious and Open-Minded: You are eager to explore connections between mathematics, physics, and computing, and motivated to learn new techniques.
 Internship Experience: An internship or collaboration in or outside academia is a plus, but not required.
 Inclusive Outlook: We welcome applications from researchers who will add to the diversity of our team, in the broad and intersectional sense of the word.

PhD-position Clinical study on bacteria-targeted tracers for detection of infections
Location: University Medical Center Groningen (UMCG), Department of Trauma Surgery, Nuclear Medicine and Molecular imaging, and Microbiology 
Are you passionate about healthcare, medical technology, innovation, infection research, and surgery? Would you like to contribute to the development of novel diagnostic approaches that improve patient care? Then this PhD position could be the perfect opportunity for you. For an interdisciplinary collaboration between the Departments of Nuclear Medicine, Medical Microbiology, and Trauma Surgery, we are looking for a motivated and ambitious PhD candidate to coordinate and conduct clinical studies on bacteria-targeted fluorescence and PET imaging of infections . In this project, you will contribute to the development, implementation, and clinical evaluation of novel bacteria-targeted fluorescent and PET tracers for the detection of infections, with a particular focus on patients with severe traumatic injuries. If you are excited about translating innovative imaging technologies into clinical practice and working within a multidisciplinary research team, we encourage you to apply and join our team.
 Project description 
Bacterial infections are a common and growing challenge across many medical specialties. Their incidence is increasing due to an ageing population, the widespread use of implanted medical devices, and the emergence of antibiotic-resistant bacteria. Early and accurate diagnosis is crucial for timely treatment and to prevent irreversible tissue damage. However, existing imaging techniques have limited specificity and often cannot reliably distinguish bacterial infection from sterile inflammation caused by trauma, fracture healing, or recent surgery. To address this challenge, our multidisciplinary team has developed a new generation of bacteria-targeted imaging tracers based on antibiotics labeled with either a near-infrared fluorescent dye or a PET radionuclide. These tracers have been evaluated in preclinical studies and are currently being prepared for clinical translation under Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) conditions. By specifically targeting bacteria, they enable accurate detection of infections and offer the unique opportunity to visualize infected tissue both non-invasively and in real time during surgery. Supported by the HTRIC and Ubbo Emmius Fund, this project aims to translate these innovative bacteria-targeted imaging agents into clinical practice by evaluating their application for fluorescence-guided detection of bacterial infections during surgery.
Your responsibilities will include: 
- Coordinating and carrying out a scientific research project.
- Actively participating in multidisciplinary meetings and project teams.
- Perform clinical studies on new bacteria-targeted tracers for infection detection (both fluorescent and PET).

REQUIREMENTS:
- MSc in medicine, biomedical engineering, (micro)biology, biotechnology 
- Good oral and written command of English.
- Good communication skills, especially for interdisciplinary collaborations
- Experience with imaging tracers (optical camera’s), near-infrared fluorescence imaging, PET imaging, and conducting clinical studies is regarded a preference.
In addition, it is beneficial if you have experience with scientific research and have written scientific articles.

To delineate the effects of genetic and environmental factors on CeD onset and progression that we have prioritized in our current research lines, we wish to expand on our current model systems to make them more physiologically relevant by including mucosal immunological or microbiome components. We envision that these patient-derived models will inform on the disease-specific barrier function and interactions with intestinal lymphocytes, and the viral or bacterial involvement in disease pathways. Moreover, we have experience with and want to expand on our expertise with CRISPR/Cas9 genetic engineering of genes of interest in our ASC and/or iPSC-derived organoid and intestine-on-chip models, as well as in intestinal tissue-resident lymphocytes. The read-outs will largely be Next Generation Sequencing-based to reveal unbiasedly the consequences of the genetic, immunological or microbial interventions that will be tested as part of the Immunogenetics lab research lines. Because CeD genetics and immunology overlap with that of other complex immune mediated diseases such as inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), multiple sclerosis (MS), and rheumatoid arthritis (RA), our research is of interest for the broader scientific community and pharmaceutical industry.
The Immunogenetics team is looking for two highly motivated colleagues interested in studying the role of genetic, immunologic, and environmental factors on immune-mediated disease in general, and especially in celiac disease (CeD).

Human interventions and climate change are exerting increasing pressure on estuarine systems, profoundly altering their dynamics and often leading to negative consequences such as reduced flood safety, ecosystem degradation, and declining water quality. Given the growing challenges faced by these environments, there is an urgent need to improve our understanding of the physical, ecological, and biogeochemical processes that govern their behaviour. 
 Job description 
The PhD candidate will develop and analyse new process-based mathematical models to improve our understanding and predictive capability of sediment dynamics in hyperturbid estuaries. These systems are characterized by extremely high suspended sediment concentrations, strong interactions between flow and sediment transport, and the formation of fluid mud layers, making them among the most challenging coastal environments to model.
The research will focus on the fundamental question of how hydrodynamics, turbulence, sediment transport, and sediment trapping interact under highly turbid conditions. Existing idealized estuarine models do not adequately capture these feedback mechanisms, particularly when sediment concentrations become sufficiently high to influence turbulence and, consequently, the flow itself. The PhD candidate will therefore extend an existing two-dimensional vertical (2DV) estuarine model by developing and implementing novel turbulence closures that explicitly account for the mutual interactions between turbulence and sediment dynamics.
Using a combination of analytical techniques, asymptotic methods, and numerical simulations, the candidate will investigate the emergence of turbidity maxima, the formation of fluid mud layers, and the mechanisms governing sediment retention in estuaries. Particular attention will be paid to identifying the dominant physical processes and determining how system behaviour changes under varying forcing conditions and parameter regimes. Model results will be evaluated against observations from several European estuaries, thereby linking fundamental theory to real-world applications.
In the second phase of the project, the research will advance beyond the traditional 2DV framework by incorporating lateral variability. This will result in a more comprehensive description of estuarine dynamics and enable the investigation of questions that cannot be addressed with width-averaged models. Specifically, the candidate will quantify the role of lateral circulation, channel-shoal interactions, and cross-estuary sediment transport in controlling the location and strength of estuarine turbidity maxima and the occurrence of fluid mud.
The project combines mathematical model development, nonlinear dynamical systems analysis, turbulence modelling, and environmental fluid mechanics. The successful candidate will contribute to the development of new theoretical understanding of sediment-rich estuarine systems and will collaborate closely with other PhD candidates and postdoctoral researchers within the iMose project. Strong interactions with knowledge institutes, including Deltares, will ensure that the research remains connected to contemporary scientific and societal challenges related to estuarine management and climate adaptation.
 Job requirements 
A Master's degree in (Applied) Mathematics, Applied Physics, or a related discipline is required. Candidates should have demonstrated expertise in the development of mathematical models for geophysical flows and turbulence, employing both analytical and numerical techniques.
We seek a researcher with a critical and inquisitive mindset, capable of rigorously evaluating results and translating findings into new and relevant research questions. The ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team is essential.
Strong communication skills are required, including fluency in English, both written and spoken. A willingness to learn the Dutch language is expected.

academictransfer:364337.description:
Are you interested in spatial ecology, species distributions, and plant functional traits? Do you want to contribute to understanding global patterns of plant diversity, and plant responses to environmental change? 
Conserving biodiversity in a rapidly changing world requires understanding why some species occupy vast geographic ranges while others remain restricted to small areas. Traditionally, efforts to answer this question have focused on understanding and predicting the distributions of individual species. However, recent advances in biodiversity and trait datasets have expanded our capacity to incorporate the functional characteristics of species, allowing us to go beyond the species concept and better capture the variation in biota using functional traits across different levels of biological organisation.
This PhD position explores how functional traits influence global patterns of plant biodiversity and plant responses to environmental change. The project focuses on three different levels of organisation, ranging from broad functional forms that capture major ecological plant strategies (e.g. tree, epiphyte, shrub), to finer levels of organisation among species (inter-specific variation) and within species (intra-specific variation). As a PhD candidate, you will make use of large trait databases like TRY and BIEN, and be responsible for setting up a greenhouse experiment similar to that of a provenance trial set-up (i.e. growing seeds collected from across a species’ native geographic range under varying environmental conditions). Specifically, your duties and responsibilities include:
 Collating plant distributions, functional traits, and environmental data from various sources
 Setting-up and conducting a greenhouse experiment to assess variation in plant phenotypic plasticity under simulated environmental conditions
 Publishing your research in peer-reviewed journals and presenting your research at (inter)national conferences
 Mentoring BSc/MSc students
 You will work here 
The research is embedded within the Plant Ecology and Nature Conservation group , which is led by Prof. David Kleijn. You will be supervised by Dr. Coline Boonman and Dr. Amanda Taylor. Prof. David Kleijn is the promotor.

REQUIREMENTS:
You have the following personal competencies and skills:
 A successfully completed MSc degree in ecology, environmental sciences or a related field
 Experience handling large biodiversity datasets and environmental data
 Highly proficient in data analysis in R and strong quantitative and statistical expertise
 Excellent oral and written communication skills in English
 The ability to work independently and collaboratively
For this position your command of the English language is expected to be at C1 level . Sometimes it is necessary to submit an internationally recognised Certificate of Proficiency in the English Language. More information can be found here .

CONTRACT: 18 months

The Faculty of Science and the Leiden Academic Centre for Drug Research (LACDR) are looking for a: 
 PhD candidate for the project “Modulation of inflammatory Dendritic cell subsets in atherosclerosis” 
Atherosclerosis is a chronic inflammatory disease where atherosclerotic plaques develop in the larger arteries. Atherosclerosis is the underlying pathology of cardiovascular disease events such as myocardial infarction or stroke. Currently, treatment focusses on lipid-lowering interventions, which do not target the chronic inflammation that causes plaque instability and major acute cardiovascular events. Therefore, studying the immune cells that contribute to atherosclerotic plaque destabilization may lead to novel therapeutic targets and intervention strategies.
In this project, we aim to investigate how inflammatory myeloid cell populations, with a focus on dendritic cell subsets contribute to the progression of atherosclerosis. Dendritic cells act as directors of the immune response by activating T cells and may thus fuel the ongoing chronic inflammatory response in advanced atherosclerosis. We aim to investigate novel mechanisms and identify new targets for more targeted therapeutic intervention.
 What you will do 
The aim of your PhD project is to obtain novel knowledge regarding myeloid immune cells in cardiovascular disease, specifically in advanced atherosclerosis.
You will:
1) identify myeloid cell subsets, with a particular focus on dendritic cells, in advanced human atherosclerosis and associate these with patient characteristics
2) investigate the functional changes of different dendritic cell subsets in advanced atherosclerosis
3) identify proatherogenic dendritic cell subsets and validate potential therapeutic targets for intervention.
You will make use of available human atherosclerotic tissue and datasets, design and perform in vitro studies and validate findings in vivo .

 English proficiency (verbally and written),

The Faculty of Science at Leiden University is a world-class faculty where staff and students work together in a dynamic international environment. The research activities are organized in eight institutes. These institutes offer eight bachelors’ and twelve master’s programmes. The faculty has grown strongly in recent years and now has more than 2,700 staff and over 6,000 students. We are located at the heart of Leiden’s Bio Science Park, one of Europe’s biggest science parks, where university and business life come together.
The division of BioTherapeutics operates at the forefront of research in the field of therapeutic modulation of cardiovascular disease. The research aims to identify new immune targets in atherosclerosis and to develop innovative biopharmaceutical concepts to intervene in cardiovascular disease. The use of specific gene-knockout technology, biologics such as vaccines, therapeutic proteins and cellular therapy, provides a unique approach for the development of new therapies for the treatment or prevention of atherosclerosis. For more information, see https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/science/drug-research/biotherapeutics.

We offer a full-time appointment of initially one year. Are you a highly motivated and enthusiastic ecologist who wants to uncover how nitrogen deposition affects plant and arthropod biodiversity? Are you excited by the idea of combining large-scale fieldwork across Northwestern Europe with hands-on experiments to answer a question that matters for biodiversity conservation? If so, this PhD-position could be the perfect fit for you! 
Human-driven nitrogen (N) deposition is changing ecosystems worldwide. It can cause an oversupply of nitrogen in the soil and soil acidification, and shift the balance of nutrients; not just how many nutrients are available, but also the ratios between them (their ‘stoichiometry’). This changes which plants thrive, and it changes the nutritional quality of the leaves and pollen that herbivorous and pollinating insects consume. However, we still poorly understand how these changes unfold within and among plant species, or how they cascade to affect insect performance and, ultimately, insect community diversity. As a PhD candidate, you will contribute to finding this out. You will combine field studies in Northwestern European forests across a N-deposition gradient spanning the Netherlands, Germany, Denmark and Sweden with greenhouse and controlled feeding experiments on caterpillars and solitary bees.
 Your duties and responsibilities include: 
 Design and conduct field studies across Northwestern Europe to assess how large- and small-scale gradients in N deposition affect soil chemistry, plant stoichiometry, and plant and arthropod diversity
 Perform experiments to find out how nutrient concentrations in plant leaves and pollen affect the performance and food preferences of insect herbivore and pollinator species
 Analyse complex ecological datasets, linking soil, plant and insect variables
 Co-supervise MSc students conducting thesis research within the project
 Publish your results in a PhD thesis, as well as in peer-reviewed papers
 You will work here 
The research is embedded within the Plant Ecology and Nature Conservation (PEN) group at Wageningen University, which is led by Prof. David Kleijn. Daily supervision will be by Dr. Philippine Vergeer, Dr. Jeroen Scheper, Dr. Fons van der Plas (all PEN) and Dr. Wim Ozinga (Vegetation and Landscape Ecology, Wageningen Environmental Research).

REQUIREMENTS:
You are a team player with strong motivation for ecological (field) studies, you like to analyze complex data sets, and have a critical, curious approach to research. You are keen to publish your findings in leading international academic journals, to communicate your findings to a wide audience, and you enjoy co-supervising MSc students doing thesis research within the framework of the project.
 You also possess: 
 An MSc in ecology, environmental sciences or a related field;
 Experience with ecological field studies (e.g., soil sampling, vegetation surveys, arthropod sampling and identification);
 Advanced skills in data analysis in R;
 Excellent written and spoken English;
 A driver's license;
For this position your command of the English language is expected to be at C1 level . Sometimes it is necessary to submit an internationally recognised Certificate of Proficiency in the English Language. More information can be found here .

Als Marien Ecoloog met affiniteit voor Deltagebieden bij Wageningen Marine Research (WMR) in Yerseke draag je actief bij aan het herstel en verbetering van de unieke natuur in de Deltawateren. Met innovatieve, duurzame oplossingen vanuit het gedachtegoed van ‘bouwen met de natuur’ vertaal je wetenschap naar praktische toepassingen met zichtbare impact.
De Zuidwestelijke Delta staat voor grote ecologische uitdagingen én kansen. Van de zandhonger in de Oosterschelde tot natuurontwikkeling in de Westerschelde en het verbeteren van de waterkwaliteit zoals in het Grevelingenmeer en Veerse Meer: jij levert een belangrijke bijdrage aan oplossingen die het verschil maken voor natuur en samenleving.
Samen met andere experts op het gebied van mariene ecologie werk je aan uiteenlopende deltavraagstukken. Je onderzoekt waar natuurontwikkeling en “nature-based solutions” voor onder andere hoogwaterbescherming en waterkwaliteit kunnen worden toegepast en weet opdrachtgevers overtuigend mee te nemen in de meerwaarde van deze duurzame aanpak. Daarnaast draag je bij aan de wetenschappelijke onderbouwing van het Natuurherstelplan en de beheerplannen voor Natura 2000-gebieden in de Zuidwestelijke Delta. Contact met opdrachtgevers en stakeholders is een integraal onderdeel van je werk.
 Jouw taken en verantwoordelijkheden als Marien Ecoloog zijn: 
 bijdragen aan een breed scala aan literatuuronderzoeken, gegevensanalyses, veld- en labexperimenten op het gebied van natuurontwikkeling en bodemdieronderzoek;
 assisteren met de verwerving van nieuwe projecten en het schrijven van onderzoeksvoorstellen
 communiceren met collega-onderzoekers en opdrachtgevers;
 het rapporteren en presenteren van onderzoeksresultaten aan opdrachtgevers, het bijwonen van conferenties en het deelnemen aan workshops;
 publiceren en presenteren van eigen onderzoek in wetenschappelijke tijdschriften en op conferenties.
 Jouw team 
Vanuit de WMR-locatie in Yerseke werk je samen binnen diverse projectteams van verschillende samenstellingen. Als projectleider geef je inhoudelijke én organisatorische sturing aan mede onderzoekers, zodat projecten efficiënt, zorgvuldig en succesvol kunnen worden uitgevoerd. In de rol van projectmedewerker lever je een inhoudelijke bijdrage aan specifieke onderdelen van projecten, passend bij jouw expertise en interesses.
 Hier ga je werken 
 Wageningen Marine Research (WMR) is één van de negen instituten die onderdeel uitmaakt van Wageningen Research. WMR is een toonaangevend, onafhankelijk onderzoeksinstituut met locaties in Yerseke, IJmuiden en Den Helder dat zich richt op strategisch en toegepast marien ecologisch onderzoek. Producten en diensten worden projectmatig uitgevoerd en zijn divers van aard: veldonderzoek, experimenten op realistische schaal, verkennende studies op laboratoriumschaal, datamanagement en modellering. academictransfer:364391.description:
We are seeking a highly motivated and talented individual to work as a doctoral candidate on the MSCA-DN DETECTIVE project.
For rapid control of virus outbreaks, fast availability of antivirals is a major bottleneck. In DETECTIVE, innovative models will be used for setting up an antiviral testing pipeline without the need for animals models.
This doctoral project will focus on developing patient-derived organotypic models to test and optimise broad-spectrum antiviral therapies. Organotypic models, such as human organoids, are miniaturised in vitro organ cultures that mimic the human tissue-specific context. In this project, gut organoid models co-cultured with immune cells will be used to determine antiviral efficacy of available broadly acting antiviral against a scala of outbreak viruses such as enteroviruses and West-Nile virus.
Patient-specific responses to virus infections will be assessed with integrated -omics techniques, and patient-dependent responses to antiviral therapy will be used to develop personalized medicine regimens for the future. With this project we will set the stage for an innovative human antiviral testing pipeline for viral outbreaks.
At the Amsterdam UMC, DETECTIVE is looking for a doctoral candidate (DC) to work on Work Package 1. As DC6, your objectives are:
 To establish patient-derived gut organoid mucosa models
 To test a panel of broadly acting antiviral compounds in patient-derived gut mucosa organoid models
 To identify virus and host factors determining treatment response by transcriptomics and proteomics
You will be supervised by:
 Dr. Katja Wolthers
 Dr. Adithya Sridhar
You will undertake international secondments within the DETECTIVE network, including:
 the Dutch Public Health Institute (Utrecht, Netherlands)
 the University of Tampere (Tampere, Finland)
These secondments will provide exposure to both academic and industrial research environments and offer opportunities to develop complementary scientific and transferable skills.

REQUIREMENTS:
master’s degree in biomedical sciences, infection, immunity or related fields;
 experience working with mammalian cell culture, qPCR, and bioinformatics is preferred;
 experience working with stem cells and organoids is desirable;
 excellent oral and written communication skills in English (minimum C1/C2 CEFR level);
 an interest in self-development and working in a multidisciplinary research environment.

 Applicants must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the Netherlands for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately preceding recruitment (1 March 2027).

 Applicants must not hold a doctoral degree at the time of recruitment.

academictransfer:364392.description:
Job description 
Within the Thrombosis and Hemostasis research group of the Laboratory of Hematology, we investigate the mechanisms that maintain the delicate balance of the hemostatic system. Disruption of this balance may result in either bleeding or thrombosis, both of which represent major causes of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Bleeding following trauma remains one of the leading causes of death in individuals under the age of 46 years, while thrombotic diseases are among the most common causes of mortality globally, with incidence increasing with age.
Identifying the cause of a bleeding tendency remains a major challenge in clinical hematology. Despite extensive laboratory and genetic investigations, no underlying hemostatic defect can currently be identified in approximately 50% of these patients. This may be further improved by evaluating clot degradation (fibrinolysis). However, assays assessing fibrinolytic capacity are poorly standardized and are not routinely available in clinical practice.
In this PhD project, you will contribute to advancing our understanding of unexplained bleeding disorders through a combination of genomic analysis, functional characterisation and translational research approaches. The project aims to identify and characterize novel genetic variants and biological mechanisms underlying bleeding phenotypes by integrating whole-genome sequencing with functional studies in individual patients and affected families.
In parallel, the project focuses on improving diagnostic strategies for fibrinolytic disorders by characterizing current diagnostic modalities and by developing, optimizing, and validating novel assays that assess fibrinolytic potential. Together, these approaches will provide novel insights into the pathophysiology of bleeding disorders and ultimately contribute to improved diagnostic evaluation and personalized patient care.
Tasks and responsibilities as PhD researcher:
Analysis of genetic data
Functional analysis of identified proteins
Conducting systematic searches in literature databases
Validation of laboratory tests
Writing scientific publications for international journals.
Presenting results at (scientific) meetings
Collaborating with promoters, supervisors and internal and external partners
All these tasks are aimed at obtaining an academic PhD. In addition, PhD students contribute to general activities taking place within the laboratory of hematology and within the research institute.

REQUIREMENTS:
Profile 
You are an aspiring PhD candidate with a keen interest in hemostasis as one of the leading causes for morbidity and mortality. You have the ambition to unravel novel fundamental biological mechanisms, and develop opportunities to improve patient care.
You are proactive in your efforts to approach this research project from multiple angles, and you have excellent communication skills to establish (novel) cooperations as well as eminent writing skills to communicate your findings with the (academic) society.
You have:
 Finished a master in Biochemistry, Molecular Biology, Molecular Life Sciences, Biomedical Sciences or a related master.
 Experience in molecular biology, pathobiology, analytical chemistry, bioinformatics.
 Languages: fluent in English.

CONTRACT: 4 years

academictransfer:364394.description:
Help pave the future for living sensing systems by decoding microorganisms' encoding of environmental history. 
 Job description 
Background:
Living microorganisms could transform how we sense and store information, replacing single-use electronics with inherently biodegradable systems that track environmental conditions over time. Even basic electronic sensing systems today require sensors, microcontrollers, memory, and batteries, and are often disposable. For example, temperature and humidity dataloggers used during food and vaccine transport become e-waste within weeks. Meanwhile, many species of microorganisms, such as the iridescent Flavobacteria, integrate environmental signals and store history structurally, all with minimal energy. Readout may be as simple as taking a photograph. Could these organisms replace conventional electronics and enable fully degradable, battery-less dataloggers? What's missing in realizing this future is our ability to interpret this biological record: we do not yet understand what the visual characteristics of organisms represent quantitatively, or how reliably we can recover that information.
This PhD:
We are seeking a highly motivated PhD student to play a formative role in understanding how to decode environmental information from living microorganisms, in pursuit of living sensing and memory systems. This effort is truly trans-disciplinary, drawing on biodesign/biotechnology, machine learning, and interaction design. This project builds on groundwork already underway in our group but is meant to be shaped substantially by the candidate's own interests and expertise.
The candidate will cultivate the living organism itself, characterize and model its visible responses to different environmental conditions, and develop and validate computational decoders that recover environmental history from an image of the living organism. Based on the found capabilities, the candidate will also design prototypes that incorporate living sensors, such as fully compostable, smart packaging for temperature and humidity monitoring for food, vaccines, or archival documents.
The PhD candidate will be situated at the intersection of the Knowledge and Intelligent Design group and the Materializing Futures group in Sustainable Design Engineering (SDE), a department within the Faculty of Industrial Design Engineering.
 Job requirements 
We look for candidates who have:
 A Master's degree (or equivalent) in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Biodesign, Design Engineering, or a related field
 Experience in building and deploying machine learning or computer vision models
 Technical competencies in one or more of the following: bio-digital systems, biodesign, applied machine learning, computer vision, computational biology, and/or physical prototyping
 Experience or strong interest in biodesign and hands-on interaction with living organisms
 Experience or interest in conducting research with sound experimental design
 Ability to work in a multidisciplinary team, communicate effectively, and take initiative
 Prior publications and experience presenting at international conferences are assets but not requirements
Doing a PhD at TU Delft requires English proficiency at a certain level to ensure that the candidate is able to communicate and interact well, participate in English-taught Doctoral Education courses, and write scientific articles and a final thesis. For more details please check the Graduate Schools Admission Requirements .
 TU Delft (Delft University of Technology) 
Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference.
For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future.
At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward.

Delft designers act as a bridge between advances in technology and the needs of people, organisations and society to create products, services and systems with purpose.

academictransfer:364430.description:
De directeur bedrijfsvoering is (eind)verantwoordelijk voor een effectieve inrichting, uitvoering en borging van de facultaire bedrijfsprocessen en heeft in dit kader een sleutelpositie richting alle organisatieonderdelen binnen de faculteit. De directeur is daarbij in het bijzonder ook verantwoordelijk voor de algehele veiligheid binnen de faculteit. Zie voor de volledige profielschets: www.merwedeexecutivesearch.nl/vacatures 
 DE FUNCTIE EN ROLLEN 
Lid faculteitsbestuur
De directeur bedrijfsvoering is lid van het faculteitsbestuur en geeft samen met de decaan en de andere bestuursleden richting aan de strategische agenda van de faculteit, in afstemming met de facultaire medezeggenschap. Als directeur bedrijfsvoering breng je hierbij gevraagd en ongevraagd het perspectief van de bedrijfsvoering in op de portefeuilles onderwijs, onderzoek en impact. Je vertaalt strategische keuzes naar een toekomstbestendige koers, waarbij de financiële gezondheid en een passend personeelsbeleid centrale pijlers vormen. Gevraagd wordt iemand die werkt vanuit het gezamenlijk belang en die actief bijdraagt aan de eenheid van bestuur. Je bent welkom in een team waar constructief meedenken verwacht wordt en prettig samenwerken gekoesterd wordt.
Eindverantwoordelijk leidinggevende faculteitsbureau
De directeur bedrijfsvoering is eindverantwoordelijk leidinggevende voor het faculteitsbureau, dat het faculteitsbestuur op de volgende thema’s ondersteunt: onderwijs- en onderzoeks-ondersteuning, HRM, financiën, huisvesting, facilitaire zaken, IT, communicatie & marketing en studentzaken. Het faculteitsbureau herbergt daarnaast ook een aantal specifieke organisatieonderdelen en functies.
Het faculteitsbureau wordt gevormd door het Support Office, het Technology Center, Huisvesting en QHSE (Quality, Health, Safety & Environment) en het proefdiercentrum ADLAS (Amsterdam Division for Laboratory Animal Science), een samenwerking van de VU en het Amsterdam UMC.
Je geeft leiding aan professionals en experts en je (indirecte) span of control is groot. Gevraagd wordt een directeur die optimaal ruimte geeft aan de zelfstandigheid en professionaliteit van medewerkers en vertrouwt op hun expertise, zoals dat past in een inhoudelijk gedreven omgeving van hoogopgeleide autonome professionals en wetenschappers. Je kunt delegeren en stuurt vanuit vertrouwen.
Samenwerking met centrale diensten
Vanuit de faculteiten wordt nauw samengewerkt met de centrale VU-diensten. Als directeur bedrijfsvoering bewaak je de kwaliteit van de dienstverlening en maak je heldere en resultaatgerichte afspraken met de dienstdirecteuren over het dienstverleningspakket, binnen de kaders van het universitaire beleid.
Lid vergadering Bedrijfsvoering en bijdrage aan VU-brede thema’s
Samen met de portefeuillehouder van het College van Bestuur, de dienstdirecteuren en collega-directeuren bedrijfsvoering van de andere faculteiten ben je lid van de Vergadering Bedrijfsvoering. Hierin lever je een actieve bijdrage aan VU-brede professionalisering van de bedrijfsvoering en vertegenwoordig je ook het belang en de behoeften van de Faculteit der Bètawetenschappen.
Externe samenwerkingen
De faculteit kent een groot aantal samenwerkingen met externe partijen die variëren van subsidierelaties tot samenwerkingen met publieke en private partijen. Als directeur bedrijfsvoering ben je verantwoordelijk voor het contractmanagement en gemandateerd tekengemachtigde.
 DE OPGAVEN 
De directeur bedrijfsvoering staat voor een aantal opgaven in het bijzonder, te weten: het leveren van een bijdrage aan de strategische koers, aandacht voor de huisvesting, verdere informatieborging en -ontsluiting, het verbeteren van de veiligheid van kennis en informatie, en het nauwgezet volgen van ontwikkelingen rondom generatieve AI.
 De opgaven worden nader toegelicht in de volledige profielschets. Deze is te downloaden op: www.merwedeexecutivesearch.nl/vacatures

REQUIREMENTS:
Gezocht wordt iemand die aantoonbare affiniteit heeft met een academische omgeving, waarin onderwijs en onderzoek nauw met elkaar verweven zijn, en die een beeld heeft van de complexiteit van onder meer structuur, financieringsstromen, belangen, cultuur. Je voelt je daarbij ook thuis in het tempo en de dynamiek van een overleg- en beleidsrijke universiteit zoals de VU ook wel gekenschetst wordt.
Je neemt een brede (maatschappelijke en inhoudelijke) oriëntatie mee, bent analytisch sterk en kunt helder redeneren, schakelt makkelijk tussen strategie en alles wat ad hoc voorbij komt, je staat boven de materie opereert vanuit overzicht, je stuurt op hoofdlijnen en weet wanneer het nodig is om de diepte in te gaan, je kunt omgaan met onzekerheden en besluiten nemen ook als niet álle informatie er is.
Gevraagd wordt een ervaren directeur die goede kennis van alle bedrijfsvoeringsaspecten heeft. Zo ben je onder meer financieel goed onderlegd. Je kunt (deel)begrotingen van de verschillende onderdelen binnen de faculteit tot in detail interpreteren en challengen vanuit bestuurlijk en strategisch perspectief. Je bent bekend met de verschillende financieringsstromen en bent in staat om in een omgeving van strikte wet- en regelgeving rondom financieringskaders óók een scherp oog te hebben voor het ondernemerschap van de faculteit.
Daarnaast heb je óók goede aansluiting op de cultuur en de inhoud van de bètaomgeving. Kenmerkend voor de faculteit zijn het hoge ambitieniveau en de sterke inhoudelijke drive van de medewerkers. De cultuur valt te omschrijven als rationeel en doelgericht. Medewerkers hebben een duidelijke mening en communiceren relatief direct. Je kunt je hierin verstaan, sluit aan op de drive en het ambitieniveau en bent in staat je te verplaatsen in het gezichtspunt van de ander.
Je hebt aantoonbare inhoudelijke affiniteit met de bètawetenschappen en techniek en spreekt de taal van de bètawetenschapper. Je inhoudelijke kennis geeft het begrip dat nodig is om het primaire proces in de faculteit zo optimaal mogelijk te faciliteren alsook om je rol op het vlak van bijvoorbeeld veiligheids- en risicomanagement goed invulling te kunnen geven. Het maakt je tot een gesprekspartner van waarde en geeft je gezag.
In de functie van directeur bedrijfsvoering bij de VU begeef je je in een groot en complex stakeholderveld van machten en krachten. Je weet zakelijk doelgericht en met begrip voor het perspectief van de ander mee te bewegen met je omgeving.
 DE FUNCTIE-EISEN 
 Afgeronde academische opleiding, bij voorkeur in een bèta- of technische richting;
 Ruime managementervaring (direct en indirect leidinggevend);
 Ervaring in of met de universitaire context van onderwijs, onderzoek en valorisatie;
 Goed ingevoerd op de verschillende bedrijfsvoeringsspecialismen, in het bijzonder de financiële, juridische en hr expertise;
 Je hebt een goede aansluiting op de cultuur en inhoud van de bètatechnische omgeving, verkregen door opleiding en/of werkervaring;
 Ervari

academictransfer:364436.description:
Are you fascinated by the influence of nature on our emotions and behaviour? Passionate about nature-inspired facade design and its influence on occupant comfort and wellbeing? Eager to embark on a multidisciplinary research project and collaborate with industry partners? If so, then this PhD position might be perfect for you.
 Information 
Can we reduce stress, thermal discomfort and energy consumption for cooling in homes by harnessing visual exposure to nature-inspired facade designs? Can we disentangle the beneficial effects of daylight and nature exposure through windows? How can we best navigate the trade-off between access to view and the amount and quality of daylight and nature content provided by a nature-inspired façade? These are some of the scientific challenges you will work on in this PhD project.
This PhD position is part of the wider ΝWO KIC project “Nature4Homes: Nature-driven building skin interventions for energy efficiency, occupant comfort, health, and biodiversity in dwellings”, which brings together the domains of building engineering, building physics, environmental psychology, meteorology, and thermophysiology to develop nature-driven building skin solutions that enhance occupant health and comfort while reducing cooling demand. This PhD project focuses specifically on the domains of environmental psychology, lighting research, and building physics.
You will conduct your research within the Human-Technology Interaction group (HTI) at TU/e, which has a long history in lighting research and environmental psychology, with a secondment at the Environmental & Climate Design section at Delft University of Technology (TU Delft), which has extensive expertise in building physics and indoor environmental quality.
In this PhD, you will investigate whether visual patterns from nature across different layers of the building skin (e.g., the façade itself, the view to the outside) within an occupant’s field of view can support mental wellbeing, increase acceptance, and enhance tolerance to visual and thermal discomfort indoors, particularly during periods of summer overheating. To address these questions, you will review the literature, perform experiments in virtual reality and real conditions, co-create nature-inspired façade elements, and test them in field studies. Your work would include collecting self-reported, physiological, and environmental data, and apply building simulation, computer vision, and advanced statistical methods for their analysis. The project also involves close collaboration with industry partners such as shading system manufacturers to develop nature-inspired façade interventions. These will be tested at the “Green Village” living lab housing of TU Delft. Throughout your PhD, you will be supervised by Dr. Kynthia Chamilothori (main supervisor) and Prof. Yvonne de Kort (promotor) at the Human-Technology Interaction group of the Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e), as well as Dr. Eleonora Brembilla (co-promotor) at the Environmental & Climate Design section at TU Delft. You will be based at TU/e with a secondment at TU Delft.

REQUIREMENTS:
A master’s degree (or an equivalent university degree) in environmental psychology, lighting research, architectural or building engineering, or human-technology interaction.
 Proficiency in experimental research with human participants and quantitative data analysis, along with experience or eagerness to learn building simulation, façade technologies and programming.
 A research-oriented attitude.
 Ability to work in an interdisciplinary team and interest in collaborating with industrial partners.
 Motivated to develop your teaching skills and coach students.
 Fluent in spoken and written English (C1 level).

CONTRACT: 4 years

academictransfer:364466.description:
Ben je een kwalitatief onderzoeker met een passie voor groene criminologie en victimologie en heb je ervaring met het uitvoeren van veldwerk? Ben je geïnteresseerd in het in kaart brengen van de talrijke uitdagingen rond de regulering van de visserij in Nederland vandaag de dag vanuit het perspectief van de verschillende belanghebbenden? Ben je gedreven, zelfstandig en geïnteresseerd in het uitvoeren van veldwerk en interviews in Nederland? Dan ben jij wellicht de persoon die wij zoeken.
 Het NSCR zoekt momenteel twee onderzoekers voor een groter project met de titel „Fishing in Troubled Waters“. Beide functies hebben een looptijd van vier jaar en maken deel uit van een groter onderzoeksteam. Dit project onderzoekt (illegale) visserij in Nederland vanuit verschillende perspectieven en met behulp van diverse methoden. Hieronder vind je de beschrijving van de eerste van deze onderzoeksfuncties.
 Het doel van deze functie is het onderzoeken van de relatie tussen visserij, milieuregelgeving en mariene ecosystemen in Nederland vanuit een criminologisch en victimologisch perspectief. Met behulp van voornamelijk kwalitatieve onderzoeksmethoden zal de onderzoeker nagaan hoe verschillende actoren de relatie tussen visserijpraktijken, milieuveranderingen en regelgeving interpreteren, en hoe deze perspectieven van invloed zijn op opvattingen over milieuschade, verantwoordelijkheid en mogelijke oplossingen. De onderzoeker zal interviews en veldwerk uitvoeren met vissers, wetshandhavingsinstanties, ecologen, ngo’s, beleidsmakers en andere groepen die betrokken zijn bij het bestuur, de regelgeving, het beheer en de belangenbehartiging van de visserij en mariene ecosystemen in Nederland. Dit project richt zich op vragen als: Wat houdt het beschermen en verzorgen van de Nederlandse visstand in en hoe interpreteren verschillende belanghebbenden dit en brengen ze dit in de praktijk? Wie wordt gezien als slachtoffer van milieuschade, en door wie? Wie weet wat de vispopulatie nodig heeft en wie kan er legitiem namens haar spreken?

REQUIREMENTS:
De ideale kandidaat beschikt over:
 Een doctoraat in de criminologie, sociologie, antropologie, milieukunde, sociaal-juridische wetenschappen, victimologie of een verwante discipline.
 Kennis van een of meer van de volgende onderzoeksgebieden: groene criminologie, milieubeheer, milieurechtvaardigheid, politieke ecologie, sociaal-juridische wetenschappen of aanverwante vakgebieden.
 Aantoonbare ervaring met het opzetten en uitvoeren van kwalitatief onderzoek, waaronder interviews, etnografisch veldwerk en/of participerende observatie.
 Ervaring met het gebruik van software voor kwalitatieve gegevensanalyse (bijv. NVivo, ATLAS.ti of MAXQDA).

 The goal of this role is to investigate the relationship between fishing, environmental regulation, and restoring marine ecosystems in the Netherlands from a criminological and victimological perspective. Using primarily qualitative research methods, the researcher will examine how different actors understand the relationship between fishing practices, environmental change, and regulation, and how these perspectives shape ideas about environmental harm, responsibility and possible solutions. The researcher will conduct interviews and fieldwork with various actors involved in fishing, the governance, regulation, care, and representation of fisheries and marine ecosystems in the Netherlands. Ben je geïnteresseerd in het vergroten van ons inzicht in de omvang en ontwikkelingen van illegale visserij en de visbestanden in Nederland? Ben je gedreven, zelfstandig en geïnteresseerd in het verkennen van nieuwe gegevensbronnen? Dan ben jij wellicht de persoon die wij zoeken.
 Het NSCR werft momenteel twee onderzoekers aan in het kader van een groter project getiteld „Fishing in Troubled Waters“. Beide functies hebben een looptijd van vier jaar en maken deel uit van een groter onderzoeksteam. Dit project onderzoekt (illegale) visserij in Nederland vanuit verschillende perspectieven en met behulp van diverse methoden. Hieronder vind je de beschrijving van de tweede van deze onderzoeksfuncties.
 Deze onderzoeker zal werken aan een project waarin de omvang en de gevolgen van illegale visserij in Nederland worden onderzocht vanuit een criminologisch en ecologisch perspectief. Hoewel uit eerder onderzoek blijkt dat illegale visserijpraktijken wijdverbreid zijn, is er in de Nederlandse context nog maar weinig bekend over dit fenomeen. Er bestaat geen centrale database die een overzicht biedt van de huidige stand van zaken met betrekking tot (illegale) visserij en de gevolgen daarvan voor de visbestanden in Nederland. Dit project richt zich op het verzamelen en analyseren van (secundaire) bronnen en databases over illegale visserij om beter te begrijpen hoe de huidige visserijpraktijken de ontwikkeling van de visbestanden kunnen beïnvloeden. Het project omvat daarom het verzamelen en analyseren van voornamelijk kwantitatieve gegevens over illegale visserij, de handhaving van visserijvoorschriften en ontwikkelingen in visbestanden in Nederland. Dit kan in de vorm zijn van registraties door de NVWA, politiedossiers, registraties door groene BOA’s, GPS-gegevens over scheepsbewegingen in Nederlandse wateren en registraties van visbestanden of andere beschikbare gegevensbronnen. Deze onderzoeksfunctie heeft tot doel vragen te beantwoorden zoals: Welke informatiebronnen bestaan er over illegale visserij in Nederland? Hoe wijdverbreid is illegale visserij in Nederland? Wat is het ‘dark number’ van illegale visserij in Nederland? Hoe registreert en reguleert de wetshandhaving de huidige visserijpraktijken? Hoe ontwikkelen visbestanden zich binnen het huidige regelgevingskader?

academictransfer:364470.description:
Waarom kan een snelle gezondheidstip op sociale media zo overtuigend klinken, ook als die misleidend of mogelijk zelfs schadelijk is? Sociale media staan vol met ‘health hacks’: korte, praktische adviezen die snelle verbeteringen beloven voor gezondheid, welzijn of uiterlijk. Sommige zijn onschadelijk, maar andere zijn misleidend of potentieel gevaarlijk. Denk aan extreme detox-kuren, recepten voor zelfgemaakte zonnebrandcrème of alternatieve behandelingen die worden aangeprezen als vervanging van wetenschappelijk onderbouwde zorg.
Deze promotieplaats maakt deel uit van het ‘Hooked by the Health Hack’-project, een vierjarig, door de NWO gefinancierd onderzoeksproject onder leiding van de Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam en de Erasmus Universiteit Rotterdam (https://www.nwo.nl/en/researchprogrammes/open-competition-ssh/granted-projects). Het project onderzoekt waarom deze ‘health hacks’ zo overtuigend kunnen zijn. Daarbij staat de wisselwerking centraal tussen individuele kenmerken, kenmerken van de online context en cognitieve processen tijdens de blootstelling.
Het project richt zich op jongvolwassenen (18-25). Deze levensfase wordt gekenmerkt door toenemende zelfstandigheid, identiteitsverkenning en groeiende verantwoordelijkheid voor gezondheidsgerelateerde keuzes. Juist omdat gezondheidsopvattingen, routines en zelfbeelden actief worden gevormd tijdens deze levensfase, is deze groep bijzonder relevant voor onderzoek naar de aantrekkingskracht en mogelijke gevolgen van deze online ‘health hacks’.
Het interdisciplinaire project verbindt communicatiewetenschap, gezondheidspsychologie en gedrags- en cognitiewetenschap in een geïntegreerd ‘mixed-methods’ design. Het project levert kennis op die kan helpen bij het ontwikkelen van strategieën die jongvolwassenen weerbaarder maken tegen misleidend en mogelijk schadelijk gezondheidsadvies op sociale media. Deze strategieën zijn erop gericht om jongvolwassenen te ondersteunen bij het kritisch beoordelen van informatie, terwijl hun zelfstandigheid en keuzevrijheid in het nemen van gezondheidsbeslissingen gerespecteerd blijven.
De twee promotietrajecten (Traject A: participatief onderzoek en Traject B: enquête- en experimenteel onderzoek) doorlopen beiden drie fasen: het identificeren van belangrijke individuele en contextuele factoren, het onderzoeken van de cognitieve processen die beoordelingen tijdens blootstelling beïnvloeden, en het vertalen van deze inzichten naar interventiestrategieën. Elk traject heeft zijn eigen methodologische focus, terwijl beide promovendi samenwerken om een gezamenlijk conceptueel model te ontwikkelen en gezamenlijk interventies te ontwerpen.
 Functieomschrijving 
Ben je geïnteresseerd in de vraag waarom jongvolwassenen zich aangetrokken voelen tot snel gezondheidsadvies op sociale media, hoe ze de informatie die ze online tegenkomen beoordelen, en hoe we hen kunnen helpen hun weg te vinden in mogelijk misleidende informatie? Dan is dit promotieproject wellicht iets voor jou.
Het PhD traject Begrijpen van ‘health hacks’: Een participatief onderzoek naar snel gezondheidsadvies in dagelijks mediagebruik (Traject A) biedt het ervaringsgerichte, praktijkgerichte perspectief binnen het grotere project: het onderzoekt hoe jongvolwassenen in hun dagelijkse digitale leven in aanraking komen met ‘health hacks’, deze interpreteren en ermee omgaan. Je maakt gebruik van een participatieve onderzoeksbenadering en werkt samen met sociale media-gebruikers in de leeftijd van 18–25 jaar als medeonderzoekers in plaats van als passieve onderzoeksparticipanten.
Je werkzaamheden omvatten:
 Het uitvoeren van een multimodale inhoudsanalyse van gevaarlijke online ‘health hacks’
 Het ontwerpen en begeleiden van participatieve workshops met jongvolwassen gebruikers van sociale media en ‘content creators’
 Het gebruik van methoden als concept- en systeem-‘mapping’ om in kaart te brengen hoe dagelijkse mediapraktijken en feedbackprocessen de vatbaarheid voor ‘health hacks’ beïnvloeden
 Het gezamenlijk ontwikkelen en iteratief evalueren van gebruikersgerichte interventiestrategieën
 Het integreren van de bevindingen uit het participatieve onderzoek met de enquête en het experimentele onderzoek van Traject B
 Het publiceren van onderzoeksresultaten, het presenteren op conferenties en het bijdragen aan kennisconstructie en -uitwisseling met praktijkpartners.

REQUIREMENTS:
Je hebt:
 Een Master of Research Master in een relevant vakgebied zoals Communicatiewetenschap, (Media) Psychologie, Sociologie, Gezondheidswetenschappen, of een gerelateerde discipline binnen de sociale wetenschappen of geesteswetenschappen
 Aantoonbare affiniteit, en bij voorkeur ervaring, met participatieve en kwalitatieve onderzoeksmethoden (bijv. participatief onderzoek, focus groepen, concept en systeem ‘mapping’, co-creatie, co-design)
 Oprechte interesse in gezondheidscommunicatie, mediageletterdheid, desinformatie en de psychologische mechanismen van overtuiging, evenals de geleefde ervaringen van jongvolwassen mediagebruikers
 Sterke organisatorische en faciliterende vaardigheden: je ontwerpt en leidt participatieve workshops en co-creatiesessies met jongvolwassen mediagebruikers
 Uitstekende academische schrijf- en communicatievaardigheden in het Engels en Nederlands (C1)
 Een samenwerkingsgerichte instelling en bent bereid om nauw samen te werken met praktijkpartners en een parallel promotietraject met een andere methodologische oriëntatie, en bij te dragen aan daadwerkelijke transdisciplinaire integratie
 Een zelfstandige werkhouding en neemt verantwoordelijkheid voor een substantieel deel van een meerjarig en multidisciplinair onderzoeksproject.
