The Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience and Maastricht University Medical Center are looking for an enthusiastic and ambitious PhD student to join a collaborative translational neuroscience project investigating how the brain controls responses to threat and stress. The project is part of a new programme aimed at strengthening the connection between fundamental neuroscience and clinical psychiatry.
Maladaptive responses to threat are an important feature of psychiatric conditions such as anxiety disorders, PTSD and depression. In this project, we will identify brain regions that can regulate threat responses and investigate whether these regions can ultimately be targeted using real-time fMRI neurofeedback.
The project provides a unique opportunity to work across the boundary between fundamental systems neuroscience and human translational neuroscience.
What will you do
You will first work at the Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience (NIN) in Amsterdam, in the laboratory of Prof. Alexander Heimel. Using mouse models of innate defensive behavior, you will identify a brain region that can regulate defensive behavior. You will use state-of-the-art approaches including behavioral analysis of innate defensive responses, activity-dependent neuronal tagging using TRAP2, viral and monosynaptic rabies tracing, optogenetic manipulation of neural circuits, fiber photometry and quantitative analysis of neural and behavioral data.
In the second part of the project, you will work with Prof. David Linden and colleagues at Maastricht UMC+, translating the circuit identified in mice to humans. You will use 7T fMRI to translate the findings from the first part and develop a real-time fMRI neurofeedback paradigm through which participants learn to regulate the identified brain region.
The ultimate aim is to develop a biologically grounded approach to neurofeedback in which targets are selected because they have a demonstrated causal role in controlling threat circuitry. The work may provide a foundation for future neurofeedback interventions in patients with stress-related psychiatric disorders.
What will you contribute
We are looking for a candidate who:
•    has, or will soon obtain, a master's degree in neuroscience, biomedical sciences, medicine, psychology, cognitive neuroscience, or a related discipline
•    has a strong interest in how neural circuits generate behavior
•    is enthusiastic about working at the interface between animal and human neuroscience
•    is interested in learning a broad range of experimental and computational techniques
•    enjoys quantitative analysis and has or is willing to develop data-analysis skills
•    wants to interact with psychiatrists and clinical psychologists to develop new paradigms
•    has good communication skills and enjoys working collaboratively
•    has a good command of spoken and written English
Experience with animal behavior, optogenetics, viral approaches, microscopy, programming/data analysis, MRI or human experimental research would be an advantage, but we do not expect applicants to already have expertise in all these areas. More important is a strong scientific curiosity and willingness to learn techniques from both animal systems neuroscience and human neuroimaging.
Because part of the project involves experimental work with mice, the candidate should be comfortable working with laboratory animals.
What we offer
You will join two complementary and highly interactive research environments. At the Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience, you will receive training in causal circuit neuroscience and the neural mechanisms underlying innate behavior. At Maastricht UMC+, you will gain expertise in human neuroimaging, high-field 7T MRI and real-time neurofeedback within a clinical neuroscience environment. The project includes regular interaction with both research groups and joint supervision throughout the PhD.
The project is funded for four years. The first two years will primarily focus on circuit discovery and causal experiments in mice, followed by human circuit validation and neurofeedback experiments during years three and four. Some travel or/and movement allowance is budgeted for making the collaboration between Amsterdam and Maastricht smooth.
You will have opportunities to present your work at international conferences, collaborate with researchers across neuroscience, psychiatry and neuroimaging, and develop a profile as a genuinely cross-species translational neuroscientist.
Research environment
The project is a collaboration between the group of Prof. Alexander Heimel at the Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience in Amsterdam and the group of Prof. David Linden at Maastricht UMC.
The Heimel group investigates the neural circuits that transform sensory information and internal state into behavior, with particular expertise in visual and innate behaviors, circuit tracing and causal manipulation in mice.
The Maastricht team has extensive expertise in fMRI neurofeedback, high-field imaging and clinical neuroscience, including subcortical neurofeedback targets. The project will also involve interaction with researchers experienced in real-time and 7T fMRI.
Information
For questions about the position, please contact Alexander Heimel (a.heimel@nin.knaw.nl) or David Linden (david.linden@maastrichtuniversity.nl). There is no deadline for the application, the vacancy will be closed if a suitable candidate has been found.
Application
You can apply via the Apply Now button, please submit:
•    A motivation letter explaining why this project interests you
•    A detailed CV, including a grade list
•    Contact details of two academic referees, who can be contacted
About the Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience
The Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience is a leading fundamental neuroscience research institute, in the international and progressive city of Amsterdam. It provides a critical mass of scientists (spanning more than 27 nationalities) and neuroscience facilities, in a highly interactive, dynamic, multi-cultural environment, with English as the working language.

Depending on education and experience the minimum salary is € 3.204 and the maximum salary is € 4.051 gross per month for a full-time appointment (scale P cao Nederlandse Universiteiten/KNAW). This is exclusive of 8% vacation allowance, 8.3% year-end bonus, travel allowance, internet allowance, home working allowance and pension accrual with ABP.
The KNAW offers its staff an excellent package of secondary benefits. A package that meets the different needs of employees depending on their stage of life, lifestyle or career ambitions. For example, by working an extra two hours a week, it is possible to increase the number of days off from 29 to 41 days a year (with full-time employment).

Diversity & Inclusion
The KNAW considers a working environment in which everyone feels welcome and appreciated of great importance. A working environment in which attention is paid to individual quality and where development opportunities are paramount. Together we strive for an inclusive culture in which we embrace differences. We would therefore like to invite candidates who want to contribute to this through their background and experience. In the event of equal suitability, preference will be given to the candidate who thus enhances diversity within the Academy.

Within the Soils for Europe project (EU-SOLO https://soils4europe.eu/), you will be responsible for the synthesis of work produced by thematic users groups and from published data on research needs with respect to soil health in Europe. We have a postdoc position open for the period of 3 years (0.8 FTE) within the PREDWEI 2 project. The aim of the project is to improve understanding of the spatial dynamics and shifting interactions among different predator species—both terrestrial and aerial—affecting ground-breeding birds (meadow, arable, and coastal species). The project will produce recommendations for effective management and policy regarding the various predator species, with the aim of increasing chick survival. The research will make an important contribution to knowledge on effective management for the conservation of ground-breeding birds and will identify the remaining knowledge gaps after completion of the study.
 Previous PREDWEI studies have provided substantial insight into the important role of various terrestrial predator species and their interactions in relation to ground-breeding birds. At the same time, these studies have revealed important knowledge gaps that are highly relevant for improving the effectiveness of policy and management aimed at protecting ground-breeding birds. This applies to the main landscape types in which these birds occur: meadow, arable, and coastal habitats, each with its own community of terrestrial and aerial predators (mammals and birds of prey).
 In each landscape type, a link will be established between nest and chick survival of ground-breeding birds and the occurrence, spatial habitat use, and diet of the various predators. This will be achieved through continued monitoring (predators, nests, and voles), diet studies (eDNA analyses of faeces and/or prey remains), and the expansion of telemetry studies of birds of prey. In this way, PREDWEI 2 builds on previous PREDWEI subprojects, while expanding the research to include the role of birds of prey through tracking studies. PREDWEI 2 will actively collaborate with several partner projects, including the Godwit Chick Survival Project, two arable bird pilot projects, and the Wij en Wadvogels project. academictransfer:364479.description:
Team 
A PhD position is available in the Neurogenesis & Neurodegeneration group at the Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience in Amsterdam. The Neurogenesis & Neurodegeneration laboratory led by Evgenia Salta employs transcriptomics and other molecular and cellular approaches to map the cellular and molecular complexity of the adult human hippocampus and dissect the biological pathways that are deregulated in dementia. The team employs primarily human postmortem brain tissue and iPSC reprogramming.
 Project 
The project is funded by the Dutch Research Council (NWO) Open Competition and is a collaboration between the Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience (NIN) and the Swammerdam Institute of Life Sciences (SILS) at the University of Amsterdam.
Repeated mild head injuries, the kind sustained by athletes, veterans, and victims of domestic violence, are increasingly linked to long-term memory problems and a higher risk of dementia later in life. Strikingly, these lasting effects can occur even when no visible brain damage is present. Yet, we still don't understand how repeated injury leads to memory decline, and there are currently no treatments that address these long-term cognitive consequences.
Beyond helping high-risk groups, this work may also shed light on Alzheimer's and other dementias that share similar underlying processes.
The research will be performed at the Salta lab at the Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience in Amsterdam. This is a joint project with the group of Carlos Fitzsimons at the SILS, University of Amsterdam.
This study is a follow up of our previously published work:
 https://www.cell.com/cell-stem-cell/fulltext/S1934-5909(26)00142-6 
 https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-49299-6 
 What you will do 
In this project, you will investigate what happens in the brain after repetitive mild traumatic brain injury, focusing on the hippocampus, the brain region central to memory. We are particularly interested in long-lasting inflammatory and neurogenic alterations and the cells involved in them, including microglia, astrocytes and immature neurons. By uncovering these mechanisms, you will help us to identify cellular or molecular targets that could guide the development of future therapies.
As a PhD candidate in our group, you will use state-of-the art single-nucleus RNA sequencing pipelines to process postmortem human brain from donors with a record of traumatic brain injury. You will be in charge of sample collection and stratification and apply advanced computational pipelines to identify cellular and molecular programs involved in the hippocampal response to injury and the downstream cognitive effects. Ultimately, you will establish in vitro human cell models to probe causal relationships between candidate targets and cellular phenotypes.
 What we expect from you 
 A Master’s degree in biomedical sciences, neuroscience or similar
 Strong affinity and hands-on experience with coding and omics-related computational analyses are a prerequisite
 Strong affinity and hands-on experience with single-cell transcriptomics are a prerequisite
 Strong experience with (iPSC) cell culture is a plus
 Excellent communication skills, as well as proficiency in spoken and written English, are expected
 Strong organizational skills, methodical and structured approach to your work, rigor, accuracy and attention to detail
 A reliable, collaborative team player who is easy to work with and delivers on commitments
 Genuine passion for scientific research
 Drive, persistence and positive attitude to tackle difficult problems that require iterative approaches, while systematically checking results against expectations to catch issues early
 What we offer 
 A stimulating, innovative and dynamic international research environment
 Opportunity to work with novel, exciting datasets and develop creative concepts and pipelines
 A strong community of care, support and scientific challenge
 Access to state-of-the art infrastructure and work conditions
 Active mentoring, supervision and training
 Opportunities for personal growth
 A particularly collaborative setting between the NIN and the SILS
 Possibility to develop your own projects and apply for third-party funding
The position is for a period of 4 years in total. The first appointment is for one year with the option for an extension for the remaining period pending on evaluation.
 Information 
For additional information, please contact Dr. E. Salta. e.salta@nin.knaw.nl
More information about the laboratory can be found on: Salta - Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience - Master the Mind (nin.nl) & https://saltalab.github.io/ 
 Application and deadline 
You can apply before December 1, 2026 via the button Apply Now.
Please send:
 A detailed CV
 A motivation letter, including a brief description of past research experience and future interests, as well as the earliest possible starting date and the name and contact details of at least two referees

Join us in developing the next generation of climate-resilient building envelopes. 
 Job description 
As a PhD candidate at TU Delft, you will explore how nature-based building skins can transform existing homes into healthier, cooler and more sustainable living environments. Working at the intersection of building physics, architecture, ecology and user-centered design, you will develop innovative façade solutions that combine vegetation, circular materials and smart ventilation strategies to improve indoor comfort without relying on energy-intensive cooling systems.
This is a unique opportunity to contribute to one of the most pressing challenges facing cities today: adapting existing housing to climate change while enhancing biodiversity and quality of life. Your work will move beyond theory. Through co-creation with residents and industry partners, full-scale prototyping and real-world testing, you will help bring innovative solutions from concept to demonstration.
While green façades and other nature-based solutions have demonstrated their potential to reduce surface temperatures and improve urban microclimates, limited knowledge exists on how integrated nature-based building skins can simultaneously deliver indoor heat resilience, ventilation performance, biodiversity enhancement, circularity and long-term user acceptance within affordable retrofit solutions for existing housing. As a PhD candidate at TU Delft, you will conduct research within the NWO-funded Nature 4 Homes project. Your research will focus on developing and demonstrating natural building skins for the heat-resilient retrofit of existing dwellings. The ambition is to create an affordable and easy-to-install building-envelope solution that integrates nature-based solutions and passive cooling strategies to mitigate overheating and regulate indoor conditions, while supporting biodiversity and circular renovation.
We are looking for a curious and motivated researcher who is excited to combine experimentation, design and stakeholder engagement. In return, you will join a collaborative and supportive research environment where independent thinking, creativity and interdisciplinary collaboration are encouraged.
At TU Delft, you will have access to world-class research facilities, international networks and the opportunity to work on solutions with direct relevance to society and the built environment sector.
Your research will combine co-creation, prototyping, experimental testing and modelling. Together with residents, manufacturers and other stakeholders, you will identify user-acceptance, maintenance and practical barriers affecting the design, installation and operation of natural building skins and translate these into design requirements. Successive prototypes will be developed and tested at MATELab, TU Delft’s outdoor full-scale façade testing facility, under real weather conditions to assess heat resilience, ventilation, heat and moisture transfer, and indoor environmental performance. The developed prototype systems will be evaluated through circular-design principles, considering material efficiency, adaptability, reuse potential and life-cycle environmental impacts. Experiments may also involve users to investigate comfort, interaction and acceptance, while numerical simulations will extend the experimental findings across different building and climate conditions.
You will join the Architectural Engineering + Technology (AE&T) Department at the Faculty of Architecture and the Built Environment and the Department of Materials, Mechanics, Management and Design, at the Faculty of Civil Engineering and Geosciences, TU Delft. You will work under the supervision of Marc Ottelé, Alessandra Luna-Navarro, and Atze Boerstra. You will collaborate closely with a postdoctoral researcher and three other PhD candidates, as well as research, industry and public-sector partners. We foster an open and collaborative environment where independent thinking, knowledge sharing and interdisciplinary research are encouraged.
 Job requirements 
 You hold an MSc in architecture, architectural engineering, civil engineering or a related field.
 You have a strong interest in human perception, building physics, building design and climate change.
 You are motivated to conduct a combination of experimental research, prototyping and environmental assessments.
 You have an affinity with measuring and modelling and analysing indoor and outdoor environmental conditions.
 You are interested in developing new façade design methods following circular principles.
 You enjoy interdisciplinary research and collaborating with academic, industry and public-sector partners.
 You have excellent oral and written communication skills in English. For more details, please check the Graduate Schools Admission Requirements.

Job description 
Take the next step in your scientific career as a Postdoctoral Researcher in Dynamic Organ-on-Chip Systems for In Vitro Bone Tissue Modeling and contribute to groundbreaking research at the interface of tissue engineering and regenerative medicine.
In the body, cells are constantly exposed to physical cues from their surroundings, and these cues change as tissues form and mature. Current in vitro models are largely static and cannot reproduce these dynamic cues. In this project, we address this gap by combining responsive biomaterials with a high-throughput organ-on-chip platform, allowing physical cues to be tuned on demand during culture. You will use this approach to build human in vitro bone tissue models for studying bone formation and for screening new therapies.
 Your main responsibilities will be to: 
 Adapt, optimize, and operate a patent-pending organ-on-chip platform for long-term 3D cell culture.
 Integrate responsive biomaterials into the platform and evaluate their cytocompatibility.
 Differentiate stem cells into osteogenic cells and establish human in vitro bone tissue models.
 Characterize cellular and tissue responses using a multiscale analytical approach, including confocal microscopy, gene expression analysis, and histology.
 Validate the bone tissue models using established bone therapeutics.
 Disseminate your findings through publications in leading peer-reviewed journals and presentations at international conferences.
 (Co-)supervise students and contribute to the organization of the laboratory.
 Engage with industrial partners and contribute to the translation of the technology toward preclinical applications.
The position is offered initially for one year, with the possibility of extension. The intended start date is 1 January 2027.

REQUIREMENTS:
Profile 
 A PhD in biomedical engineering, (bio)mechanical or chemical engineering, applied physics, materials science, (bio)chemistry, cell biology, or a related field.
 Candidates nearing completion of their PhD are also encouraged to apply, provided their thesis is approved for defense by the start date.
 Strong expertise in at least one of the following areas, and the motivation to build expertise in the other two: 
 Microfluidics or organ-on-chip systems.
 3D cell culture or cell mechanobiology.
 Hydrogel design and characterization.
 A track record of first-author publications in international peer-reviewed journals.
 Interest in translation and entrepreneurship is an advantage.
 Excellent written and spoken English, and the ability to work both independently and in a multidisciplinary team.

CONTRACT: 1 year with the prospect of extension

Do you want to pursue a PhD in political ecology, development studies or environmental humanities? Are you interested in (ground-)water? This PhD project – that examines the practices that individuals and communities in Peru engage in to care for, protect, rejuvenate and/or recharge the groundwaters they rely on for irrigating their crops – might be of interest to you.
 Caring for groundwater 
The PhD study is part of a larger project funded by an ERC Advanced Grant: “Aquiverse: a collaborative study of groundwater care to re-think, improve and support its governance”. The project aspires to learn from what irrigators and other water users do to protect and share the aquifers that they depend on for their livelihoods. Acknowledging how the over-exploitation of aquifers is linked to neo-liberal processes of agricultural intensification, the project is interested in exploring whether such caring practices can form part of a politics of transformation.
The project engages in collaborative studies of six organized initiatives of caring for aquifers – of recharge, conservation, recovery - in three countries (India, Peru and Morocco). How do these initiatives shape people’s connections with aquifers and with each other, and how do they (re-)configure possibilities for living and relating? The Peru cases centre around so-called pozas used for aquifer recharge on the desert coast and on the revival of traditional rainwater harvesting techniques in the high Andes mountains.
Connecting thick empirical description with methodological-theoretical engagement, the project aims to contribute to (among others) reflections on transformational politics, human-environment interactions and collective action (or communing). A central notion in the project is “aquiverse” – a combination of the words ‘aquifer’ and ‘pluriverse’ – . It denotes both a novel transdisciplinary understanding of groundwater and a new method to compare groundwater governance across cases.
The PhD project will have to be completed in 4 years. You will work closely with your supervisors, including Margreet Zwarteveen, as well as with the rest of the Aquiverse research team which includes another PhD fellow and 2 postdoctoral researchers (Carolina Dominguez-Guzman and Lisa Bossenbroek).
 What are you going to do 
As part of your PhD project, you are expected to engage in two or more of the following activities:
 a detailed ethnographic description of the everyday practices of people involved in the selected initiatives of caring for groundwater.
 A precise institutional and hydro-geological documentation and assessment of the functioning and performance of these initiatives.
 An in-depth historical and political-ecological analysis of how the depletion of groundwater is related to neo-liberal processes of water-based agrarian change and the politics of water (re-)allocation.
 An identification, documentation and analysis of how irrigators navigate pressures – to individualize, intensify or indeed over-exploit – in the study sites.
 What do you have to offer 
You are someone who:
 Has a (research) master’s degree in human Geography, Development Studies, Anthropology, or a closely related field.
 Is interested in (the role of water in) processes of agrarian change.
 Would like to contribute to (feminist) theorizations of human/society-environment relations (political ecology, environmental humanities).
 Has some familiarity with agrarian Peru and looks forward to spending time in remote rural areas.
 Has experience with ethnographic research methods but is not afraid of quantification.
 Has some understanding of or is curious to learn about hydrogeology.
 Enjoys engaging in inter-and transdisciplinary collaborations.
 Possesses excellent academic writing and communication skills in English
 Can communicate well in Spanish and preferably also in Quechua. Some knowledge of French, Arabic (Darija) or Hindi is an advantage.
 Cares for their colleagues and collaborators.
 Likes experimenting with creative methods of research and engagement.
 What else do we offer you 
We offer a temporary employment contract of 38 hours per week for a maximum term of four years. The initial employment is for one year. Following a positive assessment, this term will be extended by a maximum of three years, which should result in the conferral of a doctorate. You will attend courses offered by the Amsterdam Institute for Social Science Research (AISSR) and the Graduate School of Social Sciences as part of the PhD programme.

Are you intrigued by interactions between vegetation and fire? Are you passionate about lab-, field-, and remote sensing-based research? Do you like solving scientific puzzles? We are looking for a highly motivated PhD candidate to explore how moss traits affect fire ignitability in high-latitude ecosystems. 
Northern ecosystems, including boreal peatlands and tundra, are warming faster than almost anywhere else on Earth, which is changing their structure and functioning. Permafrost thaw and increasing fire frequency threaten to turn these ecosystems from carbon sinks into carbon, further accelerating climate change. Bryophytes (including mosses) dominate the vegetation across much of these carbon-dense ecosystems. Because of their unique water-retention and insulating properties, they largely determine how susceptible these regions are to severe wildfires. This PhD project examines the relationship between bryophyte functional traits and fire dynamics at the plant, ecosystem, and biome scales, combining lab experiments, fieldwork, and remote sensing. Building on the PEN research line on vegetation-climate feedbacks, your work will advance our understanding of the functional role of bryophytes in fire dynamics and help improve fire risk assessments for these vulnerable systems.
 Your duties and responsibilities include: 
 Developing methods and designing and executing experiments to test moss ignitability
 Conducting fieldwork in high-latitude ecosystems, including vegetation surveys, monitoring environmental conditions during and after fires, and possibly drone-based observations

For rapid control of virus outbreaks, fast availability of antivirals is a major bottleneck. In DETECTIVE, innovative models will be used for setting up an antiviral testing pipeline without the need for animals models. This doctoral project will focus on developing patient-derived organotypic models to test and optimise broad-spectrum antiviral therapies. Organotypic models, such as human organoids, are miniaturised in vitro organ cultures that mimic the human tissue-specific context. In this project, gut organoid models co-cultured with immune cells will be used to determine antiviral efficacy of available broadly acting antiviral against a scala of outbreak viruses such as enteroviruses and West-Nile virus. Patient-specific responses to virus infections will be assessed with integrated -omics techniques, and patient-dependent responses to antiviral therapy will be used to develop personalized medicine regimens for the future. With this project we will set the stage for an innovative human antiviral testing pipeline for viral outbreaks.
 Would you like to know more about the different phases within the PhD trajectory? You can read more about this on this page . 
At the Amsterdam UMC, DETECTIVE is looking for a Doctoral Candidate (DC) to work on Work Package 1. As DC6, your objectives are : 
 To establish patient-derived gut organoid mucosa models
 To test a panel of broadly acting antiviral compounds in patient-derived gut mucosa organoid models
 To identify virus and host factors determining treatment response by transcriptomics and proteomics

REQUIREMENTS:
Master’s degree in biomedical sciences, infection, immunity or related fields.
 Experience working with mammalian cell culture, qPCR, and bioinformatics is preferred.
 Experience working with stem cells and organoids is desirable.
 Excellent oral and written communication skills in English (minimum C1/C2 CEFR level).
 An interest in self-development and working in a multidisciplinary research environment

Do you have a passion for the ocean and would like to join expeditions to the Arctic to explore how deep-sea life is connected to our climate? Do you enjoy working in an interdisciplinary research setting? Pursuing a PhD at Naturalis in Leiden (the Netherlands) means working on research with a global impact — contributing directly to biodiversity. And you'll be well supported every step of the way. With 3,200 m² of state-of-the-art lab facilities, housed in a museum with more than 40 million natural history objects, dedicated mentorship, and access to our broad international network, this position offers everything you need to thrive as a scientist.
 As a PhD student ... 
 you will find yourself in a unique research environment, inspired by passionate scientists from a wide range of disciplines (e.g., taxonomy, evolution, ecology, and oceanography).
 You will receive dedicated supervision from an experienced researcher and work closely with several international experts and collaborators with whom you’ll regularly exchange ideas about your research. This will help you to develop a strong academic profile.
 You will build valuable connections by participating in both the academic and social activities of our PhD community.
 This is what you'll be doing 
In this PhD project, you will investigate the role of shelled zooplankton (planktonic snails or pteropods) in the biological carbon pump in a changing Arctic Ocean. You will assess the contribution to carbon fluxes and the tropic role of shelled pteropods by collecting depth-stratified samples on expeditions to the Arctic Ocean with a large scientific vessel and analyzing time series samples from the Long-Term Ecological (LTER) observatory HAUSGARTEN operated by the German Alfred-Wegener Institute (AWI). You will use a combination of state-of-the-art morphological and molecular techniques to quantify carbon fluxes as well as the ecology of current and past populations of shelled pteropods.
You will be working within an international team of Dutch research institutes (University of Amsterdam, Naturalis Biodiversity Center, and the NIOZ Royal Netherlands Institute of Sea Research) and the German Alfred-Wegener Institute (AWI) for Polar and Sea Research on an ambitious larger project including three positions (two PhD students and one Post-Doc): Plumbing the biological pump: Linking missing carbon flows between pelagic and benthic ecosystems in a changing Arctic Ocean (C-CONNECT).
The global biological carbon pump mediates the cycling and storage of carbon in our ocean and helps to regulate Earth’s climate. Arctic waters are amongst, if not the most, rapidly changing in terms of temperatures, sea-ice cover, and acidification. However, our understanding of climate-change impacts that affect the Arctic carbon pump’s size and speed of flows remains incomplete.
The main aim in C-CONNECT is to perform plumbing to the Arctic biological carbon pump by connecting important missing parts, e.g., shelled zooplankton and benthic faunal communities to the carbon cycle. C-CONNECT will improve the ability to project how future Arctic carbon cycling evolves under continued climate change and will provide essential information on Arctic ecosystem services to aid (policy and management) decision making.
This PhD position in the C-CONNECT project is funded by NWO (Dutch research council).
 Here's what we have to offer 
 A gross monthly starting salary of € 3,567.00 for a full-time contract (36 hours).
 A contract of one year, to be extended by 3 years after successful evaluation.
 End-of-year bonus of 3.4% of your gross annual salary and 8% holiday pay.
 27 days of leave per year with full-time employment. Plus 1 extra day that you can use for a holiday that is important to you.

 Fascinating knowledge events. These help you stay up to date on the latest developments in both your own field and outside it, such as our lectures and gatherings on various (scientific) topics. You can also attend – or take part in – the fascinating internal information session Naturalis Draait Door.
 Nice extras such as discounts on software and hardware for private use, collective health insurance plans, and a bicycle scheme. You’ll also enjoy discounts in our museum restaurant and unlimited free access to our award-winning museum for you and your family.
 Fun team outings. We also get together for drinks every month, organize an annual BBQ and a fantastic New Year's party. Not your scene? That's fine too, of course. All team activities are voluntary.
 A unique work environment in a state-of-the-art building where you will feel proud to work every single day – we guarantee it!

Wat ga je doen? 
Als Laborant Mediabereiding ben jij de drijvende kracht achter de schermen van het Hubrecht Instituut en het Westerdijk Institute . In een hecht en kundig team zorg je ervoor dat onze toponderzoekers nooit misgrijpen. Jouw werk is de basis van hun succes.
 Je bereidt media, reagentia en (moleculaire) hulpvloeistoffen. Je werkt hierbij met zowel high-tech mediapoeders als eigen gefabriceerde extracten.
 Je bent het aanspreekpunt voor onderzoekers; jij adviseert hen over de beste bereidingswijzen.
 Je houdt onze geavanceerde apparatuur (zoals stoomsterilisatoren en doseerpompen) in topconditie.
 Je bent verwantwoordelijk voor het verzamelen van glaswerk tot het veilig afvoeren van destructiematerialen; jij bewaart het overzicht in de lab-logistiek.
 Je draagt bij aan ons ISO 9001 kwaliteitssysteem en begeleidt de laboranten van de toekomst (stagiaires).
 Dit breng jij mee: 
 Je bent in het bezit van een relevant MLO-diploma (niveau 3 of 4).
 Je hebt een achtergrond in de microbiologie of chemie.
 Je bent servicegericht en je vindt het leuk om onderzoekers verder te helpen.
 Je spreekt vloeiend Nederlands en heb een goede beheersing van de Engelse taal.
Let op: Vanwege de aard van de werkzaamheden is deze functie specifiek ingericht voor MLO-niveau. Kandidaten met een WO- of PhD-achtergrond worden niet meegenomen in de procedure.
 Wat bieden wij? 
Je komt terecht in een klein hecht team met vijf personen, 2 spoelmederwerkers en 3 mediabereiders. In het team wordt er veel gelachen en we zijn behulpzaam naar elkaar toe. Iedere maand wordt door de leidinggevende een werkrooster opgesteld, iedere medewerker staat per dag ingedeeld voor een bepaalde taak. Daarnaast heeft iedere medewerker de verrantwoordelijkheid (beheer) over een bepaalde labruimte en is beheerder over een aantal apparaten. Wij werken volgens protocol maar er is altijd ruimte voor nieuwe ideeen om op een andere manier van werken. Samen streven we er naar een mooi product af te leveren aan de onderzoekers en zijn we daar trots op.
Wil je meer weten? 
Neem contact op met: Ron van der Waals, Manager media preparation, r.vanderwaals@hubrecht.eu .
 Over het Hubrecht Instituut 
Het Hubrecht Instituut is een onderzoeksinstituut dat zich richt op moleculaire en ontwikkelingsbiologie. Door het dynamische karakter van het onderzoeksveld heeft het instituut een wisselend aantal onderzoeksgroepen, rond de 20, die fundamenteel, multidisciplinair onderzoek verrichten op gezonde en zieke cellen, weefsels en organismen. Het Hubrecht Instituut is onderdeel van de Koninklijke Nederlandse Akademie van Wetenschappen ( KNAW ) en bevindt zich op Utrecht Science Park. Sinds 2008 is het instituut geaffilieerd met het UMC Utrecht . Dit bevordert de vertaling van het onderzoek naar de kliniek. Het Hubrecht Institute heeft een partnerschap met het European Molecular Biology Laboratory (EMBL). Voor meer informatie, ga naar www.hubrecht.eu/nl .
 Arbeidsvoorwaarden 
Het salaris bedraagt afhankelijk van opleiding en ervaring minimaal 3.147 en maximaal 3.622 bruto per maand bij een full time dienstverband (schaal 5 cao Nederlandse Universiteiten/KNAW) . Dit is exclusief 8% vakantiegeld, 8,3% eindejaarsuitkering, reiskostenvergoeding, internet- en thuiswerkvergoeding en pensioenopbouw bij het ABP.
De KNAW biedt haar medewerkers een uitstekend pakket aan secundaire arbeidsvoorwaarden. Een pakket dat voorziet in de verschillende behoeften die medewerkers afhankelijk van hun levensfase, levenswijze of loopbaanambities hebben. Zo is het mogelijk om door wekelijks twee uur per week extra te werken het aantal vakantiedagen van 29 tot 41 dagen per jaar (bij fulltime dienstverband) uit te breiden.
Voor een volledig overzicht van de arbeidsvoorwaarden wordt verwezen naar de webpagina: werken bij de KNAW .
 Het aanvragen van een VOG kan onderdeel uitmaken van de indiensttredingsprocedure .
 Diversiteit & Inclusie 
De KNAW acht een werkomgeving waarin iedereen zich welkom en gewaardeerd voelt van groot belang. Een werkomgeving waarin aandacht is voor individuele kwaliteit en waar ontwikkelmogelijkheden voorop staan. Samen streven we naar een inclusieve cultuur waarin we verschillen omarmen. We nodigen dan ook graag kandidaten uit die door hun achtergrond en ervaring hieraan een bijdrage willen leveren. Bij gelijke geschiktheid gaat de voorkeur uit naar de kandidaat die de diversiteit binnen de KNAW op deze wijze versterkt.
Acquisitie naar aanleiding van deze advertentie wordt niet op prijs gesteld.

Verder heb je:

Metabolic syndrome is a major health problem, affecting up to 40% of the population. It increases the risk of developing chronic diseases such as diabetes, cardiovascular disease, obesity and cancer.
The META-IMMUNOTYPES consortium studies the complex interaction between the immune system and metabolism in metabolic syndrome and related conditions. This could enable lifestyle interventions before symptoms arise.

 Receiving, processing, registering, storing and retrieving human biological samples, mainly blood.

 Writing, maintaining and improving SOPs and other biobank documentation, while contributing to quality control and continuous improvement.
 Supporting general laboratory organization and, where relevant, experimental work within ongoing research projects.

academictransfer:364544.description:
The Challenge 
Egypt’s horticulture sector operates under growing pressure from limited water availability, salinity, and rising competition over finite water resources. At the same time, the sector is economically important for food security, rural livelihoods, and export earnings, which means that improving water productivity is not only an environmental protection measure but also a strategic development and trade challenge.
These pressures call for better evidence on current and future water use, stronger metrics for identifying good performance, and more robust ways to link farm-level improvements to wider policy and investment decisions. They also raise questions about how private-sector actors can support and scale water-smart change, including through credible incentive and financing mechanisms.
 The position 
You will join the Water Footprint in Action programme, a multi-partner initiative funded by the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs and focused on advancing water-smart agriculture in Egypt’s horticulture sector. The programme brings together three complementary lines of work: building a strong scientific and evidence base, strengthening advisory and knowledge systems, and supporting business innovation and investment in water-smart solutions. Within this wider setting, your PhD work will mainly sit in the research and knowledge component, while also helping connect scientific insights to shared knowledge resources, decision-support tools, stakeholder learning, and new financing approaches.
A preliminary research plan looks as follows.
First, you will develop and apply quantitative approaches to analyse the present and future water consumption (i.e., the water footprint) of Egypt’s horticulture sector. This includes crop modelling using our in-house ACEA model, designing climate and socio-economic scenarios, and linking analyses across scales to local intervention settings, national policy priorities, and trade dynamics.
Next, you will work on water footprint benchmarks and performance indicators. In this part of the PhD, you will compare different ways of defining good performance, for example by looking at producer performance based on Best Available Technology and Best Available Practice, and relate these to broader sustainability and efficiency indicators.
A third part of your research will focus on how water savings and other water-smart improvements can be measured in a way that is credible, transparent, and useful in practice. You will help develop a science-based method that can underpin incentive or finance mechanisms for improved water performance, working closely with project partners and engaging with wider debates around environmental credits and integrity.
You will be embedded in an international consortium and work closely with partners in the Netherlands and Egypt, including Egyptian water and agricultural research centres. The position includes intensive interaction with stakeholders, frequent visits to project locations and case-study sites in Egypt, and an active role in a broader knowledge exchange programme through joint research, data exchange, publications, and learning activities.

REQUIREMENTS:
You have a Master’s degree in a relevant field, such as water management, agricultural systems, or environmental science.
 You have a strong quantitative profile, including experience with data analysis, modelling, programming, or computational research methods.
 You are conceptually strong and able to translate complex sustainability questions into rigorous research designs, including scenario development and method design.
 You are interested in water footprint assessment, water-smart agriculture, benchmarking, sustainability metrics, and environmental crediting approaches.
 You enjoy collaborating with international academic and practice partners and can work effectively in a multi-stakeholder environment.
 You exhibit high levels of self-motivated and have strong communication skills.
 You are willing to travel and conduct regular project visits in Egypt in connection with research activities, partner collaboration, and case studies.
 You are motivated to contribute both to high-quality academic research and to applied impact in an international, policy-relevant project setting.
 Arabic language skills are a strong asset; being an Arabic speaker and having experience in the Egyptian context is beneficial.
 You are available to start the position per 1 January 2027.

This multidisciplinary project integrates electrochemistry, metal–organic framework-based materials, and membrane chemistry to develop the next generation of high-performance membranes and unlock new possibilities for advanced molecular separation and transport.
 Can you design the membrane that powers the next generation of electrolysers? 
Electrolysis and electrocatalysis have a key role to play in creating a more sustainable chemical industry. At the heart of these technologies are membranes that control the transport of protons and other species—but today’s proton exchange membranes rely heavily on PFAS-based materials such as Nafion®. We are looking for a PhD candidate to develop a new generation of high-performance, PFAS-free proton-conductive membranes. In this project, you will combine the unique properties of proton-conductive metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) with those of proton-conductive polymers to create innovative membrane materials. You will systematically investigate how molecular structure, composition, and membrane architecture determine proton transport and overall performance. Your research will span materials chemistry, membrane science, and electrochemistry. You will establish design principles for high-performance proton-conductive membranes and put your materials to the test in different electrolyser configurations. This is an opportunity to work at the interface of fundamental materials science and real-world energy technology, with the ambition to develop membrane materials that can help enable a cleaner and more sustainable chemical industry. You hold an MSc degree in Physical Chemistry, Chemistry, Materials Science, or a related discipline, with a background in one or more of the following areas: electrochemistry, membrane chemistry, MOF synthesis, or materials characterization. Teaser Text 
 The The Leiden University's Institute of Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology at Leiden University is looking for an ambitious PhD-candidate to study the impacts of economization of seaweed as part of ‘blue economy’ strategies in South Africa. Research focuses on the impacts on coastal communities, considering that in South Africa colonial and apartheid legacies still influence patterns of access to coastal areas. You will work within the project ‘Entangled in seaweed: The politics of economizing nature in Scotland and South Africa’ funded by an NWO Open Competition grant.
 What you will do 
 You will work in a project team consisting of PhD-candidates and researchers at Leiden University, collaborating with project partners in South Africa. You will:
 Develop a research proposal in the context of the overall project theme, and conduct twelve months of ethnographic research in South Africa. An ethics review and contribution to the data management plan are included in the proposal development. Research includes document/policy analysis, participant observation, interviews, and the application of participatory visual storytelling methods.
 Analyse research findings and write a dissertation that contributes to the objectives of the ‘Entangled with Seaweed’ project.
 Actively contribute to the output and dissemination of the research project, which includes collaborating with the other team members on academic and non-academic publications, science communication, and the organization of workshops, seminars and an exhibition.
 Participate in relevant PhD-courses and masterclasses, organized in accordance with the guidelines of the Faculty of Social Science and the Institute of Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology. PhD-courses at Stellenbosch University, our partner in the project, can be included in the individual training and supervision plan as well.
 Participate in the PhD programme and other academic activities of the Institute of Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology at Leiden University. During your stay in South Africa you will also be able to participate in the PhD-programme at the Department of Sociology and Social Anthropology at Stellenbosch University.
 Where you will work 
 The Faculty of Social and Behavioural Sciences consists of five institutes: the Centre for Science and Technology Studies, Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology, Education and Child Studies, Political Science, and Psychology. The faculty is home to approximately 7,000 students and 1,000 staff members. Our institutes are dedicated not only to education but also to groundbreaking research that expands our understanding of human behavior and societal structures. What makes our faculty unique is the diversity of research topics, the variety of teaching approaches, and the structure of professional support. This provides you with the opportunity to explore and develop your interests and expertise. For an introduction to our faculty, visit our website: Welcome to the Leiden Faculty of Social and Behavioural Sciences – Leiden University .  
 Leiden University's Institute of Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology (CADS) 
Leiden University's Institute of Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology concentrates on 'global vulnerability and social resilience'. The institute has three main themes: diversity, sustainability, and digitalisation. CADS is dedicated to making a real-world impact, not just studying change, but also working with communities to promote positive change through education and research. We use a unique approach that blends qualitative, quantitative, audiovisual, and digital methods based on ethnographic fieldwork.
 With our unique blend of interdisciplinary interests, comparative regional studies, and social science research methods, we emphasize our role in the extensive collaborative network within Leiden University. In both our research and education, we engage in extensive interdisciplinary and international networks.
 The project team 
 The project team at Leiden University works closely together with colleagues at the University of Edinburgh, the Scottish Association for Marine Science, and Stellenbosch University. The PhD-students will be jointly supervised by Leiden University and Stellenbosch University, and Leiden University and the University of Edinburgh respectively. A project assistant will assist with training and dissemination activities.

 Demonstrable excellent qualitative research skills and experience with ethnographic fieldwork.
 Affinity with the topics of sustainability and environmental justice.
 Excellent oral and written communication skills.
 Strong command of English;
 Knowledge of one of the other official languages of South Africa is a bonus.
 Excellent social and organisational skills and the ability to work independently as well as in a team.

Within our terms of employment individual choices model, you can exchange leave days and/or salary for benefits such as an advantageous sports subscription and bicycle scheme;

Onze mensen worden geïnspireerd door nieuwsgierigheid, om zo fundamentele kennis te vergroten en over grenzen heen te kijken. Voor de wetenschap, én om een bijdrage te leveren aan grote maatschappelijke uitdagingen van morgen.
Het onderzoek binnen de faculteit der Wiskunde en Natuurwetenschappen varieert van wiskunde, informatica, sterrenkunde, natuurkunde, scheikunde en biofarmaceutische wetenschappen tot aan biologie en milieuwetenschappen en is belegd bij acht instituten. Daarnaast kent de Universiteit Leiden goede arbeidsvoorwaarden. Zo is er sprake van een eindejaarsuitkering (8,3%), vakantietoeslag (8%), uitstekende opleidingsfaciliteiten, betaald ouderschapsverlof, sabbatical leave en de mogelijkheid om via een keuzemodel arbeidsvoorwaarden op maat te kiezen. Alle informatie is te lezen op www.werkenbij.leidenuniv.nl .
Universiteit Leiden hecht groot belang aan diversiteit en verwelkomt daarom speciaal sollicitaties van mensen die nu in haar instelling ondervertegenwoordigd zijn.

Voor meer informatie kun je contact opnemen met Maurice Heemskerk, Hoofd Fijnmechanische Dienst en Elektronische Dienst (heemskerk@physics.leidenuniv.nl).

academictransfer:364559.description:
Wanneer een kind een ouder heeft met een ernstige psychiatrische aandoening, zoals een bipolaire of psychotische aandoening, of ernstige depressie, heeft dit kind een 2 tot 4 maal groter risico om zelf psychiatrische problemen te ontwikkelen. We willen beter begrijpen hoe en wanneer (dit risico op) een ernstige psychiatrische aandoening ontstaat. We weten dat de (hersen)ontwikkeling van een kind tijdens de zwangerschap en de eerste twee jaar van het leven heel belangrijk is voor de rest van het leven.
Maar we weten nog niet veel over hoe de hersenen van kinderen ontwikkelen in de baarmoeder. Ook weten we nog weinig over hoe pasgeboren baby's en jonge kinderen van ouders met een ernstige psychiatrische aandoening zich ontwikkelen. Daarnaast zijn er wereldwijd nog weinig gegevens bekend over de invloed van stress van ouders, kenmerken van het gezinsleven en de ouder-kindrelatie op de sociaalemotionele ontwikkeling van het kind in deze groep. Als we vroeg kunnen zien dat de ontwikkeling van deze kinderen anders verloopt, dan hopen we met goede begeleiding te voorkomen dat kinderen ziek worden of het tijdstip van mogelijk ziek worden uit te stellen.
In de PANDA-studie volgen we de hersen- en sociaalemotionele ontwikkeling van ongeboren en pasgeboren kinderen van wie minimaal één ouder een ernstige psychiatrische aandoening heeft. Dit vergelijken we met kinderen van wie de ouders geen psychiatrische aandoening hebben. Ook bekijken we hoe kenmerken van de hersen- en sociaalemotionele ontwikkeling van het kind samenhangen met de ouder-kindrelatie. We brengen de hersenontwikkeling in kaart door MRI-scans te maken van baby's in de buik en pasgeborenen. En we volgen de sociaalemotionele ontwikkeling van het kind, de ouder-kind relatie en symptomen van ouders middels (online) vragenlijsten tot het kindje 18 maanden is. Daarnaast komen wij bij de gezinnen langs met de Sophia-bus wanneer het kindje 9 maanden is. Om het sociaal-emotioneel functioneren van het kind te meten middels eye-tracking, en om de ouder-kind relatie te observeren middels video-opnames van ouder-kind interacties.
Als onderzoeksmedewerker:
 Ondersteun je de postdoctoraal onderzoeker en PhD student in het opzetten en uitvoering van het onderzoek.
 Ben je verantwoordelijk voor de werving, het plannen van afspraken, dataverzameling en dataverwerking.
 Ben je het aanspreekpunt van het project voor gezinnen.
 Neem je psychiatrische interviews af, help je bij het maken van MRI-scans van zwangeren en pasgeborenen, ga je samen met studenten met de Sophia-bus langs bij gezinnen om eye-tracking en interactietaken af te nemen.
 Begeleid je masterstudenten psychologie, pedagogiek of geneeskunde gedurende hun wetenschappelijke stage.

REQUIREMENTS:
Je moet een hoge mate van motivatie en toewijding hebben om nauwkeurig werk van hoge kwaliteit te produceren en uitstekende interpersoonlijke, organisatorische, analytische en documentatievaardigheden hebben. Het is belangrijk dat je zowel zelfstandig als in teamverband kunt werken. Daarnaast:
 Je hebt een achtergrond in psychologie, pedagogische wetenschappen, geneeskunde, biomedische wetenschappen, neurowetenschappen of een gerelateerde discipline.
 Affiniteit met wetenschappelijke vraagstukken binnen de context van de kinder- en jeugdpsychologie/-psychiatrie en hoog-risico populaties is belangrijk.
 Je hebt ervaring met kwantitatief onderzoek en/of epidemiologisch onderzoek en bij voorkeur ervaring met programmeren (bijvoorbeeld in R).
 Vloeiend Nederlands spreken, lezen en schrijven is vereist. Een goede beheersing van het Engels (mondeling en schriftelijk) is een pluspunt.
 In verband met het besturen van de Sophia-bus, is in het bezit zijn van een rijbewijs een pluspunt.
Vanwege het feit dat de MRI-scanner in het weekend of in de avonden beschikbaar is voor wetenschappelijk onderzoek, vragen we de bereidheid om flexibel in de weekenden en avonden beschikbaar te zijn. Samen bespreken we jouw inzetbaarheid. Een goede werk-privébalans vinden we belangrijk.

academictransfer:364561.description:
The Amsterdam Institute for Life and Environment (A-LIFE) invites applications for an Assistant Professor in molecular evolution in the field of Evolutionary Adaptation in the Anthropocene.
Humans are causing unprecedented and fast changes on our planet, challenging scientists to understand how anthropogenic environmental change affects the evolution of traits and interactions of species. Genetic and phenotypic variation play a crucial role in adaptation of species to anthropogenic habitats. We are looking for candidates who combine outstanding research with enthusiastic teaching, in understanding the molecular basis of adaptation in human-impacted environments, using approaches such as epigenetics, transcriptomics, and functional genetics. Candidates studying the molecular effect of selection pressure caused by pollution and/or urbanization on terrestrial invertebrates are specifically invited to apply. The position is embedded in the section Ecology & Evolution, a vibrant research group with a strong global track record in conservation genomics, stress adaptation, species interactions and trait ecology. The candidates are expected to contribute to our focus on integrative ecological and evolutionary research.
The Amsterdam Institute for Life and Environment (A-LIFE) offers a stimulating international research environment with a world-class academic reputation, and state-of-the-art facilities. We have a strong commitment to bachelor and master level teaching. Research in the institute covers a wide range of fundamental and applied research topics with the aim of advancing the fundamental understanding of the interplay between life and its environment. The section’s strength lies in the ability to integrate studies of adaptive changes across the entire range of biological organizational levels, including human populations. We do this as an international, inclusive, and collaborative group of researchers.
We ask candidates to write a concise research statement (max. 1 pages) that identifies and presents how their research plans will contribute to the research portfolio of the department in general, and the section Ecology & Evolution in particular. In addition, we ask candidates to provide a concise teaching statement (also 1 pages max.) reflecting on their teaching vision and how they will contribute to the teaching tasks of the department.
 Your duties 
 develop a vigorous, largely extramurally funded research program
 teach bachelor and master level courses in evolution, ecology, ecotoxicology or related subjects
 provide high-quality training and supervision to BSc and MSc-students, PhD-students and postdocs
 engage in professional development activities related to teaching and academic leadership

REQUIREMENTS:
PhD in evolutionary biology, molecular biology, ecotoxicology or related field with at least three years of postdoctoral experience
 strong track record of research and publications in the field of evolutionary adaptation to anthropogenic environmental changes
 proven ability for acquisition of external funding
 demonstrated skills in activating teaching methods in BSc and MSc level courses
 excellent communication skills (written and spoken English) and motivation to work in a team
 proficiency in Dutch is not required, but the successful candidate is expected to develop at least a passive proficiency within three years after appointment
As a university, we strive for equal opportunities for all, recognising that diversity takes many forms. We believe that diversity in all its complexity is invaluable for the quality of our teaching, research and service. We are always looking for talent with diverse backgrounds and experiences. This also means that we are committed to creating an inclusive community so that we can use diversity as an asset.
We realise that each individual brings a unique set of skills, expertise and mindset. Therefore we are happy to invite anyone who recognises themselves in the profile to apply, even if you do not meet all the requirements.

CONTRACT: 1 year

Join the Dutch 6G flagship project to help shape the future of communications. 
 Job description 
Join the frontier of innovation in 6G: the future of mobile networks technology! In the Netherlands, a unique alliance of 60 top-notch ICT companies, semiconductor firms, and research institutions has united to spearhead specific aspects of 6G: (1) software antennas, (2) AI-driven network software, and (3) groundbreaking 6G applications. Join us as a PhD student in this prestigious Future Network Services (FNS) flagship project, where research and entrepreneurial pursuits converge.
With 6G expected to support mission-critical services, such as autonomous mobility, remote healthcare, and industrial automation, network operators must be able to anticipate, quantify, and mitigate risks arising from both internal and external factors.
To address this need, through this PhD project, you will develop a risk profiling and resilience advisory system for 6G networks. This system will continuously compute a comprehensive risk profile for network infrastructure and operations, providing actionable recommendations for resilient network planning, evolution, and disaster recovery.
You’ll be joining an internationally diverse and thriving team, providing ample opportunities for riveting sparring and knowledge sharing. Fostering a highly collaborative and friendly atmosphere, we will give you all the support you need to develop and grow. Moreover, as a valued member of the FNS consortium, you can collaborate with various partners in pursuit of integrating your AI/ML techniques into the various 6G PoCs and demos.
 Job requerements 
Become part of an expansive ecosystem shaping the development of 6G. You will benefit from training in 5G and beyond networks, AI, and software development. Plus, you will gain exclusive access to (1) a state-of-the-art testbed where theory meets real-world application, and (2) an ecosystem that cultivates entrepreneurial endeavours.
Are you ready to challenge yourself? We're seeking candidates who have, or are about to receive, a Master-of-Science degree in a relevant computer science discipline and who like to combine theory with practice. Proficiency in English is essential, as you'll collaborate within a diverse, international community. For more details on our admission requirements, please visit https://www.tudelft.nl/onderwijs/opleidingen/phd/admission. We’ll evaluate based on your academic record, interviews, and possibly assignments. While a strong background in the field is crucial, what matters as well is your creative flair, motivation, and above all, your passion for comprehensive research!

Delft University of Technology is built on strong foundations. As creators of the world-famous Dutch waterworks and pioneers in biotech, TU Delft is a top international university combining science, engineering and design. It delivers world class results in education, research and innovation to address challenges in the areas of energy, climate, mobility, health and digital society. For generations, our engineers have proven to be entrepreneurial problem-solvers, both in business and in a social context.
At TU Delft we embrace diversity as one of our core values and we actively engage to be a university where you feel at home and can flourish. We value different perspectives and qualities. We believe this makes our work more innovative, the TU Delft community more vibrant and the world more just. Together, we imagine, invent and create solutions using technology to have a positive impact on a global scale. That is why we invite you to apply. Your application will receive fair consideration.
Challenge. Change. Impact!
 Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science 
The Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science (EEMCS) brings together three scientific disciplines. Combined, they reinforce each other and are the driving force behind the technology we all use in our daily lives. Technology such as the electricity grid, which our faculty is helping to make completely sustainable and future-proof. At the same time, we are developing the chips and sensors of the future, whilst also setting the foundations for the software technologies to run on this new generation of equipment – which of course includes AI. Meanwhile we are pushing the limits of applied mathematics, for example mapping out disease processes using single cell data, and using mathematics to simulate gigantic ash plumes after a volcanic eruption. In other words: there is plenty of room at the faculty for ground-breaking research. We educate innovative engineers and have excellent labs and facilities that underline our strong international position. In total, more than 1000 employees and 4,000 students work and study in this innovative environment.

academictransfer:364597.description:
The PhD position is part of the larger research project Re-Flex Zeeland that aims to reconstruct and visualize Zeeland's natural landscape formation processes during historical periods of rapid sea-level rise, with a focus on the last 12,000 years. The project is funded by the Delta Climate Centre (DCC) in Vlissingen and consists of two PhDs and one postdoc position in a collaboration between Utrecht University, Wageningen University & Research (WUR), NIOZ, Scalda and UNESCO GeoPark Schelde Delta.
 Your job 
The present-day landscape of Zeeland is highly regulated to support key societal, economic, and flood-safety functions. Allowing more space for natural processes to shape the landscape can contribute to flood protection and restoration of biodiversity, however, knowledge of how natural landscapes have evolved in the past and of the ecosystem services they once provided remains limited. This phenomenon is often described as shifting baselines, whereby each generation perceives the contemporary environment as the long-term norm. In reality, the Dutch landscape—and that of Zeeland in particular—has been extraordinarily dynamic and adjusting flexibly to changes in sea level. Over the Holocene, Zeeland has transitioned from an subarctic environment with boreal forest to alternating phases of peatland and intertidal environments, before becoming largely regulated through human embankment only in the past few centuries.
For the work package “Holocene peat deposits as natural archives of landscape developments” we look for a motivated PhD student who investigates these landscape and ecosystem dynamics in Zeeland based on fossil plant remains preserved in peat and lake sediment records.
 What will you be doing? 
You will design and carry out field work to map the locations and ages of peat deposits along an east-west transect around the major marine estuaries of Zeeland. You will integrate existing and new field data and investigate the botanical composition of the peat and, using pollen analysis, improve the current knowledge on past landscape reconstructions with a focus on peat to intertidal transitions. You will also co-supervise BSc and MSc courses and thesis projects that contribute to this.
The gathered data will provide new insight in the exact timing and variability in past landscape changes. Your results will furthermore contribute to computer simulations of coastal dynamics in a parallel PhD project conducted at WUR and provide context for visualisations of historic landscapes developed by a postdoc at NIOZ in a collaboration with Scalda and UNESCO GeoPark Schelde Delta.

REQUIREMENTS:
We are looking for an enthusiastic PhD candidate who is interested in landscape and vegetation development through time across different timescales and a drive to understand the relevant processes involved. The project physical geographical field work, pollen analysis and quantitative vegetation reconstruction. We require at least significant experience in one of these aspects and a motivation to develop skills in the other. The project will involve several sampling campaigns in Zeeland, in collaboration with the DCC, and training courses for the relevant techniques. You have a broad interest in geosciences, are a team player who is able to work in interdisciplinary environment, and are curiosity-driven.
We are looking for a candidate:
 with an MSc degree in Physical Geography, Earth Sciences, Landscape Ecology, or a related field;
 who has a drive to link and collaborate with different geoscientific disciplines;
 with demonstrated experience with paleogeographic and/or botanical landscape reconstructions;
 with affinity with Zeeland and willingness to spend time in and engage with the Zeeland landscape and community;
 with good English oral and writing skills: English at C1 level or better (comparable to level 3 of the Lecturer Assessment Grid) qualifies, or willingness and aptitude to obtain this level by training.
PhD candidates at Utrecht University follow courses as part of their own academic and personal development. They also assist in teaching courses at Bachelor's and Master's level at our faculty. Both activities amount to approximately 10% of the contracted time.

Do you want to contribute to ethnographic research into the politics of valuing seaweed in Scotland? 
The Leiden University's Institute of Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology, based within the Faculty of Social Sciences, is looking for an ambitious PhD-candidate to study the impacts of economization of seaweed as part of ‘blue economy’ strategies in Scotland. Research focuses on the impacts on coastal communities considering that in Scotland colonial legacies still influence patterns of unequal access to and use of coastal areas. You will work within the project ‘Entangled in seaweed: The politics of economising nature in Scotland and South Africa’ funded by an NWO Open Competition grant.
 Project Description 
The project investigates the impacts of economisation of seaweed as part of a global drive to develop ‘blue economy’ strategies. Seaweed harvesting and cultivation (as food, or fertilizer- and bioplastic ingredient) are increasing considerably and promoted as contributing to sustainable development. The project focuses on coastal communities in Scotland, which has developed a comprehensive blue economy strategy. Building on insights from political ecology and valuation studies and inspired by the multispecies turn in anthropology, this project aims to study local impacts of new forms of economisation of seaweed, and the possible contestations these may entail. It seeks to incorporate the ideas, interests, and knowledge from local groups who live from, in and with seaweed ecologies, examining how new versions of economisation affect local social relations, including the entanglements with non-humans these ecologies and economisations depend on. It does so by focusing on valuations of seaweed ecologies, based on an understanding of values as enacted through practices by all (human and non-human) stakeholders. The project employs a collaborative approach vis-à-vis research participants and a wider audience through a visual storytelling approach.
 What you will do 
You will work in a project team consisting of two PhD-candidates and researchers at Leiden University, collaborating with project partners in Scotland. You will:
 Develop a research proposal in the context of the overall project theme, and conduct twelve months of ethnographic research in Scotland. An ethics review and contribution to the data management plan are included in the proposal development. Research includes historical document/policy analysis, participant observation, interviews, and the application of participatory visual storytelling methods.
 Analyse research findings and write a dissertation that contributes to the objectives of the ‘Entangled with Seaweed’ project.

PhD-courses at the University of Edinburgh, our partner in the project, can be included in the individual training and supervision plan as well.
 Participate in the PhD programme and other academic activities of the Institute of Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology at Leiden University. During your stay in Scotland you will also be able to participate in the PhD-programme at the University of Edinburgh as well as academic activities organised by the Scottish Association for Marine Science (SAMS).

The Faculty of Social and Behavioural Sciences consists of five institutes: the Centre for Science and Technology Studies, Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology, Education and Child Studies, Political Science, and Psychology. The faculty is home to approximately 7,000 students and 1,000 staff members. Our institutes are dedicated not only to education but also to groundbreaking research that expands our understanding of human behavior and societal structures. Curious how we can turn a scanning electron microscope into a surface-sensitive diffractive microscope? Excited about building novel electron-optical systems? We're looking for you! 
 Job description 
We are looking for a postdoctoral researcher to join the Curious Beams Lab at Delft University of Technology and lead the instrumentation development for BEAMSurf: Diffractive Atomic-Scale Surface Imaging with Backscattered Electrons, an ERC Starting Grant project led by Dr. Georgios Varnavides.
BEAMSurf aims to develop a new type of scanning electron microscope that uses coherent backscattered electrons for diffractive imaging of material surfaces. By combining electron optics, MEMS technology, experimental microscopy, and computational imaging, we aim to open new possibilities for high-resolution surface imaging at low electron energies.
As the postdoctoral researcher, you will take the technical and scientific ownership of the instrument development, from electron-optical design through to fabrication, integration and experimental demonstration. You will work closely with two PhD candidates with complimentary roles: one will focus on experimental imaging, microscope characterization, and establishing the imaging methodology, while the other will develop computational imaging approaches and apply them to surface science. You will also work closely with the PI and an electron-optics technician supporting the project.
A central challenge is to develop compact electron-optical components that can separate the desired coherent backscattered-electron signal from the primary beam and direct it towards a dedicated detector. You will design and characterize these components, coordinate their fabrication and integration, and lead the commisioning and optimization of the experimental instrument.
Your work will span electron-optical design, electromagnetic and ray-tracing simulations, MEMS and nanofabrication, vacuum technology, detector integration and experimental microscopy. Working with the experimental-imaging PhD candidate, you will establish the performance of the instrument and the conditions needed to acquire high-quality diffraction data. You will also work with computational-imaging PhD candidate to connect the experimental measurements to reconstruction and imaging methods.
The position offers substantial scope to shape the technical direction of the project and to develop new instrumentation from concept through to experimental demonstration. You will have access to a new high-vacuum SEM acquired primarily for BEAMSurf, together with the broader electron microscopy infrastructure of the department.
This position is particularly suited to candidates with a background in electron optics, charged-particle optics, electron microscopy, electromagnetic simulation or scientific instrumentation. Experience with MEMS, nanofabrication, vacuum systems, detector technology or experimental microscopy is valuable. We are also interested in candidates who have developed complex experimental instrumentation in adjacent fields and are motivated to apply their expertise to electron microscopy.
Research Environment:
You will join the Curious Beams Lab, led by Dr. Georgios Varnavides, within the Microscopy and Instrumentation Techniques (MInT) cluster of the Department of Imaging Physics at TU Delft, Applied Sciences.
The MInT cluster brings together multiple research groups working across electron microscopy, from semiconductor inspection and metrology, to cryogenic electron microscopy for biological samples. The cluster has access to state-of-the-art field-emission SEMs and FIB-SEMS, with a new microscope being acquired primarily for this project.
More broadly, the ImPhys department provides an interdisciplinary environment spanning multiple imaging modalities, wavelengths, and length scaels, including extreme ultraviolet imaging, optical super-resolution, ultrasound and MRI, as-well as AI-based medical imaging.
 Job requirements 
We are looking for a curious and motivated researcher who wants to develop new experimental capabilities at the intersection of electron optics, instrumentation and imaging science.
You have:
 A PhD degree in physics, applied physics, electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, materials science, or a closely related field.

 Experience with numerical simulation, scientific programming or electromagnetic modelling is valuable.
