Are you excited about shaping the urban water systems of the future? Join us in a Dutch research project where your analysis of urban water system innovations will support decision-making. 
 Job description 
European water systems face increasing pressures from climate change, urbanization, ageing infrastructure, and stricter environmental requirements. At the same time, new hybrid urban water management approaches combining nature-based solutions and conventional gray infrastructure bring opportunities to improve system performance and adaptability. However, significant uncertainties remain regarding the environmental, economic, and societal implications of these innovations, limiting the ability of technology developers, utilities, planners, and policymakers to make responsible decisions about their development and implementation.
In this position you will investigate hybrid urban water innovations, which combe green and grey water infrastructure, seeking to anticipate the potential societal and environmental impacts associated to them. For that, you will integrate Value Sensitive Design (VSD) and ex-ante sustainability assessment within the Horizon Europe project RESILIENT-FLOWS. Therefore, this position involves two parts: Part a focuses on how stakeholders perceive urban water innovations, identifying how values such as sustainability and resilience, should be integrated in their design and implementation. For this, you are expected to develop and analyze stakeholder engagement activities (e.g. interviews, participatory workshops), and coordinate partners to conduct them across multiple European pilot sites. Part b focuses on an ex-ante Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) approach to assess the environmental impacts of hybrid urban water innovations in selected case studies from the RESILIENT-FLOWS project. Depending on your interests, you may focus more on part a or b above, however the position requires you to engage in both. The results from your research will serve as key inputs to decision-support tools developed within the RESILIENT-FLOWS consortium, enabling utilities, planners, and policymakers to evaluate alternative innovations for climate-resilient urban water management.
Your main responsibilities will include:
 Designing and coordinating stakeholder engagement activities, such as stakeholder interviews and focus groups
 Analyze how values such as resilience and sustainability could be taken into account in technology assessment and decision-making
 Apply ex-ante Life Cycle Assessment methodologies for emerging water infrastructure solutions
 Support project partners on the integration of stakeholder insights and sustainability assessment results into broader assessment and decision-support frameworks
 Publishing research findings in leading international journals and presenting results at scientific conferences
 Contributing to project deliverables and collaborating with academic and non-academic partners across Europe
You will become part of a multi-disciplinary team and collaborate closely with researchers working on nature-based solutions, water treatment technologies, digital twins, amongst others. This position offers a unique opportunity to help shape emerging approaches for integrating sustainability assessment and responsible innovation in the design of future climate-resilient water systems. In this position you will be working closely with researchers, utilities, municipalities, regulators, and technology providers across various European countries.
 Job requirements 
We are looking for a reseracher who has afinity with quantitative and qualitative methods, and who enjoys questioning assumptions, metrics, and indicators to better understand what a desirable innovation is.
For that, the vacancy's requirements are:
 PhD in Industrial Ecology, Sustainability Sciences, Technology Assessment, or a related field
 Proven experience with Life Cycle Assessment
 Proven experience with qualitative data gathering methods, such as interviewing and focus groups
 Interest in Urban Water Systems and Nature Based Solutions
 Ability to analyze both qualitative and quantitative data
 Excellent communication and scientific writting skills
 Ability to work independently while collaborating in interdisciplinary and international teams
 Excellent command of English
Good to Have
 Experience with ex-ante or prospective Life Cycle Assessment
 Background or experience with Urban Water Systems and Nature Based Solutions

For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. academictransfer:364660.description:
Are you a highly motivated and curious, and can you translate ecological expertise into successful designs of biodiverse, climate-resilient, aesthetically attractive and multifunctional green facades? Do you enjoy bridging fundamental ecological knowledge with practical applications? Then Wageningen University & Research offers an exciting opportunity for you. 
BIO-SKIN (Bio-Inspired Outer Surfaces to Kool, Insulate and Nurture) is developing bio-based, waste-derived, and circular façade systems that integrate plant growth. The project goal is to help bio-based facade panels that keep buildings cool, insulate, support biodiversity, and contribute to more sustainable urban environments. We work in a team of people with backgrounds in design, materials, biomaterial chemistry, architecture, biology, engineering, sustainability, and the built environment.
In this position, you will investigate how plant-soil-insect interactions develop in ecosystems with shallow soils and translate these ecological insights into design principles for next-generation green façades. Your research will contribute to a better understanding of how ecological communities establish and function in constrained urban environments, while helping to develop façade systems that support biodiversity and ecosystem functioning.
As a PhD candidate, you will combine fundamental and applied research to develop innovative green façade concepts that enhance ecosystem complexity and deliver key ecosystem services, including thermal insulation, carbon sequestration, microclimate regulation, and habitat provision for insects and other arthropods. This involves designing and setting up mini-ecosystems in minimal soil/vertical environments at various Living/Field Lab locations, and monitoring their performance, biodiversity and impact for energy efficiency. You will design the façade-panel experiments in close collaboration with a postdoctoral researcher, analyse ecological and physiological data, and contribute to scientific publications.
The project offers a unique opportunity to connect ecology, ecophysiology, urban greening, and green façade design.
We are looking for a candidate who enjoys working in interdisciplinary teams. You will bring strong botanical expertise to a collaborative group of researchers, designers, and material developers, and partners from companies that produce green façades, jointly creating innovative green façade solutions that contribute to sustainable construction and healthier urban environments.
Your activities include:
 Investigating plant species performance, community assembly and plant-insect-soil interactions in shallow-substrate systems (drawing on insights from literature as well as field studies);
 Year-round monitoring at various Living/Field Lab locations on the impact of plant species for enhancing energy efficiency and biodiversity by green façade panels;
 Analysing ecological and ecophysiological datasets;
 Publishing results in peer-reviewed journals and presenting findings at scientific conferences;
 Collaborating with academic and non-academic partners to translate scientific insights into practical applications;
 Teaching in courses and supervise BSc and MSc students in biodiversity-themed research.
 You will work here 
The research is embedded within the Biosystematics Group and the Laboratory of Entomology You will be supervised by dr. ir. Casper Quist and Prof. Bregje Wertheim . As a member in the BIO-SKIN team you will work one day a week together with the other BIO-SKIN PhDs and Post-docs at the AMS institute in Amsterdam . In addition, you will be embedded in the PE&RC graduate school ( Home | PE&RC ), which will allow you to follow a wide variety of training courses and provide support during your academic journey.

REQUIREMENTS:
For this project, we are looking for an enthusiastic, highly motivated and curious PhD candidate, who can translate botanical and ecological expertise into successful designs of biodiverse, climate-resilient, aesthetically attractive and multifunctional green facades.
 You have or are: 
 A successfully completed MSc degree in forest- and nature conservation or biology
 Extensive knowledge of the Dutch flora, able to accurately identify plant species in the field
 A strong interest in ecological interactions, including relationships between plants, insects, and soil organisms
 Interest in and initial experience with interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary collaboration, and the ability to engage with stakeholders from diverse backgrounds, including design, engineering, education, and ecology.
 Excellent communication skills in Dutch and English and experience with teaching and scientific writing.
For this position your command of the English and Dutch language is expected to be at C1 level . Sometimes it is necessary to submit an internationally recognised Certificate of Proficiency in the English Language. More information can be found here .

CONTRACT: 18 months

Ben jij een techneut in hart en nieren? Zie jij het werk en ben je enthousiast om te zorgen dat de klus geklaard wordt? Werk je graag aan oplossingen en sta je voor goedwerkende installatie ? Kom ons team versterken en werk mee aan een optimale dienstverlening voor internationaal baanbrekend onderzoek! 
 Dit ga je doen 
 Je bent actief op de werkvloer voor het verrichten van verschillende technische werkzaamheden met als speciaal aandachtgebied Elektrotechniek.
 Je verhelpt storingen, voert reparaties uit en denkt mee aan oplossingen om het gebouw veilig te houden.
 Je hebt en onderhoudt contacten met de eigenaar van het gebouw (KNAW) onderaannemers en leverancier.
 Je draait mee in het dienstenrooster en hebt 1 week per 4 weken bereikbaarheidsdienst.
 Dit breng je mee 
 Je hebt theoretische èn praktische ervaring in de techniek, bij voorkeur in een laboratoriumomgeving op MBO/HBO werk/denkniveau.
 Je blijft rustig in hectische omstandigheden en in een drukke werkomgeving.
 Je bent creatief in het bedenken van oplossingen en hebt lef om suggesties te doen ter verbetering van de (technische) bedrijfsvoering en onderzoek.
 Je kunt goed communiceren in het Nederlands en Engels.
 Je staat sterk in je (werk)schoenen om de dagelijkse uitdagingen aan te gaan.
 Je draagt bij aan een gezellige en serieuze werksfeer in een klein team.
 Meer weten? 
Neem contact op met:
 Dennis Peek , Teamleider Technische Dienst – 030-2121800
 Carola de Nooijer , Hoofd Facilitaire Zaken c.nooijer@hubrecht.eu 
 Over het Hubrecht Instituut 
Het Hubrecht Instituut is een onderzoeksinstituut dat zich richt op ontwikkelings- en stamcelbiologie. Bij het instituut doen meer dan 20 onderzoeksgroepen fundamenteel en multidisciplinair onderzoek, zowel in gezonde systemen als in ziektemodellen. Het Hubrecht Instituut is onderdeel van de KNAW en bevindt zich op Utrecht Science Park, ‘de Uithof’. Sinds 2008 is het instituut geaffilieerd met het Universitair Medisch Centrum Utrecht om de vertaling van het onderzoek naar de kliniek te bevorderen. Het Hubrecht Instituut heeft een partnerschap met het European Molecular Biology Laboratory (EMBL). Het huidige technische team bestaat uit drie medewerkers met daarnaast ondersteuning van installatiebedrijf Kuijpers.
 Arbeidsvoorwaarden 
Het salaris bedraagt afhankelijk van opleiding en ervaring minimaal € 3.057,- en maximaal € 3.985,- bruto per maand bij een full time dienstverband (schaal 7 cao Nederlandse Universiteiten/KNAW) . Dit is exclusief 8% vakantiegeld, 8,3% eindejaarsuitkering, reiskostenvergoeding, internet- en thuiswerkvergoeding en pensioenopbouw bij het ABP.
De KNAW biedt haar medewerkers een uitstekend pakket aan secundaire arbeidsvoorwaarden. Een pakket dat voorziet in de verschillende behoeften die medewerkers afhankelijk van hun levensfase, levenswijze of loopbaanambities hebben. Zo is het mogelijk om door wekelijks twee uur per week extra te werken het aantal vakantiedagen van 29 tot 41 dagen per jaar (bij fulltime dienstverband) uit te breiden.
Voor een volledig overzicht van de arbeidsvoorwaarden wordt verwezen naar de webpagina: werken bij de KNAW .
 Het aanvragen van een VOG kan onderdeel uitmaken van de indiensttredingsprocedure .
 Diversiteit & Inclusie 
De KNAW acht een werkomgeving waarin iedereen zich welkom en gewaardeerd voelt van groot belang. Een werkomgeving waarin aandacht is voor individuele kwaliteit en waar ontwikkelmogelijkheden voorop staan. Samen streven we naar een inclusieve cultuur waarin we verschillen omarmen. We nodigen dan ook graag kandidaten uit die door hun achtergrond en ervaring hieraan een bijdrage willen leveren. Bij gelijke geschiktheid gaat de voorkeur uit naar de kandidaat die de diversiteit binnen de KNAW op deze wijze versterkt.
Acquisitie naar aanleiding van deze advertentie wordt niet op prijs gesteld.

We are looking for an enthusiastic equine veterinarian with extensive experience in equine reproduction to join our equine reproduction team at Utrecht University on a temporary basis. The position is available for four months, from February 15th till June 15th , as maternity leave cover for one of our colleagues.
 Your job 
As a veterinarian, you will join our dedicated equine reproduction team, which consists of five veterinarians (one ACT diplomate, three ECAR diplomates and one intern), three clinical assistants, three laboratory assistants, a secretary and a group of dedicated researchers.
Our team provides diagnosis and treatment for a wide range of reproductive conditions in mares and stallions. We offer a broad range of assisted reproductive technologies as clinical services, including embryo transfer and ovum pick-up (OPU).
During the breeding season, we inseminate approximately 300 mares, perform around 150 embryo flushes, and transfer approximately 850 embryos, including embryos produced through ICSI and subsequent freezing and thawing.
You must be able to work independently and have solid experience with all of the below described clinical activities, including:
 routine reproductive management of donor and recipient mares;
 monitoring and breeding management of mares inseminated with frozen semen;
 embryo flushing and transfer procedures;
The position also includes participation in out-of-hours duties, including routine weekend work (approximately 1 in 3 weekends) and assisting with obstetrical emergencies.

REQUIREMENTS:
We are looking for a veterinarian with solid clinical experience in equine reproduction, including assisted reproductive technologies. A postgraduate qualification in equine reproduction, such as a diploma from the European College of Animal Reproduction (ECAR) or the American College of Theriogenologists (ACT), is an advantage but is not essential. Your veterinary degree must be recognized by EU (European Union)-recognized institution.
The University Equine Clinic is committed to providing high-quality, efficient care and excellent service to our clients. You share these values, enjoy working as part of a multidisciplinary team and have strong communication skills.
You are registered in the Dutch Register of Veterinary Medical Practitioners (Diergeneeskunderegister) and are legally authorized to practice veterinary medicine in the Netherlands. If you obtained your veterinary degree abroad, you must complete the applicable recognition and registration procedure. For more information about the requirements and registration process, please visit the Information in English | Diergeneeskunderegister .

Welcome to Maastricht University! 
We have developed a new class of oncology drugs that exploit the tumour microenvironment for selective activation that target the NOTCH stem-cell pathway in cancer. We are looking for an ambitious postdoctoral researcher to establish their therapeutic potential in advanced in vivo cancer models. You will determine efficacy, mechanism of action and tumour-microenvironment responses, and investigate how these drugs can improve treatment when combined with standard-of-care therapies and immunotherapy.
 Postdoctoral Researcher – Preclinical Cancer Drug Development 
 Our goal: We are developing a new class of tumour-selective small-molecule drugs targeting the NOTCH pathway, designed to become activated only within the tumour microenvironment. By restricting drug activity to tumours, we aim to target treatment-resistant cancer cells while limiting exposure and toxicity in healthy tissues. Our initial disease focus is triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), where we will determine efficacy as monotherapy and in rational combinations with established cancer treatments. The broader objective is to establish a tumour-specific precision-oncology platform that can subsequently be applied to other difficult-to-treat cancers.
 Your colleagues: You will join the group of Marc Vooijs in the Radiotherapy department at Maastricht University and Maastro Radiation Institute, working in a multidisciplinary environment spanning basic and translational cancer biology, including expertise in stem cell biology, tumour metabolomics and vesicle biology and primary (patient) tissue culture models. You will collaborate with scientists and clinicians and contribute to a programme designed to bridge academic discovery to preclinical drug development. This is a 3-year Dutch Cancer Society (Alpe d’Huzes/KWF-funded) project starting on 01-01-2027.
 What you do 
 Design, perform and analyse in vivo breast-cancer studies, using immune-competent TNBC models.
 Establish drug dose, schedule and treatment conditions for drug-combination strategies, including chemotherapy, radiotherapy and immunotherapy.
 Quantify tumour response, tolerability and survival, and relate these to pharmacokinetics, tumour-selective drug activation and target engagement.
 Characterise treatment-induced changes in the tumour microenvironment, including tumour, vascular and immune responses, using molecular, histological and imaging approaches.
 Identify and validate pharmacodynamic and response biomarkers to support patient stratification and clinical translation.
 Communicate results through project meetings, scientific presentations and high-quality publications and contribute scientifically to subsequent translational studies and funding applications.
 Support some teaching activities related to Oncology
 Are you ready to set the course for the years ahead? Then we’d love to meet you. 
 What you bring 
We are looking for a motivated biomedical scientist who wants to use advanced cancer models to translate innovative biology into new therapeutic strategies. Do you recognise yourself in this?
 PhD in cancer biology, with a demonstrated track record of peer-reviewed publications in a relevant research area.
 Strong hands-on experience within vivo cancer models is essential, including experimental design, tumour-response assessment and tissue collection. A valid Article 9 qualification or equivalent is required.
 A strong interest in translational oncology, innovation and preclinical drug development is essential.
 Experience with the tumour immune microenvironment and/or immuno-oncology is preferred.
 Experience with molecular and -omics analysis of tumours is preferred, including transcriptomic, single-cell, spatial or related approaches and their integration with in vivo treatment response.
 Experience with combination treatments, pharmacology/PK-PD or radiotherapy is an advantage; Article 5B or equivalent irradiation certification is preferred.
 What we offer 
At Maastricht University, you’ll work in an international, open, and engaged environment. We offer:
 A 12-month contract (1,0 FTE) with the prospect of a two-year extension.
 A gross monthly salary between €3.706 and €5.760 (based on full-time employment of 38 hours per week). 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus.
 29 vacation days (based on full-time), four additional days off (Carnival Monday and Tuesday, Good Friday, and Liberation Day), and the possibility to accrue up to 12 extra days through compensation hours.
 A close-knit community of colleagues to collaborate and grow with.
 A solid pension plan via ABP, company fitness schemes, and access to various university sports facilities.
 An inspiring work environment in the heart of Europe.

FHML is committed to health in the broadest sense: from molecule to human, and from healthcare to prevention. We train healthcare professionals and researchers th

academictransfer:364679.description:
Faculty:  Faculty of Veterinary Medicine Department:  Department Biomolecular Health Sciences Hours per week:  36 to 40 Application deadline:  31 October 2026
PhD position in a novel cell secretome-based therapeutics for osteoarthritis 
 Faculty: Faculty of Veterinary Medicine
 Department: Department of Biomolecular Health Sciences
 Hours per week: 36 to 40
 Application deadline: 31 October 2026
 Your job
 This PhD project will tackle key challenges in developing new therapies based on Extracellular Vesicles(EV)-enriched scretomes. The aim of the research is to develop innovative technologies that can be used to monitor batch-to-batch consistency of EV-based therapeutics, decipher EV- molecular cargo - functional relationships, and identify disease-related signatures in blood and synovial fluid from patients with osteoarthritis. Overall, the project aims to provide new insights and tools for the development of safe, effective, and consistent EV-based therapies.
 In this project hands-on analytical wet-lab experiments, including cell biological analyses, multi-omics mass spectrometry and nanoparticle analyses of EV samples, production batches and patients samples, as well as computational methods including AI-enhanced analyses are equally important. Throughout the project, you will develop core skills in fundamental cell biology and metabolism research, in mass spectrometry and integrated multi-omics analysis, and gain insights in the mechanism of action of EV-enriched cell secretome therapy in osteoarthritis. As part of an EU-funded RIA project in a 10-partner consortium including industry partnerships, you will collaborate with partner institutes in The Netherlands and abroad,  and secondments are possible. 
 Your qualities
 A relevant Master’s degree in Biology, Biomedical sciences, Biopharmaceutical Sciences, Biochemistry, or a related field, and a solid background in one or more of the following areas: cell biology, metabolism, immune regulation or joint biology;
 A strong interest in fundamental cell biology and hands-on analytical wet-lab techniques;
 Enthusiasm for nanoparticle analysis and the application of advanced technologies, such as high-resolution flow cytometry and optical fingerprinting;
 A strong interest in mass spectrometry and its applications in metabolomics, lipidomics, and proteomics. Experience with multi-omics analyses is an advantage;
 Basic proficiency in data analysis using R, Python, and/or Matlab, with a strong interest in computational methods, including AI-enhanced analyses;
 Excellent skills in writing and speaking English (C1 level);
 Interest in multidisciplinary and interdisciplinary research, reaching from fundamental to applied clinical research and from academic to industrial research;
 Ability to work as part of an interdisciplinary research consortium, with strong communication skills and interest to engage effectively with different groups (Academic & Clinical researchers, engineers, bio-informaticians and Industrial partners)
 Our offer
 a job for 12 months, with an extension to a total of four years upon a successful assessment in the first year, and with the specific intent that it results in a doctorate within this period;
 a working week of 36 - 40 hours and a gross monthly salary between €3.204 and €4.051 (salary scale P under the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities (CAO NU)). The salary is based on a 38-hour working week;
 8% holiday pay and 8.3% year-end bonus;
 a pension scheme, partially paid parental leave and flexible terms of employment based on the CAO NU.
 In addition to the terms of employment set out in our collective labour agreement, we offer attractive additional benefits, including opportunities for  personal and professional growth , flexible leave arrangements, and extra vacation days. Through the UU Terms of Employment Options Model, you can tailor your employment package to your needs. In this way, we encourage you to grow in what you do, both in your work and in your development. Read more about  our terms of employment .
 About us
 A better future for everyone. This ambition motivates our scientists in executing their leading research and inspiring teaching. At  Utrecht University , the various disciplines collaborate intensively towards major  strategic themes . Our focus is on Dynamics of Youth, Institutions for Open Societies, Life Sciences and Pathways to Sustainability.  Sharing science, shaping tomorrow .
 At the Faculty of Veterinary Medicine we train the veterinarians and researchers of the future, provide care for animals and conduct leading and societal relevant research. That is what we are good at. We see that the health and welfare of animals, humans and the environment are interconnected. By sharing our knowledge and working together, we make positive impact, both nationally and internationally. Our 1,500 students and 950 staff members inspire and strengthen each other. Our engagement connects us. The drive to, from an integral perspective, make the world a better place.
 The Department of Biomolecular Health Sciences consists of the Divisions of Pathology, Infectious Diseases & Immunology and the Division of Cell Biology, Metabolism and Cancer (CMC), and hosts the centralized research facilities: Centre for Cell Imaging, Flow Cytometry and Cell Sorting and the Metabolism Expertise Center. The research of the Division CMC aims to unravel mechanisms of intra- and extracellular communication of animal cells. This knowledge is used to prevent or to develop better treatments for non-communicable diseases in veterinary and human patients. The Cell Biology section, headed by prof. dr. Marca Wauben, aims to decipher fundamental principles of cell-derived vesicle(EV)-mediated communication in health and disease processes. This research spans from fundamental discovery to translational applications, and the development of cutting-edge technology and methodology for tailored EV-research solutions. Assistant Professor in Immune-Tumor Cell Communication 
Faculty: Faculty of Veterinary Medicine
Department: Department Biomolecular Health Sciences
 Assistant Professor in Immune-Tumor Cell Communication 
The Division of Cell Biology, Metabolism, & Cancer (CMC) is seeking an ambitious and collaborative cell biologist to establish an innovative, independent research line at the interface of intercellular communication and cancer immunology, and to contribute to teaching in cell biology. We are particularly interested in a researcher who will build strong interdisciplinary collaborations with clinical researchers and partners across Utrecht Science Park, and is keen to translate fundamental discoveries into biomedical impact.
The research of CMC aims to unravel mechanisms of intra- and extracellular communication of animal cells. This knowledge is used to prevent or to develop better treatments for non-communicable diseases such as cancer in veterinary and human patients. You will be embedded within the Cell Biology research group, which has an excellent track record in cell-derived extracellular vesicle (EV)-mediated communication.
As an Assistant Professor and Principal Investigator you will develop and lead an independent innovative research line focused on communication between tumor cells and immune cells, that complements and strengthens CMC’s scientific portfolio while fostering collaboration across veterinary and human clinical research groups. You will secure research funding, build and maintain strategic collaborations with academic, clinical and industrial partners, and supervise PhD candidates, postdoctoral researchers, and technical staff.
You will contribute to Cell Biology teaching within the Veterinary Medicine and Biomedical Sciences curricula. You should hold a University Teaching Qualification (BKO) or be willing to obtain this qualification during the first two years of appointment. Teaching tasks include lecturing, supervising practical courses, supervision of BSc and MSc students, as well as participation in course development. Teaching responsibilities will account for approximately 0.3 FTE, with the highest involvement during periods when courses are scheduled. Since most teaching is in Dutch, candidates not yet proficient in Dutch are expected to be willing to learn the language (support for this can be provided).

REQUIREMENTS:
A completed PhD in cancer immunology or extracellular vesicle (EV) biology, with experience in developing advanced in vitro cellular model systems;
 At least four years of relevant postdoctoral research experience, preferably including international research experience;
 A strong scientific track record, evidenced by scientific publications and successful acquisition of research grants;
 Experience in supervising master students, PhD candidates, technicians and/or postdocs;
 A vision for developing an independent research line that complements the current activities of the division of Cell Biology, Metabolism, and Cancer.
 Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively within interdisciplinary academic and translational research environments

academictransfer:364710.description:
The Royal Netherlands Institute of Southeast Asian and Caribbean Studies (KITLV) is looking for an enthusiastic early career post-doc researcher in the anthropology of marine nature conservation in Indonesia. The position is for 1 year, with the intention of extension with a second year, depending on performance.
 Your workplace 
The postdoc will apply ethnographic methods to study the governance of Marine Protected Areas (MPAs) in Eastern Indonesia, with a specific focus on the impact of tourism.
This project approaches MPAs as complex social-ecological institutions, in which ecological health, local livelihoods, governance, economic activities, and place-specific contestations of power, authority, and world views intersect. MPA governance involves a multitude of local, national and international actors and stakeholders, who have different views about the relationship between people and their marine environments. Tourism, in this context, is a double-edged sword. It may bring local groups in, allowing for alternative sources of MPA funding and livelihood strategies within a broader paradigm of sustainability and local agency, or it may drive stakeholders apart when the development of MPAs leads to exclusion of certain groups when economic opportunities are monopolized or appropriated, or fail to materialize.
The aim is to develop distinct local cases to analyse various understandings of the role of MPAs and the ways in which different forms of environmental knowledge clash or synergize in the context of marine conservation. Actively involving local academic and non-academic partners, the postdoc will study the nature of these tensions and interactions and how they might be overcome to produce more effective, just, and inclusive forms of MPA governance.
This position is part of a research project titled “TIDE-MPAs: Tourism Impact Dashboard for Social-Ecological-System Resilience in Marine Protected Areas.” This project is funded by the Dutch Research Council (NWO) and the Indonesian Ministry of Higher Education, Science, and Technology and led by Dr. Lisa Becking (Naturalis Biodiversity Center) and Beginer Subhan (IPB University). As a transdisciplinary and co-creative project, TIDE-MPAs seeks to synergize between marine science, social science, and practical work in marine conservation in Indonesia and the Caribbean. The postdoc will be the main researcher in a Work Package on local knowledge and authority in MPAs coordinated by Dr. David Kloos and Dr. Sikko Visscher (KITLV). They are also expected to work closely with the postdoc researcher/project coordinator at Naturalis Biodiversity Center, and to synergize with project staff in Indonesia and collaborating NGOs.
 What you will be doing 
Your key responsibilities will include:
 Carrying out autonomous ethnographic field research in one or more locations in Eastern Indonesia (specifically Maluku and/or West Papua).
 Leading at least two publications on the subject of local knowledge and governance in Marine Protected Areas.
 Supporting collaboration with key stakeholders in the broader project, including academic stakeholders, NGOs, and local partners.
 Contribute to an MPA tourism impact dashboard and tailored policy guidelines together with MPA managers, conservation professionals, and community leaders.
 Helping to organize and support joint fieldwork, workshops, consortium meetings and project events, together with the PIs and the coordinating Postdoc at Naturalis.
 Who we are looking for 
We are looking for a talented, enthusiastic and committed cultural or social anthropologist, or a social scientist with proven experience with ethnographic methods. You are grounded in, or have affinity with, the field(s) of environmental anthropology, political ecology, and/or Science & Technology Studies. You are able to work autonomously and independently, but you also know when to seek help when necessary. You enjoy collaborating with colleagues, coordinators, and external partners and are active in maintaining your network. You have an open mind toward other scientific disciplines and non-academic perspectives and concerns.
 What you will be contributing 
 A PhD-degree in anthropology, political ecology, or a related discipline;
 Experience with carrying out fieldwork in Indonesia;
 Fluency or proficiency in Indonesian language skills;
 Excellent English speaking and writing skills;
 A track record of scholarly publications;
 The ability to take initiatives and solve problems;
 Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with an open mind for different approaches and perspectives;
 A willingness to travel overseas for extended periods.
A demonstrated experience with the practical field of marine nature conservation and relevant networks in that field are considered advantages. academictransfer:364714.description:
As an intern at the University Clinic for Equine Health, you will work together with dedicated specialists, residents, and students to deliver high-quality veterinary care for horses and other equids.
 Important: Due to the short starting date this vacancy is for EU applicants only 
 Your job 
Are you a veterinarian looking to deepen your knowledge of equine medicine within an academic environment that upholds high clinical standards? An internship at the University Equine Clinic offers a unique opportunity to gain intensive practical experience, provide clinical instruction, and work with state-of-the-art facilities alongside a multidisciplinary team of specialists. We have two positions available for the spring of 2027. Depending on your area of interest, the focus of your internship will be either Internal Medicine or Orthopedics/Surgery/Anesthesia.
 Therefore, please clearly indicate your area of interest—Internal Medicine or Surgery/Anesthesia—in your motivation letter. 
As an intern, you will primarily work during the day within the team corresponding to your chosen area of interest. Additionally, following an initial orientation period, you will be deployed across all departments (Surgery, Anesthesia, Internal Medicine, Reproduction, and Ambulatory Clinic) during evening and night shifts. You will also assist in other departments during the day when necessary.
Following the daily handover by the specialists, you will play a central role in the operational functioning of the Internal Medicine or Surgery/Anesthesia department. You will also play an important role in guiding and supervising Master’s students, both during clinical work and within clinical education.
Your duties will include:
 Active participation in stable rounds, consultations, and the care of hospitalized patients.
 Performing routine clinical procedures, such as placing IV lines, catheterization, administering medication, and changing dressings
 Coordinating and managing the logistics of diagnostic procedures, including laboratory samples and diagnostic imaging.
 Supervising Veterinary Medicine master's students in clinical skills and patient care
 During evening and night shifts, you are responsible for the initial assessment and stabilization of emergency patients, the treatment of hospitalized patients, and the supervision of students on duty
We have state-of-the-art facilities at our disposal, including extensive hospitalization units and advanced imaging technologies such as MRI, CT, and diagnostic radiology. In addition, there is an extensive program of groundbreaking clinical research.

REQUIREMENTS:
You are eligible to work as a veterinarian in The Netherlands. Before applying please check: https://www.diergeneeskunderegister.nl/information-in-english 
 Upload the document of proof that you are eligible to work as a veterinarian in the Netherlands, with your application
 You are a veterinarian with an interest in and experience with horses.
 You are highly motivated to further develop yourself in the field of equine medicine.
 Practical experience is an advantage, but not a strict requirement.
 You have a proactive, positive, enthusiastic and flexible attitude.
 You have good communication skills.

What you will be doing
You will support the development of the Rewilding Expertise Centre based at the NIOO-KNAW in Wageningen. The Rewilding Expertise Centre aims to make knowledge on rewilding available publicly. You will assist in setting up a website with information on rewilding science, practice and education. Therefore, you collect, structure and prepare information for publication on the website.
In more detail, you will:
Search for existing information on rewilding, including rewilding organisations, scientific products, courses, educational videos, meetings, events etc.,;
Judge whether the information is useful and reliable;
Document found information in a clear and structured database;
Synthesize found information in logical categories including science, practice and education and place the information on the website in a clear structural and attractive way;
Contact (inter-) national institutions and individuals to ask permission to provide links to their work on the website in Dutch and in English
What we are looking for
We are looking for a colleague with enthusiasm for and affinity with rewilding and the following skills:
Knowledge of rewilding science, education and rewilding networks through education or previous work experience
Experience in organizing diverse data sources, ensuring accuracy and handling the database management
A proactive attitude with the ability to identify opportunities and propose solutions;
Strong in open communication with various stakeholders and good English and Dutch speaking and writing skills;
Creative ideas to make the information accessible on a website
You should have an EU/EEA nationality or already have a valid visa and working permit for the EU for this position.
What do we offer?
A position for on average 1-2 days per week for 12 months, depending on the number of hours per week. The position is a 0-hour contract for which the hours can be distributed over the week.
Your workplace
You will be based at the department of Terrestrial Ecology (TE) at NIOO-KNAW, consisting of a dynamic, interactive and collaborative group of researchers from diverse backgrounds. You will share an office space within the department. You will closely collaborate with colleagues from NIOO-KNAW and Wageningen University who collaborate in the Rewilding Expertise Centre through the special chair in Rewilding Ecology of prof. Liesbeth Bakker.
More information
Please contact: Liesbeth Bakker, Senior Researcher, l.bakker@nioo.knaw.nl.  More information about the Netherlands Institute of Ecology (NIOO-KNAW) and the department of Terrestrial Ecology can be found at the website:
http://www.nioo.knaw.nl
Application procedure
For the application, please include a cover letter summarizing motivation and experience with rewilding, and a CV. Deadline for application is 29 October 2026. Applications received later than this date will not be considered. Interviews are scheduled for the 6th of November 2026.
About NIOO
The Netherlands Institute of Ecology (NIOO) is a national research institute of the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences (KNAW). At NIOO we perform ecological research on biodiversity, climate change and sustainable use of land and water. We stimulate ecological research in the Netherlands and share our ecological knowledge with society. Everyone in our organisation is passionate about contributing to a sustainable world from their own area of expertise.

Depending on education and experience the minimum salary is € 3.202 and the maximum salary is € 4.159 gross per month for a full-time appointment (scale 7 cao Nederlandse Universiteiten/KNAW). This is exclusive of 8% vacation allowance, 8.3% year-end bonus, travel allowance, internet allowance, home working allowance and pension accrual with ABP.
The KNAW offers its staff an excellent package of secondary benefits. A package that meets the different needs of employees depending on their stage of life, lifestyle or career ambitions. For example, by working an extra two hours a week, it is possible to increase the number of days off from 29 to 41 days a year (with full-time employment).
For a complete overview of the terms of employment, please refer to the web page:
werken bij de KNAW
.

Diversity & Inclusion
The KNAW considers a working environment in which everyone feels welcome and appreciated of great importance. We would therefore like to invite candidates who want to contribute to this through their background and experience. EQUITY-AF is a Horizon Europe-funded project that aims to improve the diagnosis and treatment of atrial fibrillation by addressing differences related to biological sex and sociocultural gender factors.
The project will develop a sex-specific risk prediction tool that integrates hormonal, genetic and social factors. This approach aims to improve diagnostic technologies and inform more effective treatment strategies for people with atrial fibrillation.
The project brings together experts from several European countries. At Amsterdam UMC, the work package on sociocultural gender determinants is coordinated by Dr. David Doyle at the Department of Medical Psychology, Amsterdam UMC, location VUmc. You will work closely with Dr. Doyle's research group and collaborate with an international, interdisciplinary network of researchers in cardiovascular health.
As a postdoctoral researcher, you will investigate the social and cultural factors that influence gender and cardiovascular health, with a particular focus on women's health. You will contribute to research within EQUITY-AF and have opportunities to develop your own research interests in social factors related to gender and health.
The position is available for three years, with the possibility of renewal following a successful review at the end of the first year.
Your activities include:
 Contributing to research studies developed as part of the EQUITY-AF project.
 Investigating sociocultural gender determinants in cardiovascular health.
 Collaborating with researchers from different disciplines and European institutions.
 Developing your own research interests in gender, health and social factors.

REQUIREMENTS:
You are an independent and motivated researcher with a strong interest in gender and health. You are keen to contribute to research that improves women's health and healthcare.
You also have:
 A PhD in a field relevant to gender and health, particularly cardiovascular health, such as psychology, neuroscience or public health, or be close to completing your PhD in one of these fields.
 Excellent written and spoken English communication skills.
 Experience with mixed-methods research in the sociomedical sciences (desirable).
 Experience with machine learning approaches to health data (desirable).

academictransfer:364730.description:
Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic progressive demyelinating disease of the central nervous system characterized by neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration. Current disease-modifying therapies are non-curative and do not reverse progression. On the level of tissue, MS lesion progression is prevented by remyelination, a natural regeneration process after demyelination that is crucial for functional recovery and neuronal survival. In this project, you will build further on our research aimed at deciphering MS lesion evolution by decoding region-distinct differences in cellular signaling and regulatory networks. You will generate and integrate global proteomic and phosphoproteomic signatures of MS lesion rims and cores in parallel with region-specific long-read RNA sequencing. This will allow you to link changes in signaling networks and RNA- and protein isoforms to molecular processes involved in lesion expansion and lesion transition. This multi-omics data approach will further the functional disentangling of molecular and cellular pathways underlying ongoing demyelination in lesion rims and successful remyelination or remyelination failure in lesion cores. The novel layer of changes in RNA and protein diversity will advance our understanding of MS and may thereby identify novel therapeutic targets. 
The position is funded by Stichting MS Research.

REQUIREMENTS:
A junior Postdoc with a PhD degree in molecular cell biology or a related field. We are looking for an enthusiastic, highly motivated and talented postdoctoral researcher with affinity for neuroscience and a strong scientific drive. Expertise with bioinformatic analysis is an advantage. Furthermore, you will need a flexible working attitude, team player mentality, good oral and written communication skills in English, and a result-driven and pro-active attitude.

academictransfer:364732.description:
Post-doc Position on Multi-omics in Hereditary Fibrinogen Disorders: Bridging the Genotype-Phenotype Gap
Join the Fibromics consortium! 
We are looking for a highly motivated post-doc to join the proteomics lab at Sanquin Research, Amsterdam, the Netherlands within the international Fibromics consortium sponsored by an Innovation Grant from the European Hematology Association.
Patients with hereditary fibrinogen disorders are clinically challenging due to unpredictable bleeding and thrombosis conditions. Current diagnostic tools do not identify patients at risk, and management remains largely opinion-based. This project aims to bridge expertise in fibrinogen biology, clinical phenotyping, mass spectrometry-based proteomics, and fibrin network analysis to define the phenotype-specific molecular signatures underlying congenital fibrinogen disorders. You will combine plasma, fibrin clot, and platelet proteomics with protein variant mapping, fibrinogen proteolysis assays, fibrin network structure analysis, genetic data, and clinical characteristics from a well-established clinical cohort of individuals with congenital fibrinogen disorders.
We offer a diverse and multidisciplinary research environment. The Fibromics consortium brings together large international patient cohorts and leading researchers in hemostasis, proteomics, bioinformatics, and clinical hematology, including Dr. Alessandro Casini (Geneva, Switzerland), Prof. Dr. Giancarlo Castaman (Florence, Italy), Dr. Saskia Schols (Nijmegen, the Netherlands), and Dr. Tomáš Šimurda (Martin, Slovakia). You will work alongside fundamental researchers, clinicians, data scientists, and specialized laboratory staff, offering a unique combination of patient care, state-of-the-art techniques, and insight into the molecular mechanisms of congenital fibrinogen disorders.
 Candidate Profile 
We are looking for a candidate who is eager to excel as an independent researcher while contributing to a collaborative team-science environment, working closely with clinicians, proteomics specialists, and computational scientists, as well as fellow PhD and post-doctoral researchers.
Specifically, we request:
 Recent PhD degree in a related field.
 Advanced expertise in mass spectrometry-based proteomics, programming (e.g., R, Python), and statistical analysis.
 Analytical thinking, strong interest in protein biology, and enthusiasm for biomedical data integration, including clinical and laboratory data, using machine learning and AI.
 Expertise in genomics and molecular biology is an advantage.
 Motivation to work in a collaborative, interdisciplinary research environment and excellent communication and writing skills in English.
 What We Offer 
 A post-doctoral position for the duration of at least 2 years within a highly collaborative and internationally visible research program.
 Mentorship from leading experts in hemostasis, proteomics, and data science.
 Advanced analytical technologies, including state-of-the-art mass spectrometry-based proteomics, multi-omics, and computational platforms.
 Exposure to cutting-edge clinical research and contribution to large cohort studies of patients with congenital bleeding disorders.
 Participation in national and international conferences and scientific networks.
 Application 
Please submit your CV, academic transcripts, a motivation letter, and contact details for at least two references.
 More Information 
Are you interested and do you have questions about the positions? Please reach out to Dr. Maartje van den Biggelaar, Head of Proteomics Laboratory, Sanquin Amsterdam ( m.vandenbiggelaar@sanquin.nl ).

academictransfer:364737.description:
In Nederland zullen naar schatting in 2050 meer dan een half miljoen mensen dementie hebben. De maatschappelijke impact is groot en neemt toe door de vergrijzing. Daarom is het belangrijk om dementie beter te begrijpen, te behandelen en uiteindelijk te voorkomen.
Sommige mensen worden juist extreem oud zonder dementie. Hoe kan dat en wat kunnen we van hen leren? Om deze vragen te beantwoorden, is het 100-plus onderzoek gestart bij de afdeling Humane Genetica, in samenwerking met Alzheimercentrum Amsterdam van Amsterdam UMC.
Voor dit onderzoek bezoeken we mensen van 100 jaar en ouder thuis voor neuropsychologisch onderzoek en het afnemen van vragenlijsten. Ook nemen we bloed af en verzamelen we verschillende biomaterialen. Een groot deel van de deelnemers heeft aangegeven de hersenen na overlijden te willen doneren voor wetenschappelijk onderzoek. Hierdoor kunnen we onder meer onderzoeken in hoeverre Alzheimer-eiwitten aanwezig zijn in de hersenen van mensen die tijdens hun leven geen dementie hadden.
Inmiddels nemen meer dan 500 mensen van 100 jaar en ouder zonder dementie deel aan het onderzoek. Met hun bijdrage krijgen we meer inzicht in de factoren die beschermen tegen dementie en in de mechanismen die een rol spelen bij gezond ouder worden.
Meer informatie over de wetenschappelijke achtergrond vind je in de publicatie: The 100-plus Study of Dutch cognitively healthy centenarians: rationale, design and cohort description (Holstege et al., European Journal of Epidemiology , 2018).
Als research technician ben je verantwoordelijk voor laboratoriumwerkzaamheden en de praktische coördinatie van onderzoeksprojecten. Je zorgt ervoor dat experimenten zorgvuldig worden uitgevoerd, materialen beschikbaar zijn en onderzoeksgegevens volledig worden vastgelegd. Daarbij werk je zelfstandig en stem je regelmatig af met collega's en externe samenwerkingspartners.
Je houdt je onder andere bezig met:
 Het zelfstandig plannen en uitvoeren van laboratoriumwerkzaamheden, waaronder immunohistochemie (IHC), het snijden en verwerken van gefixeerd en in paraffine ingebed (FFPE) en ingevroren hersenweefsel en het werken met plasma.
 Het coördineren van onderzoeksprojecten en de bijbehorende logistiek. Je richt praktische workflows in, organiseert het transport van materialen naar samenwerkingspartners en coördineert de verwerking en opslag van humaan hersenweefsel in samenwerking met de Nederlandse Hersenbank en de biobank van Amsterdam UMC.
 Het organiseren en bewaken van de dagelijkse voortgang van projecten. Je bestelt op tijd de benodigde materialen, stemt af met interne en externe betrokkenen, signaleert praktische knelpunten en zoekt naar oplossingen. Ook ben je een aanspreekpunt voor de projecten.
 Het nauwkeurig documenteren en administreren van onderzoekswerkzaamheden. Je houdt labjournaals, samplegegevens, protocollen en projectadministratie bij, zodat onderzoekswerkzaamheden en materialen volledig traceerbaar blijven.

REQUIREMENTS:
Je werkt nauwkeurig en zelfstandig en vindt het leuk om laboratoriumwerk te combineren met het organiseren en coördineren van onderzoeksprojecten. Je neemt initiatief, houdt overzicht en werkt graag samen met collega's en andere betrokkenen.
Daarnaast breng je het volgende mee:
 Een afgeronde HLO-opleiding, een professionele bachelor in biotechnologie, een master in biomedische of biologische wetenschappen of een vergelijkbare relevante opleiding.
 Ervaring met algemene laboratoriumwerkzaamheden en het zorgvuldig uitvoeren van standaardprotocollen. Je bent gemotiveerd om nieuwe technieken en protocollen te leren.
 Affiniteit met humaan lichaamsmateriaal en basiskennis van moleculaire en cellulaire biologie en/of neurowetenschappen.
 Een proactieve, zelfstandige en praktische werkhouding, met goede organisatorische vaardigheden en het vermogen om werkzaamheden en meerdere projecten te plannen, coördineren en prioriteren.
 Goede communicatieve vaardigheden en een uitstekende beheersing van het Nederlands en Engels, zowel mondeling als schriftelijk. Je werkt prettig samen met collega's en interne en externe samenwerkingspartners.
Voor deze functie is een hepatitis B-vaccinatie vereist. Heb je deze vaccinatie al, vermeld dit dan in je cv of brief. Zo niet, dan kun je de vaccinatie na je start bij Amsterdam UMC behalen.

Ben jij gepassioneerd over open science en open onderzoek? Heb je praktijkervaring met het implementeren van open onderzoekspraktijken in de verschillende stadia van onderzoek doen? Lees verder en solliciteer!
De Erasmus Universiteit Rotterdam (EUR) is op zoek naar een Open Science-adviseur om het bewustzijn en de toepassing van open science-praktijken onder onderzoekers en medewerkers van Professional Services te vergroten. Je komt te werken bij Engagement & Research Services (ERS) – een dynamische afdeling binnen Professional Services bij de EUR – en wordt onderdeel van het Open & Responsible Science (ORS)-team, bestaande uit community- en engagementmanagers, data stewards en ethische professionals, om onze ambitieuze doelstelling mee te helpen realiseren: open science de standaardwerkwijze bij de EUR maken.
 Functieomschrijving 
Je belangrijkste taken en verantwoordelijkheden zijn de volgende:
 Advies bij onderzoek 
 Informeren en adviseren van academici, medewerkers van Professional Services en management over hoe open science academische en maatschappelijke impact kan vergroten. Voorbeeld : je wordt gevraagd om feedback te geven op het open science-beleid van een faculteit.
 Informeren en adviseren van academici bij het creëren, beschrijven, publiceren, gebruiken en archiveren van resultaten van wetenschappelijk onderzoek en impactactiviteiten in overeenstemming met de principes van open science. Voorbeeld : je voorziet een onderzoeker van de benodigde informatie om te starten met zijn of haar eerste preregistratie, of om de principes van open science toe te passen op zijn of haar engaged onderzoeksproject.
 Je adviseert en ondersteunt academici en grant officers over hoe open science op een organische manier in subsidieaanvragen kan worden geïntegreerd. Voorbeeld : je bespreekt met een NWO Vidi-subsidieaanvrager en een grant officer welke (projectspecifieke) informatie over open science in de subsidieaanvraag kan worden opgenomen.
 Onderwijs 
 Bijdragen aan het verbeteren van onderwijs en training op het gebied van open science door het ontwikkelen van cursussen en workshops, deze up to date te houden en/of deze cursussen en workshops zelf te geven. Voorbeeld : je werkt de huidige EUR ORS MOOC bij in nauwe samenwerking met een projectcoördinator, de coördinator van het educatieve ORS-framework en andere experts binnen en buiten de EUR.
 Samenwerking 
 Je werkt samen met andere afdelingen bij ERS (Research Management, Grant Support, en Innovation & Partnerships), afdelingen binnen de EUR (bijvoorbeeld de bibliotheek, IT), de Hub for Impactful & Engaged Research en strategische programma’s (bijv. Erkennen & Waarderen) om het bewustzijn te vergroten van, ondersteuning te faciliteren op, en institutionele activiteiten (direct en indirect) met betrekking tot open science op elkaar af te stemmen. Voorbeeld : je helpt bij het organiseren van een evenement over hoe open science de diversificatie van academische loopbaantrajecten kan ondersteunen, bijvoorbeeld door te brainstormen over specifieke onderwerpen die hiervoor van belang zijn en door interne/externe sprekers uit relevante netwerken hiervoor uit te nodigen.
 Je adviseert over en helpt bij het formuleren van de ORS-ambities voor de EUR, in nauwe samenwerking met academisch en Professional Services medewerkers, evenals met faculteits- en uitvoerend management.
 Overige 
 Er is daarnaast enige ruimte om aan onderzoek te doen, om zo op de hoogte te blijven van, en bij te dragen aan (inter)nationale discussies over open science. Voorbeeld : je bent medeauteur van een opiniestuk over nieuwe manieren om burgers te betrekken bij het gezamenlijk formuleren van onderzoeksvragen die zowel voor academici als voor het bredere publiek relevant zijn.

REQUIREMENTS:
Je herkent jezelf in de volgende beschrijving:
 Je hebt een academische achtergrond (minimaal MSc/MA)
 Je onderschrijft de waarden van open science en ondersteunt de praktische toepassing ervan
 Je hebt praktijkervaring met diverse vormen van open science (bijv. open data, open code, maatschappelijke betrokkenheid)
 Je communiceert effectief en overtuigend met mensen uit verschillende (academische) SSH-disciplines en in diverse stadia van hun loopbaan, van promovendus tot decaan
 Dankzij je netwerkvaardigheden kun je bruggen slaan en conflicten oplossen om een gemeenschappelijk doel te bereiken
 Je bent nauwgezet (bijvoorbeeld bij het adviseren over, medeopstellen en beoordelen van beleid)
 Je spreekt vloeiend Engels (minimaal CEFR-niveau C1)
Aanbevelingen (ervaring op de volgende gebieden is een pluspunt):
 Je bent gepromoveerd in een discipline waarin open science actief wordt bediscussieerd (bijvoorbeeld psychologie)
 Je hebt ervaring met het onderwijzen van de waarden, praktijken en/of hulpmiddelen op het gebied van open science (bijvoorbeeld door middel van het geven van lezingen of workshops)
 Je hebt (mee)geschreven aan documenten (bijvoorbeeld blogposts, opiniestukken, wetenschappelijke artikelen, beleidsdocumenten) over open science
 Je leest Nederlands (minimaal B1)

academictransfer:364765.description:
Post-doctoral Researcher: Agent-Based Modelling of Pleistocene Landscape Connectivity in Europe 
 The Department of World Archaeology, Faculty of Archaeology, Leiden University, is looking for a temporary Postdoctoral Researcher to investigate prehistoric landscape connectivity and human movement across Europe using agent-based modelling. The project is part of the NWO-VICI project Neandertal Legacy, awarded to Prof. dr. M.A. Soressi, which investigates the contacts and interactions between Neanderthals and early modern humans in Late Pleistocene Europe through an interdisciplinary archaeological approach. The successful candidate will implement the movement modelling framework developed by Coco & Iovita ( 2025 PLOS’one) to reconstruct the geography-driven movement architecture of Europe and adjacent regions during the Middle and Late Pleistocene. By simulating autonomous agents that make only local least-cost movement decisions, using Leiden University's ALICE High Performance Computing (HPC) cluster, the project will identify movement corridors, bottlenecks, and barriers that emerge solely from landscape structure. The central research question is: if hominins moved across Europe constrained primarily by palaeogeography, what large-scale patterns of movement and connectivity would naturally emerge? Predicted movement pathways will subsequently be compared with the archaeological record to evaluate how geography shaped patterns of human dispersal and landscape connectivity through time.
 What you will do 
 Adapt the Coco & Iovita (2025) agent-based movement model to reconstruct prehistoric landscape connectivity across Europe.
 Build and process palaeoenvironmental and geospatial datasets (including digital elevation models, palaeocoastlines, river networks and glacier extents) for multiple Middle and Late Pleistocene time slices using GIS and R.
 Run computationally intensive agent-based simulations on Leiden University's ALICE High Performance Computing (HPC) cluster and analyse predicted movement corridors and connectivity patterns.
 Compare predicted movement corridors and connectivity networks with archaeological datasets to evaluate the extent to which landscape structure alone explains observed patterns of prehistoric human dispersal.
 Produce reproducible datasets and code, and contribute to one scientific publication and one scientific presentation.
 Engage with the Faculty community through discussion meetings, journal clubs, and other events.
 Where you will work 
The future of the past begins at Leiden University. The Faculty of Archaeology is internationally leading for its research, home to a broad array of specializations and notable for its strong connection between teaching and research. Home to over 500 students in the multidisciplinary world of Archaeology, the Faculty, and its researchers from all areas of the archaeological field, determine the future of archaeological research. More information about our university and our faculty can be found at: https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/archaeology 
The successful candidate will join the Department of World Archaeology . They will be supervised by Prof. dr. M.A. Soressi and by Dr. E. Coco, Researcher at the Interdisciplinary Center for Archaeology and Evolution of Human Behaviour (ICArEHB) at the University of Algarve in Faro, Portugal.
They will work as a post-doctoral researcher for 0,7 to 1 fte (26,6 to 38 hours per week), maximaal 6 months, depending on the number of fte’s.
 Working arrangements 
The position can be carried out remotely. The postdoctoral researcher will work independently while maintaining regular contact with the project team through scheduled online meetings. Progress will be monitored through agreed milestones and deliverables to ensure timely completion of the project.
Expected deliverables:
 Reproducible European palaeogeographic datasets for multiple Pleistocene time slices.
 Connectivity maps identifying emergent movement corridors, bottlenecks and barriers.
 Comparison of predicted corridors with archaeological site distributions.
 Reproducible R code and documentation.
 Draft manuscript suitable for submission to a peer-reviewed journal.
 What you bring 
We are looking for someone who can work independently while collaborating effectively with the project team. Given the short duration of the appointment, you should be able to quickly familiarise yourself with the project objectives and work towards clearly defined milestones. This position is a good fit for you if you recognise yourself in the following:
 PhD degree completed by the time of appointment in Archaeology, Geography, Geosciences, Ecology, Computer Science, or a related discipline;
 Experience with GIS, spatial analysis, and processing large raster and vector geospatial datasets.
 Programming experience in R (preferred), or Python or another language suitable for spatial analysis and simulation.

Binnen Leiden University College zijn wij op zoek naar een administratieve office assistant voor 2 dagen per week (0.4 fte) voor de periode januari (of zo spoedig mogelijk) tot en met juli 2027. Er is een kans op uitbreiding of verlenging. In deze functie heb je contact met studenten en werk je samen met andere collega's binnen de studentenadministratie. Je maakt deel uit van de ondersteunende staf van LUC.
 Hier ga je werken 
Het doel van de Faculteit Governance en Global Affairs (FGGA) is bijdragen aan de samenleving. Dit doet de faculteit met hoogwaardig interdisciplinair onderwijs en (nieuwe) wetenschappelijke kennis. Of het nu gaat om terrorisme, veiligheid, artificial intelligence of een bestuurlijke oplossing voor de woningcrisis, bij FGGA komen hedendaagse vraagstukken uitgebreid aan bod.
In hartje Den Haag, waar belangrijke beslissingen worden genomen, komen studenten en professionals samen om kennis en vaardigheden op te doen. Er wordt veel samengewerkt met universitaire en maatschappelijke partners, wat ervoor zorgt dat studenten de universiteit verlaten met een glimlach en alvast met één been in de toekomst, klaar om een substantiële bijdrage te leveren aan de maatschappij.
FGGA is één van de zeven faculteiten van de Universiteit Leiden. Deze jonge, ondernemende, vernieuwende en innovatieve organisatie heeft drie wetenschappelijke instituten, twee centers, ruim 3700 studenten en 425 medewerkers. Voor meer informatie over de faculteit klik hier .
Leiden University College The Hague (LUC) is het internationale Engelstalige Honours College van de Universiteit Leiden. Getalenteerde en gemotiveerde studenten van over de hele wereld komen speciaal naar Den Haag om deel te nemen aan het innovatieve Liberal Arts and Science-programma dat zich richt op de mondiale uitdagingen van vandaag. Het LUC kan al meer dan tien jaar rekenen op een plekje in de Keuzegids Universiteiten als best gewaardeerde University Colleges van Nederland. Het wetenschappelijke personeel, met diverse achtergronden en disciplines, heeft een passie voor lesgeven en onderwijs waarin de student centraal staat.
De administratieve office assistant is onderdeel van de support staf, een gezellig en multidisciplinair team dat onze studenten en staf van Leiden University College over de volle breedte ondersteunt.
 Dit ga je doen 
 Het produceren van documenten voor studenten, zoals transcripts, brieven en verklaringen;
 Helpen met de voorbereiding van de diploma uitreiking, vooral het doorvoeren van de studieplannen in uSis en het registreren en produceren van officiële (diploma) documenten;
 Cijfers invoeren in uSis;
 Het studiematerialen archief beheren;
 Algemene administratieve processen ondersteunen, zoals het opcoeren van de studenten voor de vakken, het produceren van cijferlijsten, het ondersteunen van het vak evaluatieproces en het beantwoorden van vragen van studenten en staf over beleid, procuedures en IT systemen.
 Dit breng je mee 
In dit team zoeken we iemand die zelfstandig aan de slag kan. Uiteraard is er aandacht voor het inwerken. Deze functie past bij jou als je je herkent in de volgende punten:
 HBO werk- en denkniveau
 Minimaal 1 jaar relevante werkervaring, bij voorkeur binnen het hoger onderwijs
 Ervaring met/kennis van de verschillende internationale onderwijssystemen
 Ervaring met uSis of vergelijkare administratie systemen of processen
 Uitstekende verbale en schriftelijke communicatieve vaardigheden in Nederlands en Engels
 Accuraat en georganiseerd werken met oog voor procedures en details
 Hands on mentaliteit en teamplayer
 Interesse in het werken in een internationaal team
Herken je jezelf volledig in dit profiel óf voldoe jij niet aan alle eisen maar denk je wel dat dit de functie voor jou is? Dan nodigen wij je graag uit om te solliciteren!
 Dit bieden we je 
We streven ernaar om met elkaar een transparante, inclusieve werkomgeving te creëren, waarin iedereen zich welkom en gewaardeerd voelt. Onze organisatie is volop in beweging en met jouw ideeën voor verbetering en vernieuwing komen we verder. We besteden graag met jou aandacht aan je persoonlijke ontwikkeling.
Je kunt rekenen op een leuke maatschappelijk relevante baan binnen de wereld van onderwijs en onderzoek. De uitdagende en internationale werkomgeving van de universiteit bevindt zich op een steenworp afstand van de levendige Leidse binnenstad of in het bruisende stadscentrum in Den Haag. Ook hebben we – samen met jou – aandacht voor gezondheid en vitaliteit. Vanuit Healthy University organiseren we leuke activiteiten die hieraan bijdragen.
Daarnaast bieden we je:
 Een tijdelijke arbeidsovereenkomst van 1 januari (of zsm) tot en met 31 juli 2027. De overeenkomst valt onder de cao Nederlandse Universiteiten;
 Een salaris tussen 3202,- tot 4159,- bruto per maand bij een fulltime (38 uur) aanstelling (schaal 7);
 Vakantietoeslag (8%), een eindejaarsuitkering (8,3%) en een aantrekkelijke pensioenregeling bij het ABP;
 Volledige vergoeding van reiskosten

academictransfer:364782.description:
Curious about why cognitive abilities fluctuate over time? Interested in using cognitive models and Bayesian hierarchical approaches to tackle complex, real-world data? Join this ERC-funded project to investigate cognitive variability by integrating the dynamic cognitive and biological processes that drive fluctuations in performance across multiple timescales.
 Join us! 
We are looking for a postdoctoral researcher to join our project entitled “Next-Generation Cognitive Testing: A Theory-Driven Approach to Multi-Scale Dynamics in Cognition”, funded by an ERC Consolidator grant awarded to Dora Matzke.
Few aspects of human performance are as salient and consequential as its variability. Fluctuations are evident in essentially all areas of cognition. For example, attention fluctuates with alertness modulated by circadian timing, while cognitive abilities change over longer time scales due to skill acquisition and forgetting. Given the critical role of cognition in nearly all aspects of human functioning, including safety-critical situations, these fluctuations have profound implications. Yet, the causes and temporal scales of cognitive fluctuations remain poorly understood. The project will develop a unified theoretical framework, for the first time synthetizing the dynamics of the diverse factors underlying fluctuations in cognitive abilities across multiple temporal scales. This interdisciplinary approach will create new opportunities for the emerging field of ecological momentary assessment (EMA) in cognitive testing, enhancing reliability and predictive power, and advancing understanding of cognitive dynamics in real-world contexts. The project includes two synergistic strands: (1) Theoretical work to create a dynamic quantitative modeling framework, linking accounts of short-term variability to longer-term adaptations in performance; (2) Empirical work using EMA to investigate how and why performance on a wide range of cognitive tasks fluctuates across time scales from sub-seconds to several weeks.
This postdoctoral project has three main objectives:
 Contribute to the development of novel adaptive evidence-accumulation models for a range of cognitive tasks (e.g., stop-signal and Stroop tasks), providing theory-driven accounts of trial-to-trial fluctuations in cognitive performance.
 Integrate these models within a Bayesian hierarchical framework with formal models of learning and biological mathematical models of alertness, connecting accounts of short-term cognitive variability to longer-term adaptations in performance.
 Implement and maintain software for fitting and applying the developed models, making the new methods accessible for use in cognitive research.
 What are you going to do 
The postdoctoral researcher will be embedded in the Amsterdam Mathematical Psychology Laboratory ( https://www.ampl-psych.com/ ), within the Psychological Methods program group. Teaching is limited to 5% of the contracted hours, and consists of assisting in courses and supervising (bachelor) thesis students.
 What do you have to offer 
A strong candidate will have a clear affinity with mathematical psychology and Bayesian cognitive modeling. Given that the project sits at the intersection of psychology, cognitive science, and mathematics, we are looking for someone who is motivated to work in a multidisciplinary team and able to collaborate across fields.
Your experience and profile:
 PhD in mathematical psychology, computational cognitive modeling, psychological methods or a related discipline
 Demonstrable experience with response time modeling, particularly evidence-accumulation models
 Demonstrable experience with Bayesian hierarchical methods
 Strong programming skills in R and experience developing reproducible research software
 A strong research track record, demonstrated through peer-reviewed publications and/or other relevant research outputs
 The ability to work independently and contribute creatively to the development of new models and methods
 Strong collaborative skills
 Excellent written and spoken English
 What else do we offer you 
The position concerns temporary employment of 38 hours per week. The employment is for two years.
For this position the University Job Classification profile 'onderzoeker 3/researcher 3' applies.
Your salary will be €4.925 gross per month in the first year and will increase to €6.682 in the second year, based on full-time employment and in keeping with the Collective Labour Agreement of Dutch Universities. We additionally offer an extensive package of secondary benefits, including 8% holiday allowance and a year-end bonus of 8.3%.
The UvA offers excellent possibilities for further professional development and education.
What else do we offer
 a position in which initiative and input are highly valued
 an enthusiastic and warm team that is open to new colleagues
 an inspiring academic and international working environment in the heart of Amsterdam.

academictransfer:364789.description:
At the University of Groningen (UG), researchers from all fields of academia and technology are working on academic challenges and societal questions. Lecturers prepare their students for meaningful careers within or outside the academic world. Interdisciplinary research and teaching, sharing of knowledge, collaboration with businesses, government institutions, and societal organizations are aspects that are of the utmost importance to this European top university. The UG aims to be an open academic community with an inclusive and safe working climate that invites you to add your value.
 The Faculty of Science and Engineering (FSE) provides teaching and research across a wide range of disciplines, from physics and biology to artificial intelligence, mechanical engineering, and pharmacy. In close collaboration with partners from industry, healthcare, and society, we contribute to the urgent challenges of our time, such as energy, sustainability, digitization, and medical technology. Our community is open and informal, with more than 7,000 students, 1,000 PhD students, and 1,400 staff members from all over the world. If you would like to learn more about the Faculty of Science and Engineering, visit rug.nl/fse . 
 What are you going to do? 
 This postdoctoral position is part of a multidisciplinary consortium project bringing together three partners at the forefront of nanopore science: the Vorobieva lab at the VUB-VIB Center for Structural Biology (Brussels), a pioneer in the de novo computational design of membrane proteins and nanopores from physical principles; the group of Prof. Giovanni Maglia at the University of Groningen, a world leader in biological nanopore engineering and single-molecule protein/peptide analysis; and imec (Leuven), a global leader in solid-state nanopore fabrication and hybrid nanopore-electronic integration.
 Together, the consortium aims to combine de novo protein design, biological nanopore sensing and solid-state nanofabrication into a new generation of hybrid nanopore sensors for single-molecule protein and peptide analysis.
 •     Engineer and characterise biological nanopores for the detection, identification and analysis of proteins and peptides, building on the Maglia lab's nanopore sensing and electro-osmotic sequencing platforms.
 •     Collaborate with VUB-VIB to test, validate and adapt de novo-designed protein nanopores for functional single-molecule sensing applications.
 •     Collaborate with imec on the integration of biological/de novo nanopores with solid-state platforms towards scalable, hybrid nanopore devices.
 •     Design and perform single-molecule experiments (electrical recordings, possibly combined with optical/fluorescence readouts) to characterise pore behaviour and sensing performance.
 •     Contribute to project management and valorisation activities alongside the consortium partners, including reporting to the funding body and engagement with industrial stakeholders.
 •     Publish and present your findings in peer-reviewed journals and at international conferences, and contribute to supervising PhD students and junior lab members.

REQUIREMENTS:
•    A PhD in Biochemistry, Chemistry, Biophysics, Molecular Biology, Bionanotechnology or a related field, completed or nearly completed.
 •    Demonstrated experience with protein engineering, expression and purification; experience with membrane proteins, ion channels or nanopores is a strong advantage.
 •    Experience with single-molecule biophysical techniques (e.g. electrical/electrophysiological recordings, single-channel analysis, fluorescence-based single-molecule methods) is highly desirable.
 •    A strong record of scientific output relative to career stage (publications, conference contributions).
 •    Willingness to collaborate closely with partner labs in Brussels (VUB-VIB) and Leuven (imec), including travel for joint experiments and consortium meetings.
 •    Good written and spoken English; strong communication, organisational and mentoring skills.

CONTRACT: A fixed-term contract of 1.0 FTE for the duration of 36 months.
