PhD position on local food web dynamics within offshore wind farms in the North Sea POWER (Progress in Offshore Wind Ecological Research) consortium. 
As offshore wind farms rapidly expand in the North Sea, mitigating their ecological impact on marine ecosystems is critical. The North Sea POWER project addresses this challenge by filling vital knowledge gaps regarding underwater noise, biomass and water flows, and wildlife disturbance (such as seabirds and bats) to support a sustainable green energy transition. By reducing uncertainty in models and identifying effective mitigation options, North Sea POWER supports offshore wind development that protects marine ecosystems while contributing to a sustainable energy future.
The project is funded through the Dutch Research Agenda (NWA), developed in collaboration with the Dutch Ministry of Economic Affairs and Climate Policy.
Led by Wageningen University & Research, the project brings together a transdisciplinary consortium of leading academic institutions, societal stakeholders, conservation organisations, and energy sector partners. More about the consortium .
This position is one of twelve PhD and postdoc positions across the consortium. You will be part of a team working on shared questions, with joint meetings, fieldwork and training alongside your own project. You will be hosted at Wageningen Marine Research in Den Helder, where you will study how fouling communities in offshore wind farms affect local food web dynamics and carbon cycling in close collaboration with Wageningen University. Part of the molecular lab work will be performed in the lab of Marine Animal Ecology in Wageningen.
 Are you interested in how biofouling communities in offshore wind farms affect local food web dynamics and carbon cycling? 
We are looking for a motivated PhD candidate to join our research team on biofouling with a focus on quantifying how biofouling communities influence primary and secondary production and blue carbon sequestration in the seabed. By combining laboratory experiments, in-situ fieldwork observations, and ecosystem modelling, your work will help refine current ecosystem-scale models and inform environmental impact assessments.
 Your duties and responsibilities include: 
 conduct laboratory experiments to measure and quantify grazing rates, carbon biomass, prey preferences, particle export, and faeces sinking velocity rates across different fouling species;
 execute field surveys from research vessels;
 integrate empirical data into conceptual models;
 publish research findings in peer-reviewed journals and present them at national and international conferences;
 mentor BSc/MSc students.
 Your team 
You will be part of Wageningen Marine Research (WMR – Den Helder), as a member of the Theme Team North Sea Reefs with Dr. Joop Coolen , and Dr. Ninon Mavraki as your daily supervisors, and you are also part of the Marine Animal Ecology Group (MAE) supervised by the Associate Professor Reindert Nijland at Wageningen University and Research. In Den Helder a broad group of scientists, analysts, field workers and students work on a variety of topics, such as benthic ecology, seals, seabirds, bats and other species. You will be a member of the theme team North Sea Reefs, with multiple colleagues specialising in the ecology of natural and artificial reefs in the North Sea. Furthermore, you will have the opportunity to design experiments involving molecular tools, such as eDNA and DNA metabarcoding, which then will be performed at the molecular laboratory of MAE in Wageningen University.
 You will work here 
The position is available within Wageningen University & Research at the Marine Animal Ecology group. The organisation has good and flexible employment conditions, including good education and training facilities for PhD students. Your working location will be at Wageningen Marine Research in Den Helder, the Netherlands, where the daily supervisors Joop Coolen and Ninon Mavraki are located. WMR is an applied research institute with 3 locations (Den Helder, IJmuiden and Yerseke) in the Netherlands. Research areas in Den Helder include coastal and offshore North Sea, tropics and (ant)arctic regions. In addition to ecological research, WMR advises the government regarding protection of species and habitats, pollution, and other anthropogenic interactions with ecology, and collaborate with industry, i.a. to study nature inclusive designs. Facilities in Den Helder in addition to offices, include a benthic lab, eco-analysis lab, climate rooms, mesocosms and algae culture facilities. Additionally, WMR has an experimental hard substrate garden in the marina on the island of Texel.

REQUIREMENTS:
You are/have the following: 
 you have a master’s degree (or graduation before appointment date) in Biology, Marine Biology, Ecology, Environmental Science, or another closely related field;
 you have experience with hands-on laboratory experiments and ecological fieldwork;
 you have demonstrated background or strong interest in ecological modelling and data analysis;
 you have a strong interest in marine ecology and multidisciplinary research;
 you also have strong collaborative skills and are willing to work with a diverse group of scientists, technicians, and project stakeholders with various backgrounds.
Furthermore, you have strong quantitative and preferably technical skills, and the ability to work independently in a challenging environment.
 You also possess: 
you have a proactive, inquisitive, enthusiastic, creative and self-reliant mind-set and you are strongly motivated to obtain a PhD degree.
Finally, you are excellent in written and oral communication skills in English (a minimum of CEFR C2 level language proficiency). For more information about this proficiency level, please visit our special language page .

CONTRACT: 18 months

 Are you an experienced international agricultural development professional ready to become a leading advisor in seed systems? 
 Do you enjoy working at the intersection of agriculture, innovation, policy, institutions and markets? You bring either direct seed systems expertise or the ambition and demonstrated potential to develop into a leading seed systems advisor.

PhD: Modelling non-CO2 greenhouse gas emissions from agriculture
Your job
 The Earth Systems and Global Change Group at Wageningen University and Research invites applications for a PhD position (4 years) in “Modelling non-CO2 greenhouse gas emissions from agriculture” starting in September 2026. 
 This PhD project aims to advance monitoring, reporting, verification (MRV) systems and mitigation strategies for reducing agricultural GHG emissions by systematically evaluating and improving the accuracy, effectiveness, efficiency, and usability of both established and emerging MRV tools, as part of an exciting HORIOZON project entitled MARVELA. The research will focus on key agricultural practices, including animal husbandry, manure management, livestock feeding and grazing, soil tillage, fertilizer application, and liming, across diverse pedo-climatic zones and farming systems. By adopting a holistic, systems-oriented perspective, this project will generate harmonized metrics that enable consistent, transparent, and comparable assessments across regions and practices, while simultaneously providing new scientific insights to inform the development and implementation of robust mitigation measures for the achievement of climate neutrality goals.
 Your duties and responsibilities include:  
 As a PhD researcher, you will expand and improve an existing modelling framework to predict direct and indirect nitrous oxide and methane emissions from agriculture. You contribute to the following activities:
 Performing a SWOT analysis of existing models and model requirements to predict non-CO2 greenhouse gas emissions on regional level across Europe, including their ability to assess the impact of mitigation measures across time and space.
 Design, build and implement an integrated regional and farm system MRV meta-model for several pilot regions across Europe
 Model evaluation of mitigation measures to ‘consolidate and improve knowledge on mitigation measures for agricultural non-CO2 GHG emissions.
 You will work here 
 The research is embedded within the chair  Earth Systems and Global Change Group , which is led by  Prof. dr. Hannah van Zanten  and  Prof. dr. Nynke Hofstra . You will be supervised by  Dr. Gerard Ros ,  Dr. Mengru Wang and  Prof. dr. Hannah van Zanten from Wageningen University, and Prof Dr. Erik Meers from Ghent University. 
 Your qualities
 You are/have the following personal competencies and skills.  
 experience in data analysis, quantitative modeling and programming (e.g., R, python);
 knowledge of nutrient and/or agrochemical cycles in agriculture;

Machine Learning/AI Researcher and Project Leader
Your job
 Are you an experienced machine learning and data science professional who wants to make a real-world impact? Do you have a specialisation in machine learning and affinity with project management? Do you want to apply advanced AI solutions to contribute to a more sustainable and better world? We,  Wageningen Food & Biobased Research (WFBR), are looking for a researcher data & modelling.  Are you the one who will strengthen our team? 
 What will you do? 
 As a machine learning researcher, you will initiate and work on innovative data-driven solutions in the bioeconomy and food domains. One example is improving fermentation screening for plant‑based ingredients, a process that is traditionally slow because each substrate–strain combination behaves differently. By applying machine learning to historical experimental data, we can predict high‑potential combinations that support the creation of innovative and sustainable food products. Another example is using large language model (LLM) tools to automatically extract and structure fragmented information from internal and external sources for use in our digital solutions.
 Your duties and responsibilities include:  
 initiation of new projects / ideas for acquisition by shaping new applied research propositions and supplying the insights needed to convey the value of AI solutions to partners & clients;
 leading projects in which you and your team design and develop new AI solutions. Off course translating research questions into robust machine learning implementations, including preprocessing, model training, validation and deployment is part of your role;
 collaborating enthusiastically with domain specialists and software developers to integrate data‑driven models with mechanistic or physics‑based models and domain expertise;
 showing thought leadership on applying data & AI-solutions in the food & biobased domain: where are the big leaps, how can we actively bring the benefits of data & AI to our customers in this domain?
 Your team 
 You will work as an expert within the expertise group  Wageningen Food & Biobased Research . Together with the adjoining expertise Computer Vision it comprises about 16 diverse specialists ranging from software development to AI/ML research. At DSI, our mission is to unlock the full potential of data and AI to help transform food and biobased systems into sustainable, resilient and innovative sectors — through science, collaboration and real‑world application.
 Our projects require close interaction with WFBR domain specialists, with whom you will play a key role in translating state‑of‑the‑art digital techniques into models that meet their scientific and operational needs. 
 You will work here  
 WFBR operates at the intersection of science, industry and government, delivering applied research and innovation projects funded by both public and private partners. You will be part of a multidisciplinary environment within WFBR, working closely with experts in food technology, microbiology and chemistry. Knowledge sharing is central to how we work: we meet several times a week in Wageningen to exchange ideas, review project progress, and continuously improve our approaches. You will collaborate with business developers, researchers, software developers and clients. You will contribute to impactful applied research in the domains of food and biobased materials.
 Your qualities
 You have solid experience with AI‑ and machine‑learning‑based approaches and easily connect with colleagues from other areas of expertise, enjoying the dynamics of multidisciplinary teamwork. You are comfortable explaining complex technical concepts to non‑technical stakeholders/colleagues and can translate digital approaches into practical, usable solutions. You are proactive, innovative and a strong team player who contributes positively to collaboration and project success.
 You also possess:  
 a PhD in Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Computer Science or a related field;
 at least 3 years of hands‑on experience in AI / machine learning development (excluding PhD);
 proven expertise in machine learning and generative AI methodologies (in the range of: LLMs, RAG systems, agentic AI, feature engineering, model selection and validation, supervised and unsupervised learning, optimization techniques, (deep) neural networks, probabilistic methods and statistics, data visualization, natural language processing);

PhD position: New Synthetic Methods for Prodrug Activation
Your job
 Are you excited to work at the frontiers of synthetic organic chemistry, catalysis, and medicinal chemistry? We, Wageningen University and Research, have a vacancy for a PhD in New Synthetic Methods for Prodrug Activation. 
 We are offering a 4-year PhD position in the  Laboratory of Organic Chemistry at Wageningen University and Research, focusing on the development of new (photo)catalytic reactions and synthetic methods to activate prodrugs.
 About the project: 
Prodrugs are molecules with little to no biological activity that can harmlessly circulate through the body until they reach their target and are converted into active drugs. The use of prodrugs offers the potential for safer and more effective therapies. However, their successful application requires chemical reactions that convert prodrugs into their active forms in a controlled manner. The aim of this project is therefore to develop new synthetic methods to make precise modifications to a drug’s skeleton with catalytic control, enabling it to bind its target and thus become an active drug. By innovating prodrug activation strategies, we aim to contribute to the development of next-generation prodrugs while expanding the synthetic toolbox. As such, this PhD project combines method development with catalysis and organic synthesis.
 Your duties and responsibilities include:  
 you will contribute to the development of new synthetic methods and catalytic tools that enable the controlled activation of prodrugs under physiological conditions. A key aspect of this role is staying informed of the latest developments in the fields of synthetic organic chemistry and catalysis and integrating relevant advances into ongoing research;
 you are expected to develop research questions, design experimental approaches, and execute synthesis and characterization of organic and inorganic compounds within the context of the project.  you have a Master’s degree or equivalent in (synthetic) chemistry and can demonstrate expertise in synthetic organic chemistry and/or catalysis. Experience with photochemical techniques is desirable;

wur:16695.description:
Do you want to help combat animal disease outbreaks such as foot-and-mouth disease and bluetongue? Do you have experience with virological, immunological, and molecular techniques, and do you want to participate in research into viral diseases and thereby contribute to the health of animals and humans? Then read on and apply quickly!
An important task of WBVR as a national reference laboratory is to develop and validate diagnostic tests to detect notifiable viral diseases as effectively as possible at an early stage. In addition, research is conducted into these viral diseases to develop expertise to advise the government on the prevention and control of animal disease outbreaks.WBVR also collaborates with various clients to develop new vaccines and study their efficacy. Within the One Health Virology team, we are looking for a flexible researcher with a Bachelor's degree to work on this.
An important part of the work involves setting up, adapting, validating, and accrediting diagnostic tests (particularly PCR, sequencing, ELISA, and VNT). In addition, you are involved - especially during the critical period of an outbreak - in the further characterization of detected viruses (PCRs, whole-genome sequencing) and database management. If the situation requires it, you also contribute to the rapid development of new diagnostic tests. Furthermore, you work on (molecular) virological research projects aimed at developing and testing new vaccines and combating various viral diseases. For these tasks, experience with virological, immunological, and molecular techniques is important, alongside quality awareness and communication skills.
 Your duties and responsibilities include: 
 performing, setting up, validating, and accrediting diagnostic tests for notifiable animal diseases such as foot-and-mouth disease and bluetongue;
 contributing ideas for improving diagnostics and setting up new techniques;
 conducting research projects. These may include molecular virological studies into new vaccines, as well as studies to test the efficacy of new vaccines.
 Your team 
You will be working alongside your colleagues in the One Health Virology department at Wageningen Bioveterinary Research (WBVR) in Lelystad.
 You will work here 
 Wageningen Bioveterinary Research (WBVR) is a leading research institute in the field of animal health, and public health. Its unique selling point lies in its interdisciplinary approach to research and its focus on innovative solutions for complex problems in these fields.
WBVR has a unique position in the Netherlands, as it is the only research institute that is allowed to work with the most animal viruses and bacteria up to level vBSL4 (vDM4), such as foot-and-mouth disease and African swine fever in laboratories and animal facilities, were large livestock animals (o.a. cattle) and smaller rodents can be housed. Also, facilities are in place to do research and animal experiments for BLS3 pathogens such as avian influenza and Coxiella. Different experts on specific pathogens, host responses, bioinformatics, pathology, epidemiology and diagnostics allows WBVR to work on the mission and vision of WBVR.
WBVR contributes to a society where animals and humans live a healthy life by scientific research to prevent the spread of animal diseases and promote health.
WBVR adds value to the agricultural and life sciences value chains by conducting contract research, R&D, and statutory research tasks. We serve the interests of the Dutch agro-food sector, (veterinary) public health, and the life sciences & health sectors. As contract-research organization we focus on market needs in the animal and human life sciences sectors.
WBVR has 3 focus points, healthy livestock, one health and high tech animal models (including the 3R’s).

REQUIREMENTS:
You possess: 
 a Bachelor's degree in Life Sciences, such as Biology and Medical Laboratory Research (HLO program);
 knowledge of and experience with performing (molecular) virological and immunological techniques and ensuring the quality of tests;
 affinity with laboratory diagnostics and quality matters (ISO 17025);
 you are proactive, work accurately, think analytically, and can organize your work well;
 you value good teamwork;
 you have a good command of the Dutch language, both spoken and written The work will largely take place in buildings subject to quarantine restrictions based on EU regulations upon departure.

CONTRACT: 1 year

wur:16701.description:
Chemical Analyst
Your job
 Do you enjoy hands-on laboratory work? Would you like to work with modern laboratory equipment and contribute to food safety? Then this could be your next career step. 
 At Wageningen Food Safety Research (WFSR), we are looking for a Chemical Analyst PFAS to join our Contaminants Team. You do not need years of experience, although that is certainly welcome. What matters most to us is that you work accurately, are curious, and are eager to continue developing your skills. 
 What will you do?
 As a Chemical Analyst, you will contribute to the analysis of PFAS, a group of chemical substances that currently receives significant attention. Your work will help provide insight into the presence of PFAS in food products and other sample types.
 You will have a varied and predominantly hands-on laboratory role, while also being involved in the processing and reporting of analytical results. Your responsibilities will include:
 preparing and processing samples;
 performing PFAS analyses according to established procedures and work instructions;
 operating laboratory equipment, including LC-MS/MS;
 processing and reviewing measurement data and assessing whether results meet quality requirements;
 recording and reporting analytical results;
 maintaining accurate and complete laboratory records;
 keeping the laboratory clean, safe, and well organized.
 You will work according to established procedures and clear instructions. If something appears unusual or a sample does not meet expectations, you will raise the issue and discuss it with colleagues.
 Initially, you will work closely with experienced analysts. This allows you to learn the profession in practice and gradually develop greater independence.
 Your Team
 You will join the Contaminants Team at WFSR in Wageningen. The team consists of chemical analysts, researchers, and project leaders. Together, we investigate chemical substances that may be present in food and other products.
 PFAS forms an important part of our work, and we expect a growing number of analyses in the coming years. This means there is plenty of work and many opportunities to learn and develop.

wur:16717.description:
Are you interested in spatial ecology, species distributions, and plant functional traits? Do you want to contribute to understanding global patterns of plant diversity, and plant responses to environmental change? 
Conserving biodiversity in a rapidly changing world requires understanding why some species occupy vast geographic ranges while others remain restricted to small areas. Traditionally, efforts to answer this question have focused on understanding and predicting the distributions of individual species. However, recent advances in biodiversity and trait datasets have expanded our capacity to incorporate the functional characteristics of species, allowing us to go beyond the species concept and better capture the variation in biota using functional traits across different levels of biological organisation.
This PhD position explores how functional traits influence global patterns of plant biodiversity and plant responses to environmental change. The project focuses on three different levels of organisation, ranging from broad functional forms that capture major ecological plant strategies (e.g. tree, epiphyte, shrub), to finer levels of organisation among species (inter-specific variation) and within species (intra-specific variation). As a PhD candidate, you will make use of large trait databases like TRY and BIEN, and be responsible for setting up a greenhouse experiment similar to that of a provenance trial set-up (i.e. growing seeds collected from across a species’ native geographic range under varying environmental conditions). Specifically, your duties and responsibilities include:
 Collating plant distributions, functional traits, and environmental data from various sources
 Setting-up and conducting a greenhouse experiment to assess variation in plant phenotypic plasticity under simulated environmental conditions
 Publishing your research in peer-reviewed journals and presenting your research at (inter)national conferences
 Mentoring BSc/MSc students
 You will work here 
The research is embedded within the Plant Ecology and Nature Conservation group , which is led by Prof. David Kleijn. You will be supervised by Dr. Coline Boonman and Dr. Amanda Taylor. Prof. David Kleijn is the promotor.

REQUIREMENTS:
You have the following personal competencies and skills:
 A successfully completed MSc degree in ecology, environmental sciences or a related field
 Experience handling large biodiversity datasets and environmental data
 Highly proficient in data analysis in R and strong quantitative and statistical expertise
 Excellent oral and written communication skills in English
 The ability to work independently and collaboratively
For this position your command of the English language is expected to be at C1 level . Sometimes it is necessary to submit an internationally recognised Certificate of Proficiency in the English Language. More information can be found here .

wur:16732.description:
Are you a highly motivated and enthusiastic ecologist who wants to uncover how nitrogen deposition affects plant and arthropod biodiversity? Are you excited by the idea of combining large-scale fieldwork across Northwestern Europe with hands-on experiments to answer a question that matters for biodiversity conservation? If so, this PhD-position could be the perfect fit for you! 
Human-driven nitrogen (N) deposition is changing ecosystems worldwide. It can cause an oversupply of nitrogen in the soil and soil acidification, and shift the balance of nutrients; not just how many nutrients are available, but also the ratios between them (their ‘stoichiometry’). This changes which plants thrive, and it changes the nutritional quality of the leaves and pollen that herbivorous and pollinating insects consume. However, we still poorly understand how these changes unfold within and among plant species, or how they cascade to affect insect performance and, ultimately, insect community diversity. As a PhD candidate, you will contribute to finding this out. You will combine field studies in Northwestern European forests across a N-deposition gradient spanning the Netherlands, Germany, Denmark and Sweden with greenhouse and controlled feeding experiments on caterpillars and solitary bees.
 Your duties and responsibilities include: 
 Design and conduct field studies across Northwestern Europe to assess how large- and small-scale gradients in N deposition affect soil chemistry, plant stoichiometry, and plant and arthropod diversity
 Perform experiments to find out how nutrient concentrations in plant leaves and pollen affect the performance and food preferences of insect herbivore and pollinator species
 Analyse complex ecological datasets, linking soil, plant and insect variables
 Co-supervise MSc students conducting thesis research within the project
 Publish your results in a PhD thesis, as well as in peer-reviewed papers
 You will work here 
The research is embedded within the Plant Ecology and Nature Conservation (PEN) group at Wageningen University, which is led by Prof. David Kleijn. Daily supervision will be by Dr. Philippine Vergeer, Dr. Jeroen Scheper, Dr. Fons van der Plas (all PEN) and Dr. Wim Ozinga (Vegetation and Landscape Ecology, Wageningen Environmental Research).

REQUIREMENTS:
You are a team player with strong motivation for ecological (field) studies, you like to analyze complex data sets, and have a critical, curious approach to research. You are keen to publish your findings in leading international academic journals, to communicate your findings to a wide audience, and you enjoy co-supervising MSc students doing thesis research within the framework of the project.
 You also possess: 
 An MSc in ecology, environmental sciences or a related field;
 Experience with ecological field studies (e.g., soil sampling, vegetation surveys, arthropod sampling and identification);
 Advanced skills in data analysis in R;
 Excellent written and spoken English;
 A driver's license;
For this position your command of the English language is expected to be at C1 level . Sometimes it is necessary to submit an internationally recognised Certificate of Proficiency in the English Language. More information can be found here .

PhD Replacing Chemicals with Electricity: Engineering Local pH Environments
Your job
 Can electricity replace acids, bases, and cleaning chemicals used throughout industry today? How do local pH conditions develop near electrodes and membranes in electrochemical systems, and how can they be controlled? In this PhD project, you will investigate these questions by combining modelling and experimental data to develop electrically driven alternatives for industrial cleaning and separation processes. 
 What will you do? 
 Many industries rely on acids, bases, detergents, and other chemicals to clean equipment, recover valuable products, and produce high-quality process water. These chemicals increase environmental impact, complicate water re-use and require downstream treatment. In this project, we take a different approach: rather than adding chemicals, we aim to create the required chemical conditions directly using electricity.
 A key challenge in replacing these chemicals with electricity is that electrochemical systems create localized pH environments near electrodes and membranes. These local conditions often differ strongly from bulk solution properties, yet they determine chemical speciation, surface interactions, selectivity, cleaning efficiency, and fouling behavior. The aim of this PhD project is to understand, predict, and engineer these local pH environments in electrochemical systems.
 As a PhD candidate, you will investigate how local pH environments develop near electrodes and membranes in complex water matrices. You will integrate theory, modelling, and experiments to determine how local pH conditions develop, how they depend on water composition and material properties, and how they can be engineered for practical applications. The insights obtained in this project can be used to develop electrically driven, chemical-free technologies for industrial cleaning and separations.
 You will be part of the  Electrically-driven Chemical-free Operations (ECO) consortium , a collaboration between the Institute for Sustainable Process Technology, the University of Twente, TU Delft, the University of Groningen, the University of Copenhagen, Wageningen University & Research, and industrial partners from the food, chemical, paper, and water sectors.
 Your duties and responsibilities include:  
 investigate how electrically induced local pH environments develop in electrochemical systems;
 develop theoretical and computational models to predict local pH conditions in complex water matrices and investigate the impact of water composition, electrode materials, and membrane materials on pH conditions;
 design experiments to quantify local pH environments near electrodes and membranes and integrate experimental observations and modelling results to develop design principles for electrically driven processes;
 use the obtained insights to guide the design of electrochemical cleaning and separation technologies in close collaboration with the industrial partners in the consortium;
 present research results at consortium meetings, international conferences, and scientific workshops and publish findings in leading peer-reviewed scientific journals.
 You will work here 
 The research is embedded within the  Environmental Technology group . You will join the Electrified Interfaces group, a research group studying transport, reactions, and selectivity at charged interfaces in environmental technologies, including electrochemical systems, membrane processes, adsorption and ion-exchange materials. You will be supervised by Dr. Jouke Dykstra and Dr. Hanieh Bazyar from TU Delft. 
 Your qualities
 You are an enthusiastic and curious researcher who enjoys working on complex scientific challenges. You combine analytical thinking with creativity and have a strong interest in understanding fundamental processes at interfaces. You are a team player and open to collaborating in a consortium of other researchers and industrial partners, with regular consortium meetings. You can communicate your research to people with a broad, technical background, and you can contribute to defining your own research, in agreement with the consortium.
 You also possess:  
 a successfully completed MSc degree in Chemical Engineering, Water Technology, Environmental Technology, Physical Chemistry, Process Engineering, or Applied Physics, or a related discipline;
 demonstrated affinity with electrochemistry, transport phenomena, membrane processes, colloid and interface science, and/or water technology;
 experience with experimental methods, modelling, or both, and enthusiasm to combine theory and experiments;
 excellent English communication skills and the motivation to publish your work in leading scientific journals.

 In addition to these first-rate employee benefits, you will receive a fully funded PhD position and you will be offered a course program tailored to your needs and the research team.

This is based on a full-time working week of 38 hours. We offer a temporary contract for 18 months which will be extended for the duration of the project if you perform well.

Marine Ecologist
Your job
 As a Marine Ecologist specialized in the Delta ecosystems at Wageningen Marine Research (WMR) in Yerseke, you will play an active role in restoring and enhancing the unique natural environment of the Delta waters. Using innovative, sustainable solutions based on the philosophy of ‘building with nature’, you will translate scientific knowledge into practical applications with a tangible impact.
 The South-Western Delta presents major ecological challenges as well as opportunities. From the sand deficiency in the Oosterschelde to nature conservation in the Westerschelde and improving water quality in Delta waters such as Lake Grevelingen and Lake Veere: you will make a significant contribution to solutions that make a difference to nature and society.
 Together with other experts in the field of marine ecology, you will work on a wide range of delta-related issues. You will investigate where nature development and nature-based solutions can be applied to areas such as flood protection and water quality improvement and will be able to convincingly demonstrate to clients the added value of this sustainable approach. In addition, you will contribute to the scientific basis of the Nature Restoration Plan and the management plans for Natura 2000 sites in the South-Western Delta. Liaising with clients and stakeholders is an integral part of your work.
 Your duties and responsibilities as a Marine Ecologist include: 
 contribute to a wide range of literature reviews, data analyses, and field and laboratory experiments in the field of nature conservation and benthic fauna research;
 assist with securing new projects and drafting research proposals;
 communicate with fellow researchers and clients;
 report and present research findings to clients, attend conferences and take part in workshops;
 publish and present results in academic journals and at conferences.
 Your team 
 Based at WMR’s site in Yerseke, you will work alongside various project teams of differing compositions. As a project leader, you will provide substantive and project-related guidance to fellow researchers so that they can carry out their work efficiently and thoroughly. As a project member, you will often focus on a specific area that matches your expertise. 
 You will work here  
 Wageningen Marine Research  (WMR) is one of the nine institutes that form part of Wageningen Research. WMR is a leading, independent research institute with sites in Yerseke, IJmuiden and Den Helder, which focuses on strategic and applied marine ecological research. Products and services are delivered on a project basis and are diverse in nature: field research, realistic-scale experiments, exploratory laboratory-scale studies, data management and modelling. The institute has modern research facilities and is ISO 9001 certified.
 Your area of work will primarily be the south-western Delta, but other parts of the Netherlands, such as the North Sea and the Wadden Sea, as well as international projects, are also possibilities.
 Your qualities
 You are curious about the interactions within ecosystems and are committed to contributing to the protection and restoration of marine and coastal ecosystems. Thanks to your ability to take a broader perspective, you feel at home at the interface between science and policy. You naturally build professional relationships with others and value each team member’s contribution to the overall project outcome. You can cope with time pressure and plan your work to meet deadlines. You are driven, proactive, collaborative, customer-focused and a strong communicator.
 You also possess:  
 a successfully completed relevant academic degree in the natural sciences or life sciences. A PhD in the field specified for this post is an advantage;
 experience with nature based solutions for flood protection;
 demonstrable work experience in ecological estuary and Delta research;
 a good command of both Dutch and English.
 In our international working environment there is an increasing amount of communication in English. For this position it is about  language level  B2.

PhD PFAS removal with activated carbon in drinking water treatment
Your job
 PFAS are among the most challenging contaminants facing drinking water utilities worldwide. Although granular activated carbon (GAC) is widely applied for PFAS removal, utilities face challenges with rapid PFAS breakthrough and  as a consequence  more frequent re-activation of activated carbon filters. The factors controlling breakthrough under realistic drinking water conditions remain insufficiently understood, particularly in the presence of natural organic matter (NOM) in the water matrix. 
 As a PhD candidate, you will investigate how water composition, natural organic matter, and activated carbon properties influence PFAS removal in drinking water treatment. You will combine laboratory experiments, column studies, and data analysis to identify the factors governing PFAS breakthrough at environmentally relevant conditions and concentrations.
 Working closely with drinking water company Evides, you will study PFAS adsorption in realistic drinking water matrices and evaluate how differences in NOM composition affect filter performance. The insights obtained in this project will support the development of improved operational strategies for activated carbon filtration and help drinking water utilities better predict and manage PFAS breakthrough in practice.
 Your duties and responsibilities include:  
 investigating the mechanisms governing competitive adsorption of PFAS and natural organic matter on granular activated carbon;
 designing and conducting batch and column experiments at environmentally relevant PFAS concentrations;
 analysing experimental data and developing predictive tools for activated carbon filter performance;
 identifying key water quality parameters that can serve as indicators for PFAS breakthrough;
 publishing your results in international scientific journals and presenting your work at conferences.
 You will work here 
 The research is embedded within the Chair Group of  Environmental Technology at Wageningen University & Research. The Environmental Technology group develops scientific understanding and technologies for sustainable water treatment, resource recovery, and environmental protection.
 You will be part of the Electrified Interfaces team, a research group studying transport, adsorption, reactions, and selectivity at environmental interfaces. Within this team, you will contribute to research on adsorption and separation processes for water treatment and environmental applications. The team is led by  dr. Jouke E. Dykstra .
 The project is carried out in close collaboration with Evides, one of the largest drinking water companies in the Netherlands, providing unique opportunities to connect fundamental research with real-world drinking water challenges.
 The project will be supervised by Prof. Dr. Ir. A. van der Wal and co-supervised by Dr. Ir. Jouke E. Dykstra.
 Your qualities
 You are an enthusiastic and curious researcher who enjoys working on complex scientific challenges. You combine analytical thinking with creativity and have a strong interest in understanding fundamental processes at interfaces. 
 You also possess:  
 a successfully completed MSc degree in Environmental Technology, Chemical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Environmental Sciences, Chemical Engineering, or a related field;
 affinity with adsorption processes, water treatment, colloid and interface science, or environmental chemistry;
 experience with laboratory research and experimental design;
 strong analytical and quantitative skills, with interest in data analysis and modelling;

wur:16768.description:
Dit ga je doen
 Als financial controller bij de NVWA speel je een sleutelrol in het versterken van de financiële beheersing van een organisatie die dagelijks werkt aan voedselveiligheid, dierenwelzijn, natuur en milieu. Met jouw financiële expertise, analytisch vermogen en oog voor verbetering zorg je voor betrouwbare financiële informatie, goed ingerichte processen en een solide basis voor verantwoorde besluitvorming.
Als financial controller ben je verantwoordelijk voor het bewaken, verbeteren en verder ontwikkelen van financiële processen binnen de NVWA. Je bent een belangrijke gesprekspartner voor management, business controllers en externe partijen. Met jouw kennis van financiële verslaggeving, interne beheersing en financiële analyses zorg je voor betrouwbare rapportages, inzichtelijke dashboards en toekomstgerichte adviezen.
 Jouw rol
 Je werkt aan uiteenlopende financiële vraagstukken en combineert operationele financiële werkzaamheden met een adviserende en verbetergerichte rol. Je draagt bij aan een betrouwbare financiële basis door het verzorgen van afsluitingen, rapportages en analyses en ondersteunt bij belangrijke financiële processen zoals de jaarrekening en accountantscontrole.
Daarnaast signaleer je kansen om processen slimmer en efficiënter in te richten. Je denkt mee over verdere professionalisering van Finance & Control en draagt bij aan innovatie, bijvoorbeeld door het gebruik van dashboards, proces mining, robotisering (RPA) en andere technologische ontwikkelingen.
 Kerntaken
 Als financial controller houd jij je onder andere bezig met:
 Het bewaken en verbeteren van het financieel beheer binnen één van de directies van de NVWA, in nauwe samenwerking met de business controller.
 Het opstellen en analyseren van financiële rapportages en dashboards.
 Het ondersteunen bij de jaarrekening, accountantscontrole en diverse financiële vraagstukken.
 Het uitvoeren van financiële analyses en het vertalen van inzichten naar concrete adviezen voor management en stakeholders.
 Het versterken van de interne beheersing door het verbeteren van AO/IC, risicomanagement en financiële processen.
 Het initiëren en realiseren van verbeteringen binnen Finance & Control, bijvoorbeeld op het gebied van procesoptimalisatie, automatisering en digitalisering.
Je werkt nauw samen met collega’s binnen Finance & Control, de business en externe partijen. Door jouw verbindende rol, inhoudelijke expertise en focus op verbetering draag je bij aan een betrouwbare, toekomstbestendige en efficiënte financiële organisatie.
Spreekt dit je aan en herken jij je in onderstaande functie-eisen? Zet je idealen dan om in daden en solliciteer bij de NVWA. Graag ontvangen wij je CV en motivatie! We verzoeken je daarbij om in je motivatie (max 1 A4 – adressering, aanhef en ondertekening kun je weglaten) specifiek antwoord te geven op onderstaande vragen:
 Waarom wil je als financial controller bijdragen aan de financiële beheersing van de NVWA en wat spreekt je specifiek aan in de financiële opgaven van onze organisatie?
 Beschrijf een concreet voorbeeld waarin je het financieel beheer, de AO/IC of de rechtmatigheid binnen een organisatie hebt verbeterd. Wat was jouw rol en wat was het resultaat?

Je krijgt een Individueel Keuzebudget (IKB) van 16,50% van je bruto jaarsalaris. Je kunt je IKB bijvoorbeeld laten uitbetalen, bijvoorbeeld per maand of per jaar, maar je kunt ook extra verlofuren kopen. Daarnaast kun je je IKB gebruiken om belastingvrij een (elektrische) fiets voor woon-werkverkeer aan te schaffen, je thuiskantoor in te richten, fiscaal voordelig je studieschuld af te lossen tot een max van €2000,- per jaar of zelfs je woning te verduurzamen. Om dit aan te moedigen biedt de Rijksoverheid bovenop het IKB hierbij ook een werkgeversbijdrage.

Per jaar heb je recht op 144 vakantie-uren en 64 IKB-verlofuren, wanneer je 36 uur per week werkt. Werk je meer of minder? Dan worden deze uren naar verhouding berekend. Je ontvangt een mobiliteitskaart waarmee je voor woon-werk verkeer 2e klas met de trein kunt reizen. Daarnaast kun je deze gebruiken voor dienstreizen indien je naar andere locaties moet voor je werk. Ga je met de fiets naar het werk? Dan ontvang je per gefietste kilometer een reiskostenvergoeding.

wur:16784.description:
Are you intrigued by interactions between vegetation and fire? Are you passionate about lab-, field-, and remote sensing-based research? Do you like solving scientific puzzles? We are looking for a highly motivated PhD candidate to explore how moss traits affect fire ignitability in high-latitude ecosystems. 
Northern ecosystems, including boreal peatlands and tundra, are warming faster than almost anywhere else on Earth, which is changing their structure and functioning. Permafrost thaw and increasing fire frequency threaten to turn these ecosystems from carbon sinks into carbon, further accelerating climate change. Bryophytes (including mosses) dominate the vegetation across much of these carbon-dense ecosystems. Because of their unique water-retention and insulating properties, they largely determine how susceptible these regions are to severe wildfires. This PhD project examines the relationship between bryophyte functional traits and fire dynamics at the plant, ecosystem, and biome scales, combining lab experiments, fieldwork, and remote sensing. Building on the PEN research line on vegetation-climate feedbacks, your work will advance our understanding of the functional role of bryophytes in fire dynamics and help improve fire risk assessments for these vulnerable systems.
 Your duties and responsibilities include: 
 Developing methods and designing and executing experiments to test moss ignitability
 Conducting fieldwork in high-latitude ecosystems, including vegetation surveys, monitoring environmental conditions during and after fires, and possibly drone-based observations
 Analysing remote sensing data and global vegetation databases
 Publishing your research in peer-reviewed journals and presenting it at national and international conferences
 Co-supervising BSc and MSc students
 You will work here 
The research is embedded within the Plant Ecology and Nature Conservation group, specifically within the Vegetation-Climate Feedbacks team. You will be co-supervised by Dr. Thomas Janssen, Dr. José van Paassen and Dr. Juul Limpens.

REQUIREMENTS:
You are a candidate with strong experimental skills, and conduct research responsibly. You work independently to find solutions for research challenges, while staying in communication with the team. You enjoy working with multiple project partners to efficiently arrange field and lab work.
 You also possess: 
 A successfully completed MSc degree in ecology, environmental sciences, climate studies or a related field
 Affinity and experience with experimental design of lab- and/or field experiments
 Excellent organizational and communicational skills
 Excellent English language skills, both written and spoken
 Experience with fire-related research is a plus
For this position your command of the English language is expected to be minimally at C1 level . Sometimes it is necessary to submit an internationally recognised Certificate of Proficiency in the English Language. More information can be found here .

CONTRACT: 18 months

Your job
 Wageningen University is renewing its BSc portfolio: fewer, sharper programmes with healthier intake. The first track concerns the subset around BTO, BBC, BEB and BIN, where intake is declining most sharply. As quartermaster, you will work with a temporary curriculum committee to design new, complementary BSc programmes that together replace the current ones.
 Your tasks 
 You lead the design of the new programmes, in line with the regular demand-supply model, and ensure they complement each other.

 You work with various departments within and outside ESA, including the Teaching & Learning Centre, Policy, Student Recruitment and Quality & Strategic Information.
 The design is about more than courses and credits. We also ask: good for whom, and to what end? What kind of people are we educating, and where in the programme is there room for risk, encounter and independent judgement?
 Your qualities
 What do you bring? 
 In-depth knowledge of the Wageningen education system: the educational model, the Framework for Education, the EMC cycle, the roles of the Board of Education, Examining Board and participatory bodies, and the relationship between programmes and chair groups.
 Distance from the programmes and chair groups involved. You have no stake in the allocation of courses, budget or students and have preferably not been (recently) involved as a lecturer, programme director or chair group staff member in the programmes within the portfolio.
 The weight and authority to hold difficult conversations, including with professors and programme directors whose courses or programmes will change or disappear. You remain businesslike, and can both listen and make tough decisions.
 Experience with curriculum design or large-scale educational innovation in higher education, and a feel for boundary work between disciplines, groups and interests.
 Experience chairing a committee or working group without formal line authority.
 Affinity with (one of) the domains: social sciences, economics, business and management, development, communication or health.

PhD Researcher in Atmospheric Sciences - Emerging extreme fire weather risks
Your job
 Are you a meteorologist or climate scientist with a passion to investigate the interactions between climate extremes and wildfire risks? Do you want to work on a research project that aims to understand the most extreme fire weather events possible, and how they will evolve in a warming world? Then this position may be the perfect opportunity for you! 
 The Meteorology and Air Quality (MAQ) Group at Wageningen University and Research is looking for a PhD candidate with a background in meteorology, atmospheric or climate sciences to work on unprecedented and emerging fire weather risks.
 Extreme fire weather, referring to the meteorological component of fire risk that reflects the combined effects of heat, drought, wind, and atmospheric aridity, is one of the key factors influencing wildfire spread and intensity. Climate change is increasing the frequency and severity of fire weather extremes across many regions, including the Northern Hemisphere mid-latitudes. Therefore, understanding and anticipating the most intense, persistent or otherwise most impactful fire weather conditions plausible today, as well as how these conditions may worsen under future warming, is crucial for fire risk assessment and preparedness. What are worst-case fire weather conditions possible under current climate versus in a warmer world, what atmospheric or climatic mechanisms drive them, and how this relates to actual fire occurrence and behaviour, are all questions that will be addressed within this PhD project. To answer them, you will investigate the most extreme events in the historical record and how they compare to the most extreme events in state-of-the-art climate modelling experiments. 
 This project will be supervised by Dr. Laura Suarez-Gutierrez in collaboration with Prof. Guido van der Werf and carried out in the highly multidisciplinary setting of the MAQ group. You will join a thriving, highly collaborative research environment with leading expertise in weather and climate extremes, fire dynamics, and their interactions.
 Your qualities
 You hold a MSc degree in meteorology, atmospheric sciences, climate sciences, physics, engineering, or related field;
 You are passionate about understanding climate extremes and fire risks;
 You are enthusiastic and motivated to work on this research project with independence as well as in a collaborative environment
 You are experienced in handling large data sets, for example weather and/or climate model and/or satellite data; 
 You have good programming skills (Python, shell scripts, and/or comparable experience);
 Prior knowledge and research experience in weather and climate extremes, fire risk, atmospheric and climate dynamics, and/or climate modelling is valued.

PhD – Militarization of Societal Resilience
Your job
 The Dutch government aims to strengthen societal resilience against war and disaster. The military plays a prominent role in these efforts, raising concerns about militarization and its adverse impact. In this PhD, you study how militarization in the Netherlands unfolds and examine its effects.
 Your duties and responsibilities include:

PhD: 3D radiation in clouds and wildfire plumes using GPUs and machine learning
Your job
 This PhD project is part of ORCRIST: Optimized Ray-tracing for Cloud-Radiation Interaction Simulations in 3D using GPUs and Machine Learning, funded by the NWO Open Technology Programme.
 Sunlight and heat radiation move through the atmosphere in three dimensions, yet almost every weather and climate model still treats radiation as a purely vertical process. We want to change that. As a PhD candidate in Wageningen, you will help build the first Monte Carlo ray tracer for the atmosphere that is fast enough for forecasting, and use it to find out how 3D radiation shapes clouds, solar energy availability, climate sensitivity and wildfire plumes. You will work in a tandem with a fellow PhD student in computer science at Leiden University, who focuses on GPU optimization, while you lead the physics. Together you will develop a machine-learning denoiser that brings the ray tracer to operational speed. Your research has a clear route to society: throughout the project you will work with a user committee of KNMI, weather forecasting company Whiffle, TNO, software company VORtech and Columbia University. 
 Your duties and responsibilities include:  
 Setting up three benchmark simulations in the GPU-accelerated model MicroHH: solar energy forecasting, tropical climate, and a real wildfire plume.
 Developing a 3D thermal radiation solver within the RTE-RRTMGP-CPP ray tracer, including smart strategies for sampling radiation sources.
 Quantifying how 3D radiation changes clouds, surface irradiance and plume dynamics compared to conventional 1D radiation.
 Co-developing a physics-informed machine-learning denoiser with your Leiden colleague, and evaluating it together with the user committee in operational settings.
 Publishing your results in leading journals and presenting them at international conferences and to users from the field.

Your job
 We are looking for a talented Post-Doctoral Researcher for a 1- to 2-years position for the development of AFM-IR infrared nanospectroscopy in combination with microfluidics to achieve chemical analysis of protein and their assemblies in liquid physiological conditions. 
 As a post-doctoral researcher, you will contribute to push the boundaries of nano-chemical analysis, withing the Ruggeri’s lab at Wageningen University in the frame of the project  Nano-Scope . 
 The Nano-Scope project focuses on the study of protein interactions and self-assembly in disease and drug formulations at the single-molecule level; and it runs in collaboration with dr. Ioana Ilie at Amsterdam University, as well as several industrial partners: Bruker Nano (USA); Digital Surf (France); Novo Nordisk (Denmark); Discoveric Bio Alpha (Switzerland).
 Your duties and responsibilities include:  
 developing and applying nano-chemical imaging and spectroscopy via AFM-IR to study protein structure and chemical properties;
 developing the technical capabilities of AFM-IR in liquid environment leveraging microfluidics;
 preparing and pre-characterising protein-based samples for nano-analysis;
 writing manuscripts for publication in peer-reviewed scientific journals reporting on the results of your research;
 supervising MSc and PhD students.
 Your team 
 You will work with  dr Francesco Simone Ruggeri and his team of Nanoscale Imaging and Spectroscopy, which will include several PhDs and Post-Doctoral researchers. The group develops and applies advanced nanoscale imaging and spectroscopy approaches to investigate the chemical, structural, and physical properties of complex molecular systems.

 a strong academic record and PhD in physical chemistry, physics, chemistry, biophysics or a related topic;

Your job

As a functional application manager, your challenge will be to work with the team to ensure the continuity of the current financial platforms and to ensure a smooth transition to a new platform. 
 In this team, you will use your knowledge of, for example, procurement processes, accounting processes, project administration and customer relationship management processes to support users and ensure the software is optimally configured. Your knowledge of IT infrastructure, data models and data management will enable you to make the right choices and refine processes for smooth operational application management. We need your proactive, collaborative and sociable nature to organise all the operational work and the changes effectively. We need you now – a go-getter who takes the initiative, gets things done and inspires others with your ability to bring about change!
 Your main tasks and responsibilities as a functional application manager: 
 you are fluent in the Dutch language
 functional application management and user support for financial platforms (you’ll focus primarily on Unit4 Business World);
 acting as a liaison between the user organisation, suppliers and the IT organisation;
 refining processes for platform management and user support;
 monitoring security aspects and requirements;
 ensuring that the platform infrastructure aligns with the requirements and processes of the user organisation.
 This is where you’ll be working 
 At WUR, you’ll be working within Digitalisation & Information Services (DIS). This department brings together all the teams collaborating on WUR’s digital agenda. Within DIS, there are plenty of opportunities to specialise further and develop your skills in your field.
 Your team is part of the IT Operations department. The management and support of the financial applications are handled by the Finance, Procurement and Projects (FP&I) team. Here, you will work alongside five functional application managers, a product owner, a scrum master and a business analyst. Together, you will be responsible for the security, continuity and quality of the data in the software used for project administration, expense claims, financial administration and procurement.
 Your qualities
 What do we look for in your experience and personality? 
 you are someone who demonstrably takes the initiative easily and knows how to tackle initiatives in an organised manner;

 As part of the application procedure, we ask you to submit a Certificate of Good Conduct (VOG) and obtaining references is part of the procedure.
 In our international working environment, communication is increasingly taking place in English. For this role, the requirement is CEFR level B1 . If you have not yet reached this level, we will of course help you, and you are welcome to contact our language centre, Wageningen in’to Language .

 Would you like to use data to show what works and help colleagues make better decisions? There is plenty of room to bring your own knowledge, experience and ideas to the role. 
 As a Marketing Data Analyst, you will help us strengthen our data-driven approach to marketing. Together with our target audience teams, data analysts and online marketing specialists, you will analyse data from our website, campaigns and online channels. You will connect data from different sources to provide insight into what happens throughout the funnel and customer journey. You will identify trends and anomalies and work with colleagues to understand what is behind the numbers. You will make sure the right data and insights are available and help colleagues interpret and apply them.
 Technical expertise and analysis are an important part of your work, but what you do with the insights is just as important. You will share them with colleagues, advise them on how to interpret the data and help turn insights into concrete actions.

wur:16831.description:
Are you a highly motivated and curious, and can you translate ecological expertise into successful designs of biodiverse, climate-resilient, aesthetically attractive and multifunctional green facades? Do you enjoy bridging fundamental ecological knowledge with practical applications? Then Wageningen University & Research offers an exciting opportunity for you. 
BIO-SKIN (Bio-Inspired Outer Surfaces to Kool, Insulate and Nurture) is developing bio-based, waste-derived, and circular façade systems that integrate plant growth. The project goal is to help bio-based facade panels that keep buildings cool, insulate, support biodiversity, and contribute to more sustainable urban environments. We work in a team of people with backgrounds in design, materials, biomaterial chemistry, architecture, biology, engineering, sustainability, and the built environment.
In this position, you will investigate how plant-soil-insect interactions develop in ecosystems with shallow soils and translate these ecological insights into design principles for next-generation green façades. Your research will contribute to a better understanding of how ecological communities establish and function in constrained urban environments, while helping to develop façade systems that support biodiversity and ecosystem functioning.
As a PhD candidate, you will combine fundamental and applied research to develop innovative green façade concepts that enhance ecosystem complexity and deliver key ecosystem services, including thermal insulation, carbon sequestration, microclimate regulation, and habitat provision for insects and other arthropods. This involves designing and setting up mini-ecosystems in minimal soil/vertical environments at various Living/Field Lab locations, and monitoring their performance, biodiversity and impact for energy efficiency. You will design the façade-panel experiments in close collaboration with a postdoctoral researcher, analyse ecological and physiological data, and contribute to scientific publications.
The project offers a unique opportunity to connect ecology, ecophysiology, urban greening, and green façade design.
We are looking for a candidate who enjoys working in interdisciplinary teams. You will bring strong botanical expertise to a collaborative group of researchers, designers, and material developers, and partners from companies that produce green façades, jointly creating innovative green façade solutions that contribute to sustainable construction and healthier urban environments.
Your activities include:
 Investigating plant species performance, community assembly and plant-insect-soil interactions in shallow-substrate systems (drawing on insights from literature as well as field studies);
 Year-round monitoring at various Living/Field Lab locations on the impact of plant species for enhancing energy efficiency and biodiversity by green façade panels;
 Analysing ecological and ecophysiological datasets;
 Publishing results in peer-reviewed journals and presenting findings at scientific conferences;
 Collaborating with academic and non-academic partners to translate scientific insights into practical applications;
 Teaching in courses and supervise BSc and MSc students in biodiversity-themed research.
 You will work here 
The research is embedded within the Biosystematics Group and the Laboratory of Entomology You will be supervised by dr. ir. Casper Quist and Prof. Bregje Wertheim . As a member in the BIO-SKIN team you will work one day a week together with the other BIO-SKIN PhDs and Post-docs at the AMS institute in Amsterdam . In addition, you will be embedded in the PE&RC graduate school ( Home | PE&RC ), which will allow you to follow a wide variety of training courses and provide support during your academic journey.

REQUIREMENTS:
For this project, we are looking for an enthusiastic, highly motivated and curious PhD candidate, who can translate botanical and ecological expertise into successful designs of biodiverse, climate-resilient, aesthetically attractive and multifunctional green facades.
 You have or are: 
 A successfully completed MSc degree in forest- and nature conservation or biology
 Extensive knowledge of the Dutch flora, able to accurately identify plant species in the field
 A strong interest in ecological interactions, including relationships between plants, insects, and soil organisms
 Interest in and initial experience with interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary collaboration, and the ability to engage with stakeholders from diverse backgrounds, including design, engineering, education, and ecology.
 Excellent communication skills in Dutch and English and experience with teaching and scientific writing.
For this position your command of the English and Dutch language is expected to be at C1 level . Sometimes it is necessary to submit an internationally recognised Certificate of Proficiency in the English Language. More information can be found here .

CONTRACT: 18 months

Pedagogical trainer/educational advisor
Your job
 Inspire our educators to provide innovative, high-quality teaching at Wageningen University. As a creative and professional trainer, you drive impactful teacher development, advise on GenAI thoughtfully, and help teachers build dynamic learning environments to bring our educational vision to life. 
 You have a passion for didactical (pedagogical) development of teachers within higher education. You develop and provide teacher training in Supervision, Teaching, Design, and Assessment, which contributes towards the learning of our teachers within the University Teaching Qualification (UTQ). 
 You are creative and you balance your creativity with project management skills in the development and quality management of courses, workshops, and resources for teacher professionalization. You have experience in and a view on use of and impact on GenAI in education. In your training and advising, you inspire and facilitate teachers to develop themselves as professional teachers of Wageningen University. 
 Through the professionalization of teachers and teaching teams you inspire and support the development and implementation of innovative learning environments. In doing so, you support the implementation of the University’s vision for education. 
 Your qualities
 You are a professional with: 
 a passion for education with a relevant MSc-degree in the field of Educational or pedagogical sciences;
 knowledge of educational theories, methods, structures and design, and preferably knowledge and experience in communication models, theories, and best practices;
 experience as trainer or teacher in higher education, with a focus on soft skills (e.g. communication, group supervision, community building);
 knowledge of advice, development and implementation of educational improvements and innovations in higher education curricula/programmes, especially regarding GenAI;
 an ability to work agile, with deadlines and a stress resistant attitude;
 excellent proficiency in English (C2), if you do not speak Dutch, a willingness to follow Dutch language courses is preferred; 
 competences:  clear communicative abilities, able to deal with different stakeholders, intercultural sensitivity, assertive, solution oriented, team player, creative and curious.

 The Teaching and Learning Centre (TLC) is dedicated to fostering excellence in education. With a focus on innovation and continuous improvement, TLC strives to enrich the educational experience for both students and faculty.
 We are a dynamic educational organisation that constantly seeks innovative (IT) tools, pedagogical approaches and activities for its stakeholders and our development. Hence, there is ample room for personal contributions and initiatives. The Teaching and Learning Centre has an entrepreneurial, open and informal organisational culture. Within the TLC, your homebase will be the TLC Teaching Academy. The Teaching Academy is where educators come for professionalization that equips, empowers, and inspires them to grow as a professional educator, to be a leader and partner in education and to bring to life the WUR Vision.

 sabbatical leave, study leave, and partially paid parental leave;
 working hours that can be discussed and arranged so that they allow for the best possible work-life balance;
 there is a strong focus on vitality and you can make use of the sports facilities available on campus for a small fee;
 a fixed year-end bonus of 8.3%;
 excellent pension scheme.
 In addition to these first-rate employee benefits, you will of course receive a good salary. As for your contract, we initially offer a one-year contract with the intention of converting it into a contract for an indefinite period. A contract based on a 32-hour working week is possible.

PhD: The link between mountains, downstream agriculture and ecosystems globally
Your job
 Are you interested in the role of mountains in the global hydrological cycle? And in what happens to downstream water supply when mountains change? Do you like working with numerical models? Then this PhD might be your next step! 
 A large part of the freshwater that sustains human societies is generated in the mountains. The seasonal melting of snow and ice supports agriculture, industries, households and the environment downstream. However, mountainous regions are changing rapidly, as they are hit hard by climate change. The impact of these changes on downstream water users is poorly understood. Global hydrological models rarely account for complex mountain processes. However, understanding how mountain processes influence global water availability is important to address sustainable water use.
 We are looking for a PhD student who is interested in the link between changing mountain processes and increasing water use downstream. This position is part of the project ‘MountAInWater’ in which a consortium of international, interdisciplinary researchers collectively aims to answer the question How is the water supply from the world’s mountain ranges changing and which non-linear feedbacks may cause unprecedented societal impacts?
 As a PhD student at Wageningen University you will apply a large scale hydrology-crop model in river basins that are originating from snow and ice covered mountains. 
 Your duties and responsibilities include:  
 Analyse how missing complex mountain processes in global precipitation products and hydrological models affect water availability estimates.  
 Quantify the importance of mountainwater for agriculture and ecosystems globally, by analyzing how meltwater flows interact with crop growing seasons and environmental flow requirements in basins with large irrigation demand and high meltwater flows.
 Run the hydrology-crop model in combination with mountain streamflow (from high resolution mountain hydrology models) for selected basins to analyse mountain water contributions to downstream river flow, agricultural water use, and sustaining ecosystems for hotspot areas.
 Using a global mountain reanalysis dataset to evaluate for all mountain areas globally their contribution to downstream river flows, agriculture and ecosystems.
 You will publish your research findings in high ranking scientific journals and present it at conferences. 
 You will also be asked to contribute occasionally to education, by helping in the supervision of MSc students that work on their thesis projects, and supporting in courses. 
 You will work here 
 The research is embedded within the chair Water Systems and Global Change. You will be supervised by Prof. Dr. Hester Biemans, Dr. Manoj Khaniya and a third supervisor tbd. 
 Your qualities
 You are / You have: 
 enthusiasm for the research topic;
 a MSc degree in the field of Hydrology, Crop Science, Earth System Science, Environmental Science, Climate Science, or a related field;
 a MSc thesis related to quantitative assessment of water- and/or food security;
 demonstrated experience in working with large datasets and large-scale numerical modelling in context of global change;
 experience with scripting and programming, eg in R, Python or Matlab and the willingness to learn a new programming language (C);
 creativity in communication and visualisation of model results in maps and figures;
 some experience with numerical modelling on High Performance Computing Platforms is a pre;
 willingness to work in multidisciplinary and internationally teams;
 a high level of English, both oral and written. 
 For this position your command of the English language is expected to be at C1  level . Sometimes it is necessary to submit an internationally recognised Certificate of Proficiency in the English Language. More information can be found  here .

 working hours that can be discussed and arranged so that they allow for the best possible work-life balance;
 there is a strong focus on vitality and you can make use of the sports facilities available on campus for a small fee;
 a fixed year-end bonus of 8.3%;
 excellent pension scheme.
 In addition to these first-rate employee benefits, you will receive a fully funded PhD position and you will be offered a course program tailored to your needs and the research team.

 Creating a work schedule;

 Performing measurements using our modern LC-(HR)MS/MS systems;
 Processing and interpreting data.

Your job
 Are you an organisational talent with a head for finance, who enjoys connecting people and keeping projects running smoothly? As Business Support Officer in Wageningen, you are the link between the Philosophy and Strategic Communication chair groups, management and WUR's support departments. 
 Together with one other Business Support Officer and three Management Assistants, you form the support staff of CPT (Communication, Philosophy and Technology), part of the Section CPTE. As a team, you are the link between the staff of the chair groups and management within our university organisation.
 Within the team, you are specifically responsible for project management and financial management for the Philosophy and Strategic Communication chair groups. You are the point of contact for a diverse group of people – including lecturers, researchers, PhD candidates and students – as well as guests and support departments, on matters relating to finance, projects and, where needed, HR.
 Your duties and responsibilities include:  
 monitoring the budgets of ongoing projects, preparing financial reports and supporting the preparation of the annual and multi-year budgets, including keeping staff and PhD overviews up to date;
 reviewing and checking expense and hours claims, orders, purchases and invoices, and supporting project leaders with acquisition and project administration, in close consultation with project leaders and project controllers;
 drawing up sales invoices and intercompany bookings, and checking and approving timesheets and project registrations;
 preparing staffing requests and supporting the recruitment and appointment of staff, student assistants and research assistants, including the related administration (employment contracts, guest and email accounts and, for international staff and PhD candidates, matters such as working from abroad and residence permits);
 acting as the point of contact for, and maintaining contact with, staff, PhD candidates, guests, departments such as Finance & Control, HR, Liaison Office, WASS, Project Control and Business Control, and external parties.
 Your team 
 You will join an enthusiastic and professional team with one other Business Support Officer and three Management Assistants. Your line manager is the section chair, Prof. Rens Vliegenthart.
 You will work here  
 The staff of the Section CPTE (Communication, Philosophy, Technology and Education) research transformations in domains such as agriculture, climate and environment, and advance societal engagement with these transformations. They do so from an inclusive, process-oriented, empirical, critical and reflexive perspective. They also teach on these topics in various bachelor's and master's programmes at WUR.
 Your qualities
 You have a proactive, flexible and enterprising personality. You know how to set priorities, work accurately and handle the processing and checking of data with care. You are decisive and see yourself as a connector: you actively seek collaboration with your direct colleagues and other departments. You know how to motivate others and take initiative where needed. Experience in a coordinating role and in a complex organisation such as a university is an advantage.
 You also possess:  
 a post-secondary vocational (MBO+) or bachelor's-level (HBO) background, with knowledge of and affinity with financial and other management processes;
 demonstrable financial insight and relevant administrative experience;
 experience with MS Office, Excel in particular, and the ability to pick up new software systems quickly;
 a good command of Dutch and English.
 In our international working environment there is communication in both English and Dutch. For this position, the required  language level is at least B2 for both.

 sabbatical leave, study leave, and partially paid parental leave;
 working hours that can be discussed and arranged so that they allow for the best possible work-life balance;
 there is a strong focus on vitality and you can make use of the sports facilities available on campus for a small fee;
 a fixed year-end bonus of 8.3%;
 excellent pension scheme.
 In addition to these first-rate employee benefits, you will of course receive a good salary. As for your contract, we initially offer a one-year contract that can be extended, if possible within (company) organizational circumstances, on good performance.
