Do you want to steer the strategic deployment of AI within Wageningen Livestock Research? Connect science, data, and technology, and help build innovative applications that shape the future of animal sciences?
Acting as a AI lead, you are responsible for the strategic development and integration of AI within the Wageningen Livestock Research research portfolio. You connect researchers, data scientists, and IT specialists; bring together technological developments and research questions; and translate AI capabilities into concrete, impactful applications. In doing so, you guide AI innovation and strengthen Wageningen Livestock Research’s position as a leading knowledge partner in the field of AI within animal sciences.
 Your duties and responsibilities include: 
 Gaining a clear understanding of available AI tools and establishing a practical framework for their application in research;
 Demonstrating vision and leadership regarding the application of data and AI solutions in the agri-food sector: identifying opportunities for major leaps forward and determining how to actively bring the benefits of data and AI to our clients in this sector;
 Developing and updating the vision for AI within animal science; promoting the use of AI in research projects and organizational development;
 Connecting domain specialists with software developers and modelers, both within WUR and among external partners;
 Initiating AI-related projects and driving acquisition and business development; building and maintaining a strong internal and external network focused on AI and data science; translating (inter)national AI developments into opportunities and innovations for Wageningen Livestock Research.
 Your team 
Together with colleagues—researchers, project leaders, measurement technicians, and analysts—you will work on innovative solutions for the livestock farming of the future. As an AI lead, you will work in a team setting, both within your department and in various project teams. While the “Animal Welfare and Health” department will be your home base, you will be active across Wageningen Livestock Research and beyond. You will also play an active role in our “Data Science” expertise team.

REQUIREMENTS:
You are a strategic and entrepreneurial professional with a strong foundation in AI and data science, skilled at connecting people, disciplines, and organizations. With your affinity for animal husbandry and innovation in both research and practice, you combine subject-matter expertise with a keen eye for opportunities. You possess excellent communication and networking skills and use your connecting personality to build lasting relationships and partnerships. In doing so, you bring the right people together and translate ideas and opportunities into successful collaborations and tangible results.
 You also possess: 
 Academic level of working and thinking.
 Demonstrable expertise in artificial intelligence and data science.
 Experience with strategic positioning, innovation, or business development.
 Affinity with animal science and/or agrifood research.
In our international working environment there is an increasing amount of communication in English. For this position it is about language level B2.

wur:16915.description:
Are you an ecologist who wants to contribute to the restoration of Dutch freshwater ecosystems? Do you have knowledge of freshwater ecology and the organisms that inhabit these systems, experience in ecological research, and an interest in translating research results into practical applications? Then this position may be for you! 
As a Freshwater Ecology Researcher, you will work with other researchers on a variety of projects for water managers and policymakers. You will contribute to field research and desk studies, data analysis, and the reporting and presentation of research findings.
The projects focus on current topics in Dutch freshwater ecology. Examples include:
 Investigating the effectiveness of restoration and management measures in different freshwater habitats.
 Reintroducing macroinvertebrate species.
 Assessing the effects of salinization and drought on biodiversity.
 Evaluating innovative monitoring techniques.
 Contributing to the development of ecological monitoring and assessment systems.
The work is varied and dynamic. Your responsibilities may include conducting fieldwork in streams and peatland areas, contributing to analyses of existing datasets from water authorities, and carrying out literature reviews. You will work in multidisciplinary project teams with varying compositions. All project work takes place within the Netherlands.
 Your Team 
You will collaborate with researchers in the Freshwater Ecology Research Group, which is part of the Water & Food Team at Wageningen Environmental Research (WENR) . The group focuses on restoring and improving aquatic ecosystems by developing, sharing, and applying knowledge that supports water management and policy.

REQUIREMENTS:
You are proactive, results-oriented, able to work independently as well as in a team, and possess strong communication and organizational skills. In this role, it is important that you can solve both practical and theoretical or scientific problems.
 You also have: 
 A relevant degree in Ecology.
 Knowledge of the functioning of Dutch freshwater ecosystems and wetlands from a landscape ecology or systems ecology perspective.
 Knowledge of one or more taxonomic groups, such as macroinvertebrates, plants, algae, birds, or ground beetles.
 The ability to analyze, report, and present research results to different audiences in the Netherlands, primarily water managers, policymakers, and researchers.
 A driver's license is considered an advantage.
In our international working environment, English is increasingly used for communication. For this position, an English proficiency level of B2 is required. If you do not yet meet this level, we will support your development through Wageningen in’to Language, our language training center.
We recognize that this role offers plenty of challenges, which can also be viewed as development opportunities. Therefore, if you do not yet have the exact track record described in the vacancy but do have solid relevant work experience, we still encourage you to apply.
